Bui\n</span><span class=\"ltx_author_notes\"><span class=\"ltx_author_notes_content\">\n<span class=\"ltx_contact ltx_role_affiliation\"><span class=\"ltx_contact_name\">Affiliation: </span>OpenDev\n</span>\n<span class=\"ltx_contact ltx_role_affiliation\"><span class=\"ltx_contact_name\">Affiliation: </span>\n<span id=\"id1\" class=\"ltx_inline-block fas fa-github\" aria-hidden=\"true\">\n</span> <a href=\"https://github.com/opendev-to/opendev\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter\">https://github.com/opendev-to/opendev</a>\n</span>\n<span class=\"ltx_contact ltx_role_affiliation\"><span class=\"ltx_contact_name\">Affiliation: </span>\n<span id=\"id2\" class=\"ltx_inline-block fas fa-rust\" aria-hidden=\"true\">\n</span> Codebase written in Rust\n</span>\n<span class=\"ltx_contact ltx_role_email\"><span class=\"ltx_contact_name\">Email: </span><a href=\"mailto:%E2%80%82\">\n<span id=\"id3\" class=\"ltx_inline-block fas fa-envelope\" aria-hidden=\"true\">\n</span> <span id=\"id4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">bdqnghi@gmail.com</span></a>\n</span></span></span></span></div>\n\n<div id=\"abstract1\" class=\"ltx_abstract\"><h6 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_abstract\">Abstract</h6>\n    \n<p id=\"abstract1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">The landscape of AI coding assistance is undergoing a fundamental shift from complex IDE plugins to versatile, terminal-native agents. Operating directly where developers manage source control, execute builds, and deploy environments, CLI-based agents offer unprecedented autonomy for long-horizon development tasks. In this paper, we present <span id=\"abstract1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps\">OpenDev</span>, an open-source, command-line coding agent written in <span id=\"abstract1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Rust</span>, engineered specifically for this new paradigm. Effective autonomous assistance requires strict safety controls and highly efficient context management to prevent context bloat and reasoning degradation. <span id=\"abstract1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps\">OpenDev</span> overcomes these challenges through a compound AI system architecture <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib103\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">103</a>]</cite> with workload-specialized model routing, a dual-agent architecture separating planning from execution, lazy tool discovery, and adaptive context compaction that progressively reduces older observations. Furthermore, it employs an automated memory system to accumulate project-specific knowledge across sessions and counteracts instruction fade-out through event-driven system reminders. By enforcing explicit reasoning phases and prioritizing context efficiency, <span id=\"abstract1.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps\">OpenDev</span> provides a secure, extensible foundation for terminal-first AI assistance, offering a blueprint for robust autonomous software engineering.</p>\n  \n</div>\n<div id=\"p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<table id=\"p1.1\" class=\"ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_align_top\">\n<tbody class=\"ltx_tbody\">\n<tr id=\"p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_tr\">\n<td id=\"p1.1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_td ltx_align_center\"><span class=\"ltx_rule\" style=\"width:0.0pt;height:24.0pt;--ltx-bg-color:black;display:inline-block;\"></span></td></tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n</div>\n<section id=\"S1\" class=\"ltx_section\">\n<h2 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_section\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_section\">1 </span>Introduction</h2>\n\n<figure id=\"S1.F1\" class=\"ltx_figure\"><img src=\"2603.05344v3/top.png\" id=\"S1.F1.g1\" class=\"ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape\" style=\"aspect-ratio:648/310;\" width=\"648\" height=\"310\" alt=\"Refer to caption\">\n<figcaption class=\"ltx_caption ltx_centering\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure\">Figure 1: </span>Overview of <span id=\"S1.F1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps\">OpenDev</span>. Work is organized into concurrent sessions, each composed of multiple specialized sub-agents; each agent executes typed workflows (Execution, Thinking, Compaction) that independently bind to a user-configured LLM. This four-level hierarchy (session <math id=\"S1.F1.m4\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\to\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo stretchy=\"false\">→</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\to</annotation></semantics></math> agent <math id=\"S1.F1.m5\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\to\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo stretchy=\"false\">→</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\to</annotation></semantics></math> workflow <math id=\"S1.F1.m6\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\to\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo stretchy=\"false\">→</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\to</annotation></semantics></math> LLM) enables fine-grained model selection, allowing cost, latency, and capability trade-offs to be optimized per workflow.</figcaption>\n</figure>\n<div id=\"S1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">The rapid advancement of large language models (LLMs) has catalyzed a new paradigm in software development: AI-powered coding assistants that operate as autonomous agents <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib95\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">95</a>, <a href=\"#bib.bib105\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">105</a>, <a href=\"#bib.bib99\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">99</a>]</cite>. Unlike traditional code completion tools that suggest inline snippets, agentic coding assistants can reason about complex tasks, execute multi-step plans, and interact with the development environment through tool use. Comprehensive surveys have documented the explosive growth of code intelligence research <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib47\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">47</a>, <a href=\"#bib.bib46\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">46</a>]</cite>, and roadmaps for Agentic Software Engineering <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib35\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">35</a>]</cite> have formalized the methodological principles governing human–AI collaboration. Systems such as SWE-Agent <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib95\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">95</a>]</cite>, OpenHands <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib84\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">84</a>]</cite>, and HyperAgent <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib69\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">69</a>]</cite> have demonstrated the potential of autonomous agents on standardized benchmarks. The commercial impact has been equally dramatic, with GitHub Copilot surpassing 15 million developers <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib30\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">30</a>]</cite>, rapid revenue growth for AI-native editors <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib4\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">4</a>]</cite>, and major labs launching autonomous coding agents <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib18\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">18</a>, <a href=\"#bib.bib65\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">65</a>]</cite>, signaling that agentic coding has moved from research prototype to industrial deployment.</p>\n</div>\n<section id=\"S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">The rise of terminal-native agents.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">For the past few years, AI coding assistants have been tightly integrated into IDEs, acting as reactive copilots requiring constant human oversight. Recently, a major shift has begun, moving away from complex IDE plugins toward simpler command-line interfaces. Claude Code <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib2\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">2</a>]</cite> led this shift, demonstrating that a terminal-native agent could match or exceed IDE-integrated tools in real-world software engineering tasks. The terminal is the operational heart of software development, natively supporting source control, build systems, remote SSH sessions, and headless server environments. Early systems such as Aider <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib28\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">28</a>]</cite>, CodeAct <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib83\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">83</a>]</cite>, and Open Interpreter <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib63\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">63</a>]</cite> demonstrated the viability of terminal-based AI pair programming and executable code actions. Today, every major AI lab offers a CLI agent <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib2\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">2</a>, <a href=\"#bib.bib32\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">32</a>, <a href=\"#bib.bib65\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">65</a>]</cite>, alongside open-source alternatives such as Goose <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib10\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">10</a>]</cite>, OpenCode <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib19\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">19</a>]</cite>, and Crush <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib13\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">13</a>]</cite>. However, realizing this potential is non-trivial. Benchmarks such as Terminal-Bench <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib57\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">57</a>]</cite> and LongCLI-Bench <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib25\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">25</a>]</cite> demonstrate that even frontier models struggle with continuous terminal operation, underscoring the need for purpose-built engineering solutions.</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">These benchmark results point to three fundamental engineering challenges that any long-running terminal agent must solve: managing finite context windows over sessions that routinely exceed the model’s token budget, preventing destructive operations when the agent can execute arbitrary shell commands, and extending capabilities without overwhelming the agent’s prompt budget. We organize the architectural response around two phases: <em id=\"S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.1\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">scaffolding</em>, which assembles the agent (system prompt, tool schemas, subagent registry) before the first prompt, and the <em id=\"S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.2\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">harness</em>, which orchestrates tool dispatch, context management, and safety enforcement at runtime <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib102\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">102</a>]</cite> (<a href=\"#S2.SS2\" title=\"2.2 Agent Core Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.2</span></a>). Yet the design space for terminal-native agentic tools remains largely underexplored: most production systems are closed-source with undocumented architectural decisions, and existing open-source frameworks either target benchmarks rather than interactive use or lack published technical reports <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib56\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">56</a>, <a href=\"#bib.bib39\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">39</a>]</cite>. Three critical open questions motivate this work: How should multi-model architectures balance cost, latency, and capability across different cognitive tasks? What safety mechanisms prevent destructive operations without hampering developer productivity? And how can systems sustain long-running conversations within finite context limits?</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">In this paper, we present <span id=\"S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps\">OpenDev</span>, an open AI-powered command-line agent for software engineering. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive technical report for an open-source, terminal-native, interactive coding agent. Existing systems occupy one of two categories: benchmark-oriented frameworks such as SWE-Agent <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib95\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">95</a>]</cite> have published research papers but are primarily designed for automated evaluation rather than interactive daily use; OpenHands <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib84\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">84</a>]</cite> is both production-grade and well-documented but operates through a browser-based UI rather than a terminal interface; CLI-native agents such as Aider <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib28\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">28</a>]</cite>, Goose <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib10\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">10</a>]</cite>, OpenCode <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib19\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">19</a>]</cite>, Crush <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib13\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">13</a>]</cite>, and Gemini CLI <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib32\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">32</a>]</cite> lack published technical reports documenting their design decisions; and Claude Code <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib2\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">2</a>]</cite> is CLI-native but neither open-source nor accompanied by a published technical report. <span id=\"S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">The purpose of this paper is not to present a novel algorithmic breakthrough, but rather to share the design decisions, trade-offs, and lessons learned from engineering a production-ready, agentic coding system that bridges the gap between closed-source industrial practice and open academic discourse.</span></p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">A central design principle of <span id=\"S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps\">OpenDev</span> is that it is a <span id=\"S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">compound AI system</span> <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib103\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">103</a>]</cite>: not a single monolithic LLM, but a structured ensemble of agents and workflows, each independently bound to a user-configured LLM (<a href=\"#S2.SS2.SSS5\" title=\"2.2.5 Workload-Optimized Multi-Model Architecture ‣ 2.2 Agent Core Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.2.5</span></a>). This framing, articulated by Zaharia et al., argues that state-of-the-art AI results are increasingly achieved by systems that compose multiple models, retrievers, and tools rather than relying on a single model call. <span id=\"S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps\">OpenDev</span> operationalizes this principle: its decoupled architecture makes the system model-agnostic by construction, and techniques like learned model routing <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib62\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">62</a>]</cite> can be applied at the workflow level. Switching providers or optimizing cost requires only a configuration change, not a code change. The system’s capabilities are therefore not fixed at deployment but continuously upgradeable as better models emerge.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S1.SS0.SSS0.Px2\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Design principles and contributions.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">The design of <span id=\"S1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps\">OpenDev</span> is guided by three overarching principles. First, <em id=\"S1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">separation of concerns</em>: each architectural decision (model selection, context management, safety enforcement, tool dispatch) should be independently configurable and replaceable without affecting the others. Second, <em id=\"S1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">progressive degradation</em>: the system should function gracefully as resources are exhausted, whether that means token budget, iteration count, or network connectivity. Third, <em id=\"S1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.4\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">transparency over magic</em>: every system action (tool calls, safety vetoes, context compaction, memory updates) should be observable and overridable by the developer. These principles manifest in five concrete contributions:</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<ul id=\"S1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1\" class=\"ltx_itemize\">\n<li id=\"S1.I1.i1\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\">1.</span> \n<div id=\"S1.I1.i1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S1.I1.i1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S1.I1.i1.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Per-workflow LLM configurability via a compound architecture.</span> Different execution phases impose different demands on model capability, latency, and cost. We present a per-workflow LLM binding architecture where each cognitive workflow independently selects a model via user configuration (<a href=\"#S2.SS2.SSS5\" title=\"2.2.5 Workload-Optimized Multi-Model Architecture ‣ 2.2 Agent Core Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.2.5</span></a>), informed by the compound AI systems perspective <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib103\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">103</a>]</cite> and model routing research <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib62\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">62</a>]</cite>.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"S1.I1.i2\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;padding-top:0.5pt;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\">2.</span> \n<div id=\"S1.I1.i2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S1.I1.i2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S1.I1.i2.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Extended ReAct execution pipeline.</span> We extend the standard ReAct cycle <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib99\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">99</a>]</cite> with explicit thinking and optional self-critique phases that separate deliberation from action (hereafter, the <em id=\"S1.I1.i2.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">ReAct loop</em>; <a href=\"#S2.SS2.SSS6\" title=\"2.2.6 Extended ReAct Execution Loop ‣ 2.2 Agent Core Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.2.6</span></a>), and integrate staged context compaction directly into the reasoning loop, drawing on insights from context engineering research <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib56\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">56</a>, <a href=\"#bib.bib39\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">39</a>]</cite>.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"S1.I1.i3\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;padding-top:0.5pt;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\">3.</span> \n<div id=\"S1.I1.i3.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S1.I1.i3.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S1.I1.i3.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Behavioral steering over long horizons.</span> We present event-driven system reminders that counteract instruction fade-out in long-running sessions by injecting targeted guidance at the point of decision rather than relying solely on the initial system prompt (<a href=\"#S2.SS3.SSS4\" title=\"2.3.4 Context-Aware System Reminders ‣ 2.3 Context Engineering Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.3.4</span></a>). A conditional prompt composition pipeline assembles agent instructions from independent, priority-ordered sections that load only when contextually relevant, reducing prompt overhead while preserving comprehensive guidance (<a href=\"#S2.SS3.SSS1.Px2\" title=\"Mode-specific variants and variable substitution. ‣ 2.3.1 Dynamic System Prompt Construction ‣ 2.3 Context Engineering Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.3.1</span></a>).</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"S1.I1.i4\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;padding-top:0.5pt;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\">4.</span> \n<div id=\"S1.I1.i4.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S1.I1.i4.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S1.I1.i4.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Token-efficient extensibility and defense-in-depth safety.</span> We present a registry-based tool architecture with lazy-discovered external tools via MCP <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib1\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">1</a>]</cite> (<a href=\"#S2.SS4.SSS7\" title=\"2.4.7 Token-Efficient External Tool Discovery via MCP ‣ 2.4 Tool System ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.4.7</span></a>) and a five-layer safety architecture that enforces constraints at progressively lower levels of abstraction: prompt-level guardrails, schema-level tool gating through dual-agent separation (<a href=\"#S2.SS2\" title=\"2.2 Agent Core Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.2</span></a>), a runtime approval system with persistent permissions, tool-level validation, and user-defined lifecycle hooks (<a href=\"#S2.SS1.SSS0.Px5\" title=\"Safety Architecture. ‣ 2.1 Overview ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.1</span></a>).</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"S1.I1.i5\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;padding-top:0.5pt;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\">5.</span> \n<div id=\"S1.I1.i5.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S1.I1.i5.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S1.I1.i5.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Context engineering as a first-class concern.</span> We treat context management as a first-class engineering concern <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib3\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">3</a>, <a href=\"#bib.bib56\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">56</a>]</cite>, presenting Adaptive Context Compaction (<a href=\"#S2.SS3.SSS6\" title=\"2.3.6 Adaptive Context Compaction ‣ 2.3 Context Engineering Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.3.6</span></a>), event-driven system reminders to counteract attention decay (<a href=\"#S2.SS3.SSS4\" title=\"2.3.4 Context-Aware System Reminders ‣ 2.3 Context Engineering Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.3.4</span></a>), and an experience-driven memory pipeline <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib66\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">66</a>, <a href=\"#bib.bib106\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">106</a>]</cite> that accumulates project-specific knowledge. Our compaction and memory strategies align with the entropy-reduction and minimal-sufficiency principles identified in recent theoretical work on context engineering <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib39\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">39</a>, <a href=\"#bib.bib101\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">101</a>]</cite>.</p>\n</div></li>\n</ul>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S1.SS0.SSS0.Px3\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Paper organization.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S1.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S1.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">The remainder of this paper follows the path from construction to reflection to context. <a href=\"#S2\" title=\"2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2</span></a> details what was built: the four-layer system architecture spanning agent reasoning, context engineering, tooling, and persistence. <a href=\"#S3\" title=\"3 Discussion ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">3</span></a> examines what was learned: five cross-cutting design tensions that emerged during iterative development and the transferable lessons they yield. <a href=\"#S4\" title=\"4 Related Work ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">4</span></a> positions these decisions within the broader research landscape, and <a href=\"#S5\" title=\"5 Conclusion and Future Directions ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">5</span></a> identifies future directions. The appendix provides reference-level catalogs of tools, prompts, configuration schemas, and implementation constants.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2\" class=\"ltx_section\">\n<h2 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_section\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_section\">2 </span>System Architecture</h2>\n\n<figure id=\"S2.F2\" class=\"ltx_figure\"><img src=\"2603.05344v3/overview.png\" id=\"S2.F2.g1\" class=\"ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape\" style=\"aspect-ratio:648/325;\" width=\"648\" height=\"325\" alt=\"Refer to caption\">\n<figcaption class=\"ltx_caption ltx_centering\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure\">Figure 2: </span>System architecture of <span id=\"S2.F2.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps\">OpenDev</span>, organized into four layers: Entry &amp; UI, Agent, Tool &amp; Context, and Persistence. Arrows indicate primary data-flow directions.</figcaption>\n</figure>\n<section id=\"S2.SS1\" class=\"ltx_subsection\">\n<h3 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_subsection\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection\">2.1 </span>Overview</h3>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Figure <a href=\"#S2.F2\" title=\"Figure 2 ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2</span></a> illustrates the architecture of <span id=\"S2.SS1.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps\">OpenDev</span> across four principal layers: Entry &amp; UI, Agent, Tool &amp; Context, and Persistence. A user query flows through this pipeline sequentially, from the entry point through agent reasoning and tool execution, before results are persisted and rendered.</p>\n</div>\n<section id=\"S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Entry &amp; UI Layer.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">The <em id=\"S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">CLI Entry Point</em> parses arguments and bootstraps four shared managers (ConfigManager, SessionManager, ModeManager, and ApprovalManager), which are injected into all downstream components. <span id=\"S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps\">OpenDev</span> supports two frontends: a <em id=\"S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">TUI</em> built on Textual using blocking modal approvals, and a <em id=\"S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.4\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">Web UI</em> backed by FastAPI and WebSockets using asynchronous polling approvals. Both implement a shared <span id=\"S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.5\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">UICallback</span> contract, keeping the agent layer UI-agnostic.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS1.SSS0.Px2\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Agent Layer.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps\">OpenDev</span> assigns five specialized model roles to distinct LLMs (<a href=\"#S2.SS2.SSS5\" title=\"2.2.5 Workload-Optimized Multi-Model Architecture ‣ 2.2 Agent Core Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.2.5</span></a>), each lazily initialized and informed by a locally cached capability registry. The system operates in two modes: <em id=\"S2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">Normal Mode</em> with full read-write tool access for execution, and <em id=\"S2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">Plan Mode</em> restricted to read-only tools for safe planning (<a href=\"#S2.SS2\" title=\"2.2 Agent Core Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.2</span></a>). Reasoning proceeds through the <em id=\"S2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.4\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">Extended ReAct Loop</em> (<a href=\"#S2.SS2.SSS6\" title=\"2.2.6 Extended ReAct Execution Loop ‣ 2.2 Agent Core Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.2.6</span></a>), which runs four phases per turn: automatic context compaction when the token budget nears exhaustion; an optional thinking phase for pre-action reasoning at configurable depth; an optional self-critique phase; and the standard Reason-Act-Execute-Observe action phase.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS1.SSS0.Px3\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Tool &amp; Context Layers.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">The <em id=\"S2.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">Tool Execution Layer</em> is built around a <span id=\"S2.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">ToolRegistry</span> that dispatches calls to typed handlers covering file operations, process execution, and web access, with support for batch parallel execution and on-demand MCP tool discovery (<a href=\"#S2.SS4.SSS7\" title=\"2.4.7 Token-Efficient External Tool Discovery via MCP ‣ 2.4 Tool System ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.4.7</span></a>). A Skills system lazily injects reusable, domain-specific prompt templates from a three-tier hierarchy (built-in, project, user). The <em id=\"S2.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">Context Engineering Layer</em> manages the LLM context window through four subsystems: System Reminders (<a href=\"#S2.SS3.SSS4\" title=\"2.3.4 Context-Aware System Reminders ‣ 2.3 Context Engineering Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.3.4</span></a>) for context-aware behavioral guidance, Prompt Composer for modular system-prompt assembly, Memory for cross-session continuity, and Compaction (<a href=\"#S2.SS3.SSS6\" title=\"2.3.6 Adaptive Context Compaction ‣ 2.3 Context Engineering Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.3.6</span></a>) for reclaiming token budget.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS1.SSS0.Px4\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Persistence Layer.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S2.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps\">OpenDev</span> persists state across four stores: a <em id=\"S2.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">Config Manager</em> that resolves settings through a project-local, user-global, environment-variable, and built-in default hierarchy; a <em id=\"S2.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">Session Manager</em> that saves full conversation histories as JSON; a <em id=\"S2.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.4\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">Provider Cache</em> that stores model capability metadata locally; and an operation log that tracks file changes for rollback.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS1.SSS0.Px5\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Safety Architecture.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS1.SSS0.Px5.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS1.SSS0.Px5.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Because the agent can execute arbitrary shell commands, overwrite files, and spawn persistent processes, a single safety mechanism is insufficient. <span id=\"S2.SS1.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps\">OpenDev</span> therefore employs a <em id=\"S2.SS1.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">defense-in-depth</em> architecture with five independent safety layers (<a href=\"#S2.F3\" title=\"In Safety Architecture. ‣ 2.1 Overview ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Figure</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">3</span></a>), each designed to prevent a class of harm independently so that no single point of failure compromises the system.</p>\n</div>\n<figure id=\"S2.F3\" class=\"ltx_figure\"><span class=\"ltx_inline-block\"><svg id=\"S2.F3.pic1\" class=\"ltx_picture ltx_centering\" style=\"padding-bottom: 3.0pt;\">\n<span id=\"S2.F3.pic1.1.8.1.1\" class=\"ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top\" style=\"width:427.1pt;\">\n<span id=\"S2.F3.pic1.1.8.1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S2.F3.pic1.1.8.1.1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\" style=\"--ltx-fg-color:#000000;\">DANGEROUS_PATTERNS</span><span id=\"S2.F3.pic1.1.8.1.1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text\" style=\"--ltx-fg-color:#000000;\"> blocklist, stale-read detection, output truncation, timeouts</span></span>\n</span></td></tr>\n<tr id=\"S2.F3.pic1.1.9\" class=\"ltx_tr\" style=\"--ltx-bg-color:#FAEBF0;\">\n<td id=\"S2.F3.pic1.1.9.1\" class=\"ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_left ltx_align_top\">\n<span id=\"S2.F3.pic1.1.9.1.1\" class=\"ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top\" style=\"width:427.1pt;--ltx-bg-color:#FAEBF0;\">\n<span id=\"S2.F3.pic1.1.9.1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S2.F3.pic1.1.9.1.1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\" style=\"--ltx-fg-color:#000000;\">Layer 5: Lifecycle Hooks</span><span id=\"S2.F3.pic1.1.9.1.1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text\" style=\"--ltx-fg-color:#000000;\"> (</span><a href=\"#S2.SS4.SSS1\" and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\" style=\"--ltx-fg-color:#000000;\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.4.1</span></a><span id=\"S2.F3.pic1.1.9.1.1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text\" style=\"--ltx-fg-color:#000000;\">)</span></span>\n</span></td></tr>\n<tr id=\"S2.F3.pic1.1.10\" class=\"ltx_tr\">\n<td id=\"S2.F3.pic1.1.10.1\" class=\"ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_left ltx_align_top\">\n<span id=\"S2.F3.pic1.1.10.1.1\" class=\"ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top\" style=\"width:427.1pt;\">\n<span id=\"S2.F3.pic1.1.10.1.1.1\"
