Staged compaction (<a href=\"#S2.SS3.SSS6\" title=\"2.3.6 Adaptive Context Compaction ‣ 2.3 Context Engineering Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.3.6</span></a>) and todo-based completion validation (<a href=\"#S2.SS3.SSS4\" title=\"2.3.4 Context-Aware System Reminders ‣ 2.3 Context Engineering Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.3.4</span></a>) addressed additional failure modes discovered during this phase.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS2.SSS7\" class=\"ltx_subsubsection\">\n<h4 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection\">2.2.7 </span>Subagent Orchestration</h4>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS2.SSS7.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS2.SSS7.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Some tasks benefit from focused expertise (codebase exploration, user clarification) while others require coordination with main agent state (task management). The main agent can spawn specialized subagents for specific subtasks, each with filtered tool access and specialized prompts. Subagents execute in isolated contexts with their own iteration budgets, preventing unbounded execution.</p>\n</div>\n<section id=\"S2.SS2.SSS7.Px1\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Subagent specialization.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS2.SSS7.Px1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS2.SSS7.Px1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Different subagents serve different roles:</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S2.SS2.SSS7.Px1.p2\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<ul id=\"S2.SS2.SSS7.Px1.p2.1\" class=\"ltx_itemize\">\n<li id=\"S2.I2.i1\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\"><math id=\"S2.I2.i1.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\bullet\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\bullet</annotation></semantics></math></span> \n<div id=\"S2.I2.i1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S2.I2.i1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S2.I2.i1.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Code explorer:</span> Read-only tools for codebase navigation. Specialized for understanding existing code structure.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"S2.I2.i2\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\"><math id=\"S2.I2.i2.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\bullet\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\bullet</annotation></semantics></math></span> \n<div id=\"S2.I2.i2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S2.I2.i2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S2.I2.i2.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Strategic planner:</span> Read-only tools plus extended reasoning. Focuses on high-level planning without execution.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"S2.I2.i3\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\"><math id=\"S2.I2.i3.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\bullet\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\bullet</annotation></semantics></math></span> \n<div id=\"S2.I2.i3.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S2.I2.i3.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S2.I2.i3.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Web tools:</span> Web fetching and file writing for cloning web content. Combines retrieval with persistence.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"S2.I2.i4\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\"><math id=\"S2.I2.i4.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\bullet\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\bullet</annotation></semantics></math></span> \n<div id=\"S2.I2.i4.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S2.I2.i4.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S2.I2.i4.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">User clarification:</span> Minimal toolset for gathering input. Focuses on eliciting information without distraction.</p>\n</div></li>\n</ul>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS2.SSS7.Px2\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Tool filtering rationale.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS2.SSS7.Px2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS2.SSS7.Px2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Subagent capabilities are deliberately restricted for three reasons. First, task management tools are excluded from subagents so that only the main agent coordinates todo lists, preventing race conditions and inconsistent state. Second, limited tool access reduces context size and focuses each subagent on its specific role, meaning an exploration subagent does not need write capabilities. Third, restricted tools limit the blast radius of errors: an exploration subagent cannot accidentally modify files.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS2.SSS7.Px3\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Parallel execution.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS2.SSS7.Px3.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS2.SSS7.Px3.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">The main agent can spawn multiple subagents concurrently (each in its own thread) for independent queries such as parallel file searches, codebase exploration, or web fetches. The system prompt explicitly guides the agent on when and how to parallelize: when the user requests multiple independent analyses, when exploring a large codebase, or when tasks have no data dependencies. Making multiple <span id=\"S2.SS2.SSS7.Px3.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">spawn_subagent</span> calls in the same response triggers automatic parallel execution. Upon completion, the agent is instructed to synthesize all subagent results into a single unified response organized by topic, rather than summarizing each agent separately. This trades thread overhead for latency reduction on independent operations.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS2.SSS7.Px4\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Subagent prompt refinements.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS2.SSS7.Px4.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS2.SSS7.Px4.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Subagent prompts include explicit termination conditions to prevent over-exploration. The Code Explorer subagent has stop conditions (“<em id=\"S2.SS2.SSS7.Px4.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">stop when evidence is clear</em>,” “<em id=\"S2.SS2.SSS7.Px4.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">stop if progress stalls</em>,” “<em id=\"S2.SS2.SSS7.Px4.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">prefer depth over breadth</em>”) and an anti-loop instruction (“<em id=\"S2.SS2.SSS7.Px4.p1.1.4\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">re-reading the same file triggers immediate stop</em>”). The Planner subagent is instructed to include the <span id=\"S2.SS2.SSS7.Px4.p1.1.5\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">plan_file_path</span> in its completion summary so the main agent can immediately pass it to <span id=\"S2.SS2.SSS7.Px4.p1.1.6\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">present_plan</span>. The thinking-mode prompts encourage spawning Code Explorer subagents for tasks requiring deep codebase analysis.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS2.SSS7.Px5\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Design evolution.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS2.SSS7.Px5.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS2.SSS7.Px5.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Early versions gave subagents the same tools as the main agent. This caused context pollution, role confusion, and conflicts when both agents attempted to update todos simultaneously. Restricting each subagent’s tool set to its specific role improved both focus and efficiency. Early subagent prompts lacked clear stop conditions, leading to unbounded exploration where the Code Explorer would read the same files repeatedly; adding explicit stop conditions and anti-loop instructions resolved this.</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S2.SS2.SSS7.Px5.p2\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS2.SSS7.Px5.p2.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">The agent core produces reasoning traces and tool calls; the Context Engineering Layer, described next, manages what the model sees at each step, shaping the inputs that determine every decision the agent makes.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n</section>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS3\" class=\"ltx_subsection\">\n<h3 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_subsection\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection\">2.3 </span>Context Engineering Layer</h3>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">LLM-based agents do not simply send user messages to a model and receive responses. The quality of every response is determined primarily by what the model is allowed to see in its context window: which instructions it receives, how much conversation history is retained, what it has learned from prior interactions, and how relevant external information is assembled before each call <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib56\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">56</a>, <a href=\"#bib.bib39\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">39</a>, <a href=\"#bib.bib101\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">101</a>]</cite>. We refer to the set of mechanisms that manage this window collectively as the <em id=\"S2.SS3.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">Context Engineering Layer</em> <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib56\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">56</a>, <a href=\"#bib.bib39\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">39</a>, <a href=\"#bib.bib101\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">101</a>]</cite>.</p>\n</div>\n<figure id=\"S2.F9\" class=\"ltx_figure\"><img src=\"2603.05344v3/context_engineering.png\" id=\"S2.F9.g1\" class=\"ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape\" style=\"aspect-ratio:648/362;\" width=\"648\" height=\"362\" alt=\"Refer to caption\">\n<figcaption class=\"ltx_caption ltx_centering\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure\">Figure 9: </span>Expanded view of the Tool &amp; Context layer from <a href=\"#S2.F2\" title=\"In 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Figure</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2</span></a>. Six subsystems cooperate to fill and maintain the model’s context window across a session. The subsystems are presented in lifecycle order: dynamic system prompt construction initializes behavioral instructions; dual-memory and tool result optimization shape what enters the context; system reminders and error recovery inject targeted guidance at runtime; and adaptive context compaction manages overflow when the token budget nears exhaustion.</figcaption>\n</figure>\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.p2\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.p2.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><a href=\"#S2.F9\" title=\"In 2.3 Context Engineering Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Figure</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">9</span></a> shows the subsystems and their interactions. A user query enters via the <span id=\"S2.SS3.p2.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">QueryProcessor</span>, which hands off to <span id=\"S2.SS3.p2.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">ContextPicker</span> for context assembly. The assembled context passes through <span id=\"S2.SS3.p2.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">ContextCompactor</span> for token-budget enforcement before entering the ReAct reasoning loop. Each turn, the result flows back to the <span id=\"S2.SS3.p2.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">SessionManager</span> for persistence, and tool outcomes that represent learning opportunities are processed by the adaptive memory subsystem. The remainder of this section presents each subsystem in the order it first influences the context window within a session. A final subsection (<a href=\"#S2.SS3.SSS7\" title=\"2.3.7 Context Retrieval and Assembly Pipeline ‣ 2.3 Context Engineering Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.3.7</span></a>) synthesizes these components into a unified end-to-end pipeline from user query to LLM API call.</p>\n</div>\n<section id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1\" class=\"ltx_subsubsection\">\n<h4 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection\">2.3.1 </span>Dynamic System Prompt Construction</h4>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">In an LLM-based agent, the system prompt is the primary instrument of behavioral control: it encodes the agent’s identity, capability boundaries, safety constraints, and task conventions. Every behavioral property that cannot be enforced through code, how the agent reasons, which tools it prefers, how it recovers from errors, is expressed as natural language in the system prompt. Getting this prompt right at startup is therefore not a minor configuration detail; it is the central initialization problem.</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.p2\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.p2.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">A naive approach loads a single monolithic prompt containing every possible instruction. This has two compounding costs. First, sections that are irrelevant to the current session (such as git workflow rules in a non-repository directory, subagent orchestration guidance when subagents are unused, or task-tracking instructions when the feature is disabled) consume context-window budget without contributing any behavioral value. Second, irrelevant instructions dilute the sections that <em id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.p2.1.1\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">do</em> matter, making the agent’s behavior noisier. The fix is not to trim the prompt by hand, but to make loading <em id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.p2.1.2\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">context-sensitive</em> from the start.</p>\n</div>\n<section id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px1\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Priority-ordered conditional composition.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px1.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps\">OpenDev</span> assembles each agent’s system prompt at runtime through the pipeline illustrated in <a href=\"#S2.F10\" title=\"In Priority-ordered conditional composition. ‣ 2.3.1 Dynamic System Prompt Construction ‣ 2.3 Context Engineering Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Figure</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">10</span></a>. Behavioral instructions are factored into independent <em id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px1.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">sections</em>, each stored as a separate markdown file and registered with two metadata fields: a <em id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px1.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">condition</em> predicate over a runtime context dictionary (<span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px1.p1.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">None</span> means always include), and a <em id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px1.p1.1.5\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">priority</em> integer that controls reading order. At initialization the <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px1.p1.1.6\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">PromptComposer</span> executes four steps:</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px1.p2\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<ul id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px1.p2.1\" class=\"ltx_itemize\">\n<li id=\"S2.I3.i1\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\">1.</span> \n<div id=\"S2.I3.i1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S2.I3.i1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S2.I3.i1.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Filter.</span> Evaluate each section’s predicate against the current environment snapshot. Sections that return <span id=\"S2.I3.i1.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">False</span> are excluded before any file I/O occurs. For example, <span id=\"S2.I3.i1.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">main-git-workflow.md</span> is gated on <span id=\"S2.I3.i1.p1.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">in_git_repo</span>; it is never loaded when the working directory is not a repository.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"S2.I3.i2\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;padding-top:0.5pt;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\">2.</span> \n<div id=\"S2.I3.i2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S2.I3.i2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S2.I3.i2.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Sort.</span> Order the surviving sections by ascending priority: lower values appear earlier, placing identity and persona rules before environment-derived context.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"S2.I3.i3\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;padding-top:0.5pt;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\">3.</span> \n<div id=\"S2.I3.i3.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S2.I3.i3.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S2.I3.i3.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Load.</span> Read each markdown file, strip human-readable frontmatter, and resolve <span id=\"S2.I3.i3.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">${VAR}</span> placeholders via a centralized name registry that decouples template prose from concrete tool identifiers.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"S2.I3.i4\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;padding-top:0.5pt;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\">4.</span> \n<div id=\"S2.I3.i4.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S2.I3.i4.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S2.I3.i4.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Join.</span> Concatenate loaded sections and append to the core role text and dynamically collected environment block, producing the complete system prompt.</p>\n</div></li>\n</ul>\n</div>\n<figure id=\"S2.F10\" class=\"ltx_figure\"><img src=\"2603.05344v3/prompt_composer.png\" id=\"S2.F10.g1\" class=\"ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape\" style=\"aspect-ratio:648/283;\" width=\"648\" height=\"283\" alt=\"Refer to caption\">\n<figcaption class=\"ltx_caption ltx_centering\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure\">Figure 10: </span>Detailed view of the prompt composition subsystem from <a href=\"#S2.F9\" title=\"In 2.3 Context Engineering Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Figure</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">9</span></a>. Sections are registered with optional condition predicates and priority values. At agent initialization the <span id=\"S2.F10.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">PromptComposer</span> evaluates each predicate against the runtime environment, sorts surviving sections by ascending priority, loads their markdown templates, and joins them into the final system prompt. Four logical tiers, Core Identity, Tool Definitions, Safety &amp; Rules, and Dynamic Context, which organize sections by function. Dashed borders indicate conditionally loaded sections that are included only when their predicate is satisfied.</figcaption>\n</figure>\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px1.p3\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px1.p3.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">The default action-mode agent registers modular sections across five functional tiers: <em id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px1.p3.1.1\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">Core Identity</em> for persona and non-negotiable constraints, <em id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px1.p3.1.2\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">Tool Definitions</em> for tool-use and code-quality guidance needed during execution, <em id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px1.p3.1.3\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">Safety &amp; Rules</em> for conditionally loaded policies such as git conventions and task-tracking instructions, <em id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px1.p3.1.4\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">Provider-Specific Guidance</em> for LLM-provider-specific behavioral hints, and <em id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px1.p3.1.5\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">Dynamic Context</em> for session-specific metadata. The thinking-mode agent registers fewer sections, deliberately omitting tool-use guidance to avoid biasing tool-free reasoning toward premature action. <a href=\"#A3\" title=\"Appendix C Modular System Prompt Composition ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Appendix</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">C</span></a> provides the complete section registry with conditions and summaries for all main and thinking sections; <a href=\"#A11\" title=\"Appendix K Full System Prompt Templates ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Appendix</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">K</span></a> reproduces the verbatim content of every template.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px2\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Mode-specific variants and variable substitution.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Different reasoning phases require fundamentally different prompts. Normal (action) mode loads all registered sections across five tiers. Thinking mode, a tool-free reasoning pre-phase, loads only a small set of purpose-built sections: available-tool awareness (so the model knows what actions are possible without being tempted to invoke them), subagent guidance, code-reference conventions, and output-format rules. Planning mode uses a standalone template optimized for read-only exploration. This mode specialization is achieved through a factory function: <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px2.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">create_composer(templates_dir, mode=\"system/main\")</span> returns the full action composer, while <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px2.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">mode=\"system/thinking\"</span> returns the minimal thinking composer.</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px2.p2\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px2.p2.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Templates use <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px2.p2.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">${VAR}</span> placeholders resolved at render time by a <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px2.p2.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">PromptRenderer</span>. A centralized <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px2.p2.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">PromptVariables</span> registry maps symbolic names to concrete tool identifiers; for example, <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px2.p2.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">${EDIT_TOOL.name}</span> resolves to <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px2.p2.1.5\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">edit_file</span>. This indirection decouples template prose from tool naming: renaming a tool requires changing one registry entry rather than editing every template.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px3\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Provider-specific conditional sections.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px3.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px3.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Different LLM providers have meaningfully different capabilities and conventions: Anthropic models support <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px3.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">tool_use</span> content blocks and extended thinking, OpenAI models use function calling with structured output support, and inference providers like Fireworks have different context window limits. Without provider-specific guidance, the agent may reference capabilities it does not have. The <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px3.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">PromptComposer</span> addresses this with mutually exclusive conditional sections gated on the <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px3.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">model_provider</span> field from the runtime environment context. Exactly one provider section (OpenAI, Anthropic, Fireworks) is included per prompt based on the active provider, and unknown providers receive no section (graceful degradation).</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px4\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Provider-level prompt caching.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px4.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px4.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">For providers that support input caching (currently Anthropic), the <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px4.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">PromptComposer</span> offers a <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px4.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">compose_two_part()</span> method that splits the assembled prompt into a <em id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px4.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">stable</em> part and a <em id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px4.p1.1.4\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">dynamic</em> part. Each section is annotated with a <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px4.p1.1.5\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">cacheable</span> flag (defaulting to <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px4.p1.1.6\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">True</span>); sections marked cacheable (base instructions, tool descriptions, safety policy) are concatenated into the stable part, and the remainder (environment metadata, session-specific context) into the dynamic part. The <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px4.p1.1.7\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">AnthropicAdapter</span> structures these as a two-element content array: the stable block carries a <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px4.p1.1.8\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">cache_control: {\"type\": \"ephemeral\"}</span> header, while the dynamic block carries none. Since the system prompt is re-sent on every LLM call and the stable portion typically comprises 80–90% of the total, caching it yields substantial cost savings over a multi-turn session (approximately 88% reduction in input token cost for the cached portion). Providers that do not support this mechanism receive the full concatenated prompt as a single string, with no behavioral difference.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px5\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Two-tier fallback.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px5.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS1.Px5.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">If an individual section file is missing, the composer skips it and proceeds, so the agent starts with a slightly reduced prompt rather than failing. If modular composition fails wholesale (e.g., the templates directory is absent), the builder falls back to a monolithic core template. This guarantees agent startup under partial-deployment conditions.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS3.SSS2\" class=\"ltx_subsubsection\">\n<h4 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection\">2.3.2 </span>Tool Result Optimization</h4>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Raw tool outputs consume far more tokens than their informational value warrants. A single <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS2.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">read_file</span> may return 2,000–3,000 tokens of source code, a directory listing may enumerate hundreds of entries, and a test-runner invocation may produce thousands of lines of TAP output. Left unchecked, verbose results dominate the context window within a few iterations, crowding out the user query and system instructions that drive the agent’s behavior. Tool result optimization addresses this by transforming raw outputs into compact, semantically preserving representations before they enter the conversation history.</p>\n</div>\n<section id=\"S2.SS3.SSS2.Px1\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Per-tool-type summarization.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS2.Px1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS2.Px1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Each tool result passes through a dedicated summarizer that maps the tool name and raw output to a concise summary (typically 50–200 characters). The summarizer is dispatched by tool name and applies a type-specific compression strategy:</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS2.Px1.p2\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<ul id=\"S2.SS3.SSS2.Px1.p2.1\" class=\"ltx_itemize\">\n<li id=\"S2.I4.i1\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\"><math id=\"S2.I4.i1.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\bullet\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\bullet</annotation></semantics></math></span> \n<div id=\"S2.I4.i1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.I4.i1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S2.I4.i1.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">File reads</span> are replaced with metadata: “<math id=\"S2.I4.i1.p1.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\checkmark\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mi>✓</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\checkmark</annotation></semantics></math><span id=\"S2.I4.i1.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\"> Read file (142 lines, 4,831 chars)</span>”. The full content remains available through re-reading, but the context carries only the proof that the read occurred and the file’s approximate size.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"S2.I4.i2\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\"><math id=\"S2.I4.i2.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\bullet\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\bullet</annotation></semantics></math></span> \n<div id=\"S2.I4.i2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.I4.i2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S2.I4.i2.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Search results</span> report match counts rather than matched lines: “<math id=\"S2.I4.i2.p1.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\checkmark\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mi>✓</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\checkmark</annotation></semantics></math><span id=\"S2.I4.i2.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\"> Search completed (23 matches found)</span>”. When a search returns no results, the summary reflects this explicitly so the agent can redirect.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"S2.I4.i3\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\"><math id=\"S2.I4.i3.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\bullet\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\bullet</annotation></semantics></math></span> \n<div id=\"S2.I4.i3.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.I4.i3.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S2.I4.i3.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Directory listings</span> are collapsed to item counts: “<math id=\"S2.I4.i3.p1.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\checkmark\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mi>✓</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\checkmark</annotation></semantics></math><span id=\"S2.I4.i3.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\"> Listed directory (47 items)</span>”. The raw listing, which often contains deeply nested paths, is replaced by a single-line summary.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"S2.I4.i4\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\"><math id=\"S2.I4.i4.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\bullet\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\bullet</annotation></semantics></math></span> \n<div id=\"S2.I4.i4.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.I4.i4.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S2.I4.i4.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Command execution</span> adapts to output length: short outputs (<math id=\"S2.I4.i4.p1.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\leq\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo>≤</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\leq</annotation></semantics></math>100 characters) are retained verbatim; longer outputs report line counts: “<math id=\"S2.I4.i4.p1.m2\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\checkmark\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mi>✓</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\checkmark</annotation></semantics></math><span id=\"S2.I4.i4.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\"> Command executed (312 lines of output)</span>”.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"S2.I4.i5\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\"><math id=\"S2.I4.i5.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\bullet\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\bullet</annotation></semantics></math></span> \n<div id=\"S2.I4.i5.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S2.I4.i5.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S2.I4.i5.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Errors</span> are truncated to 200 characters with a classified prefix: “<math id=\"S2.I4.i5.p1.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\times\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\times</annotation></semantics></math><span id=\"S2.I4.i5.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\"> Error: FileNotFoundError: ...</span>”. This ensures the agent receives enough information for error recovery (<a href=\"#S2.SS3.SSS5\" title=\"2.3.5 Context-Injected Error Recovery ‣ 2.3 Context Engineering Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.3.5</span></a>) without consuming excessive context on stack traces.</p>\n</div></li>\n</ul>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS3.SSS2.Px2\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Large output offloading.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS2.Px2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS2.Px2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">For outputs that exceed 8,000 characters (approximately 2,000 tokens), the summarizer is insufficient: the full output would still dominate the context even after summarization. These outputs are <em id=\"S2.SS3.SSS2.Px2.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">offloaded</em> to scratch files before entering the conversation history. The system writes the full output to a session-specific scratch directory (<span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS2.Px2.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">~/.opendev/scratch/&lt;session_id&gt;/</span>) and replaces the output in the conversation with a 500-character preview plus a reference path: “<span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS2.Px2.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">[Output offloaded: 2,341 lines, 48,203 chars <math id=\"S2.SS3.SSS2.Px2.p1.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\to\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo stretchy=\"false\">→</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\to</annotation></semantics></math> &lt;path&gt;]. Use read_file to see full output if needed.</span>” This creates a natural tiering system: the agent sees enough to understand the content and can <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS2.Px2.p1.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">read_file</span> the full output on demand, which is itself subject to the same offloading threshold.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS3.SSS2.Px3\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Agent-aware truncation hints.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS2.Px3.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS2.Px3.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">When output is offloaded to a scratch file, the truncation message includes a tailored recovery hint based on the current agent’s capabilities. If the agent has access to subagent delegation (the <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS2.Px3.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">spawn_subagent</span> tool), the hint suggests: “<em id=\"S2.SS3.SSS2.Px3.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">Delegate to a Code Explorer subagent to process the full output via search and read tools.</em>” If the agent lacks subagent capability (e.g., it <em id=\"S2.SS3.SSS2.Px3.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">is</em> a subagent), the hint instead suggests: “<em id=\"S2.SS3.SSS2.Px3.p1.1.4\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">Use the search tool with offset/limit parameters to process the output incrementally.</em>” This agent-aware advice prevents the common failure mode where an agent attempts a recovery strategy unavailable in its tool set, for example, a Code Explorer subagent trying to spawn another subagent.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS3.SSS2.Px4\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Interaction with compaction.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS2.Px4.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS2.Px4.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Tool result summaries and offloaded outputs serve complementary roles. At ingestion, they provide immediate context savings by replacing the full result in the conversation history. During compaction (<a href=\"#S2.SS3.SSS6\" title=\"2.3.6 Adaptive Context Compaction ‣ 2.3 Context Engineering Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.3.6</span></a>), the compactor preferentially uses pre-computed summaries when sanitizing messages for LLM-based summarization, avoiding redundant re-processing. This synergy means that even when emergency compaction is triggered, the input to the summarizer LLM is already substantially compressed, improving both the speed and quality of the compaction output.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS3.SSS2.Px5\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Design evolution.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS2.Px5.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS2.Px5.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Early versions stored full tool output in the conversation history regardless of length. A single long-running test suite could consume 30,000 tokens of context in one tool call. The per-tool summarizer reduced this to under 100 tokens in most cases. Adding the 8,000-character offloading threshold addressed the remaining outliers (large file reads, verbose command outputs) that exceeded the summarizer’s compression ratio, extending typical session length from 15–20 turns (before context overflow) to 30–40 turns without compaction.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS3.SSS3\" class=\"ltx_subsubsection\">\n<h4 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection\">2.3.3 </span>Dual-Memory Architecture for Bounded Thinking</h4>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS3.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS3.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">The thinking phase (Phase 1 of the ReAct loop, <a href=\"#S2.SS2.SSS6\" title=\"2.2.6 Extended ReAct Execution Loop ‣ 2.2 Agent Core Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.2.6</span></a>) requires conversation context for strategic reasoning, but the full conversation history can grow to hundreds of thousands of tokens. Providing the thinking model with unbounded history is infeasible: it would exceed the model’s context window and waste budget on stale detail. Providing only recent messages loses strategic context, causing the agent to “forget” its overall goals. We resolve this tension through a dual-memory architecture inspired by human cognitive science, which separates compressed long-range context from detailed short-range context.</p>\n</div>\n<section id=\"S2.SS3.SSS3.Px1\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Episodic memory.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS3.Px1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS3.Px1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">An LLM-generated summary of the full conversation history captures strategic, long-range context: decisions already made, overall goals, key findings, and important file paths. The summarizer is instructed to preserve actionable identifiers (file paths, function names, variable names, error codes) while omitting verbose tool outputs and redundant exchanges. This summary is regenerated periodically (every 5 new messages, controlled by a <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS3.Px1.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">regenerate_threshold</span> parameter) rather than on every turn. Periodic regeneration serves two purposes: it amortizes the cost of the summarization call, and it prevents <em id=\"S2.SS3.SSS3.Px1.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">summary drift</em>, a phenomenon where iteratively summarizing a summary causes accumulated distortion. By regenerating from the full history, each episodic memory snapshot is a fresh compression rather than a compression of a compression.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS3.SSS3.Px2\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Working memory.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS3.Px2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS3.Px2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">The last several message pairs (the most recent 6 exchanges by default, controlled by <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS3.Px2.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">exclude_last_n</span>) are reproduced verbatim. These recent messages contain the fine-grained operational details needed for immediate decision-making: exact file contents read in the last few turns, specific error messages, precise line numbers, and the outcome of the most recent tool calls. Summarization would destroy exactly the details that matter most for the next action.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS3.SSS3.Px3\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Combined injection.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS3.Px3.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS3.Px3.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Before each thinking LLM call, the system constructs the thinking context by concatenating: (1) the episodic memory summary, providing the “big picture”; (2) the working memory messages, providing operational detail; and (3) the current user query. This structure mirrors the distinction between episodic and working memory in cognitive architecture <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib7\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">7</a>]</cite>: episodic memory stores the gist of past experience for long-range planning, while working memory holds detailed, recently acquired information for immediate use. The thinking token budget remains bounded regardless of conversation length, since the episodic summary has a fixed maximum length (500 characters) and the working memory window is constant.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS3.SSS3.Px4\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Design evolution.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS3.Px4.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS3.Px4.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Early attempts used pure summarization for the entire history, but critical identifiers (file paths, variable names) were lost, causing the agent to reference non-existent files or misname functions. The opposite extreme, using only recent messages, lost long-range strategic context: the agent would “forget” the user’s original goal after 10 turns. The hybrid architecture addresses both failure modes. We also discovered that summarizing a previous summary (incremental summarization) accumulates errors over multiple rounds; periodic regeneration from the full history corrects this drift.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4\" class=\"ltx_subsubsection\">\n<h4 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection\">2.3.4 </span>Context-Aware System Reminders</h4>\n\n<figure id=\"S2.F11\" class=\"ltx_figure\"><img src=\"2603.05344v3/system_reminder_motivation.png\" id=\"S2.F11.g1\" class=\"ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape\" style=\"aspect-ratio:648/509;\" width=\"648\" height=\"509\" alt=\"Refer to caption\">\n<figcaption class=\"ltx_caption ltx_centering\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure\">Figure 11: </span>Detailed view of the reminder subsystem from <a href=\"#S2.F9\" title=\"In 2.3 Context Engineering Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Figure</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">9</span></a>. Without reminders (left), an agent with one incomplete todo declares completion, forcing the user to intervene and causing a loss of trust. With reminders (right), the <span id=\"S2.F11.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">ReactExecutor</span> detects the unfinished state, injects a targeted user-role message listing the outstanding item, and the agent resumes work and completes the task correctly.</figcaption>\n</figure>\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">System reminders address a fundamental reliability problem in long-running agent sessions: as the conversation grows, the model’s attention drifts away from the initial system-prompt instructions, leading to silent failures such as premature task completion, abandoned error recovery, and unchecked exploration spirals (<a href=\"#S2.F11\" title=\"In 2.3.4 Context-Aware System Reminders ‣ 2.3 Context Engineering Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Figure</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">11</span></a>).</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.p2\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.p2.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Consider a coding agent that is told, in its system prompt, to always run tests after editing code. For the first few turns, it does. But after 20 tool calls, with file contents, search results, and command outputs piling up in the conversation, it quietly stops. The instruction is still there in the system prompt, but the model no longer pays attention to it. The same pattern appears in other forms: an agent told to “<em id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.p2.1.1\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">finish all tasks before stopping</em>” declares victory with half the list incomplete; an agent that hits a file-editing error gives up instead of re-reading the file and retrying, even though its instructions say to retry.</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.p3\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.p3.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">The root cause is simple: the system prompt sits at the very beginning of the conversation. As the conversation grows longer, the model’s attention shifts toward recent messages and away from that initial block of instructions. The rules are still present in the context window, but their influence fades with distance. This is not a hypothetical concern; it is a predictable, reproducible failure mode that we observed consistently in sessions exceeding 15 tool calls.</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.p4\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.p4.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Putting all instructions up front works initially but degrades over long sessions. Re-injecting the entire system prompt every few turns wastes tokens on instructions the agent does not currently need. <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.p4.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps\">OpenDev</span> addresses this with <em id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.p4.1.2\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">system reminders</em>: short, single-purpose messages injected <em id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.p4.1.3\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">exactly when the agent needs them</em>, right before the decision point where it would otherwise go wrong. Each reminder is a brief <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.p4.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">role: user</span> message placed at maximum recency in the conversation, immediately before the next LLM call. <a href=\"#S2.F12\" title=\"In 2.3.4 Context-Aware System Reminders ‣ 2.3 Context Engineering Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Figure</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">12</span></a> illustrates the architecture.</p>\n</div>\n<figure id=\"S2.F12\" class=\"ltx_figure\"><img src=\"2603.05344v3/system_reminder.png\" id=\"S2.F12.g1\" class=\"ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape\" style=\"aspect-ratio:648/378;\" width=\"648\" height=\"378\" alt=\"Refer to caption\">\n<figcaption class=\"ltx_caption ltx_centering\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure\">Figure 12: </span>Architecture of the Reminder Injection Layer. After each iteration of the ReAct Executor Loop (top), eight event detectors examine the conversation state. When a detector fires, the corresponding reminder template is resolved via <span id=\"S2.F12.6\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">get_reminder()</span> from <span id=\"S2.F12.7\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">reminders.md</span> (with <span id=\"S2.F12.8\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">.txt</span> fallbacks for longer prompts), checked against guardrail counters that cap how many times each reminder can fire, and appended to the message list as a <span id=\"S2.F12.9\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">role: user</span> message. The next LLM call sees this reminder as the most recent input, maximizing its influence on the model’s next decision.</figcaption>\n</figure>\n<section id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.Px1\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Event detectors.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.Px1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.Px1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">As shown in <a href=\"#S2.F12\" title=\"In 2.3.4 Context-Aware System Reminders ‣ 2.3 Context Engineering Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Figure</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">12</span></a>, the injection layer monitors eight conditions at the boundary between tool execution and the next LLM call: tool failure without retry (with six error-specific recovery templates), exploration spirals (5+ consecutive reads), denied tool re-attempts, premature completion with incomplete todos, continued work after all todos are done, plan approval without follow-through, unprocessed subagent results, and empty completion messages. Each detector fires its corresponding reminder template from a catalog of named reminders organized into several categories: phase control, task lifecycle, todo enforcement, error recovery, behavioral correction, and JSON retry (<a href=\"#A6\" title=\"Appendix F System Reminder Catalog ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Appendix</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">F</span></a> provides the full catalog and injection timing).</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.Px2\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Template resolution.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.Px2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.Px2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">All reminder text lives outside source code. A single file (<span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.Px2.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">reminders.md</span>) stores short templates in named sections delimited by <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.Px2.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">--- section_name ---</span> markers. Longer prompts fall back to standalone <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.Px2.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">.txt</span> files. The entry point <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.Px2.p1.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">get_reminder(name, **kwargs)</span> parses the file once into a module-level cache on first call, looks up the section by name, and fills placeholders (e.g., <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.Px2.p1.1.5\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">{count}</span>, <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.Px2.p1.1.6\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">{todo_list}</span>) via <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.Px2.p1.1.7\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">str.format()</span>. Keeping templates in plain text makes them auditable and editable without touching Python code.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.Px3\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Guardrail counters.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.Px3.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.Px3.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">A reminder that fires on every iteration stops being helpful and becomes noise the model learns to ignore. To prevent this, each reminder type is governed by a counter or a one-shot flag tracked in the per-session <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.Px3.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">IterationContext</span> (right column of <a href=\"#S2.F12\" title=\"In 2.3.4 Context-Aware System Reminders ‣ 2.3 Context Engineering Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Figure</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">12</span></a>). Incomplete-todo nudges fire at most twice (<span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.Px3.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">MAX_TODO_NUDGES = 2</span>); error-recovery nudges fire at most three times (<span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.Px3.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">MAX_NUDGE_ATTEMPTS = 3</span>); plan-approved, all-todos-complete, and completion-summary signals each fire exactly once. If the agent does not respond to a capped nudge, the system accepts the agent’s judgment and moves on rather than looping.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.Px4\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Rationale for <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.Px4.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">role: user</span>.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.Px4.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.Px4.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Reminders are injected as <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.Px4.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">role: user</span> messages rather than <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.Px4.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">role: system</span>. After 40 turns of conversation, another system message blends into the background that the model has already partially forgotten. A user message appears at the position of highest recency in the dialogue flow; the model treats it as something that just happened, something requiring a response. Early experiments with <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.Px4.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">role: system</span> injection confirmed this: user-role reminders produced noticeably higher compliance rates.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.Px5\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Graceful degradation.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.Px5.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.Px5.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">If a reminder template is missing or retrieval fails, the agent still has its system prompt. Reminders reinforce existing instructions; they do not introduce new ones. The system works without them, but it works measurably better with them.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.Px6\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Design evolution.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.Px6.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.Px6.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">The initial system relied entirely on the system prompt. In long sessions (30+ tool calls), agents reliably exhibited attention-decay failures: premature completion, exploration loops, and failure to recover from errors. Adding just-in-time reminders resolved each failure mode. Early error recovery used a single generic “<em id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.Px6.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">try again</em>” message; classifying errors into six types with specific guidance substantially improved recovery rates, as “<em id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.Px6.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">read the file again</em>” is more actionable than “<em id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.Px6.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">fix the issue</em>.” Before one-shot flags and attempt budgets, some reminders fired on every iteration, causing the agent to loop on the nudge itself; guards were essential for stability. Early experiments also injected reminders as <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS4.Px6.p1.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">role: system</span> messages, which were less effective because the model treated them as background instructions rather than conversational prompts demanding a response.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS3.SSS5\" class=\"ltx_subsubsection\">\n<h4 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection\">2.3.5 </span>Context-Injected Error Recovery</h4>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS5.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS5.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">When a tool call fails, the raw error message enters the conversation as a tool result. Without intervention, the agent often responds with an apology rather than a recovery attempt, because the error message alone does not convey <em id=\"S2.SS3.SSS5.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">how</em> to recover. Template-based error recovery addresses this by injecting targeted recovery guidance directly into the context window, turning error messages into actionable instructions that the model can follow.</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS5.p2\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS5.p2.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">The mechanism operates in four steps: (1) classify the error by pattern-matching the message to one of six categories (permission error, file not found, edit mismatch, syntax error, rate limit, timeout); (2) retrieve the corresponding recovery template from a centralized template store; (3) format the template with context-specific details (the failing file path, the mismatched content, the specific error message); and (4) inject the formatted template as a system message immediately before the next LLM call, placing it at maximum recency in the conversation. For example, an edit-mismatch error produces the guidance: “<em id=\"S2.SS3.SSS5.p2.1.1\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">the file has changed since you last read it; re-read the file and retry your edit with the current content.</em>” This is substantially more actionable than a generic retry instruction, because it tells the model <em id=\"S2.SS3.SSS5.p2.1.2\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">what changed</em> and <em id=\"S2.SS3.SSS5.p2.1.3\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">what to do next</em>.</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS5.p3\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS5.p3.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">A budget of 3 nudge attempts per error sequence prevents infinite retry loops: after three consecutive failed recovery attempts on the same error, the system accepts the failure and allows the agent to proceed or ask the user for help. Templates are stored as plain text outside the source code, making recovery strategies extensible (new error categories require adding a template, not modifying code) and customizable (users can override templates for project-specific recovery patterns).</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS3.SSS6\" class=\"ltx_subsubsection\">\n<h4 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection\">2.3.6 </span>Adaptive Context Compaction</h4>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS6.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS6.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">As an agent operates within a ReAct loop, tool observations, such as file contents and command outputs, accumulate and quickly dominate the context window, frequently consuming 70–80% of the available token budget. Standard systems rely on a binary emergency compaction threshold (typically triggered at 95–99% capacity) that performs a lossy summarization of the conversation history. This approach results in late activation, severe information loss, and compounding errors upon subsequent compactions.</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS6.p2\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS6.p2.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">To mitigate these issues, <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS6.p2.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps\">OpenDev</span> monitors token usage incrementally, using the API’s reported <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS6.p2.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">prompt_tokens</span> count as a calibration anchor, and implements <em id=\"S2.SS3.SSS6.p2.1.3\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">Adaptive Context Compaction (ACC)</em>, a framework that manages context pressure through a five-stage pipeline of progressively aggressive reduction strategies (<a href=\"#S2.F13\" title=\"In 2.3.6 Adaptive Context Compaction ‣ 2.3 Context Engineering Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Figure</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">13</span></a>).</p>\n</div>\n<figure id=\"S2.F13\" class=\"ltx_figure\"><img src=\"2603.05344v3/adaptive_compaction_mechanism.png\" id=\"S2.F13.g1\" class=\"ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape\" style=\"aspect-ratio:648/319;\" width=\"648\" height=\"319\" alt=\"Refer to caption\">\n<figcaption class=\"ltx_caption ltx_centering\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure\">Figure 13: </span>Detailed view of the compaction subsystem from <a href=\"#S2.F9\" title=\"In 2.3 Context Engineering Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Figure</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">9</span></a>. Five stages activate at progressive pressure thresholds (70%, 80%, 85%, 90%, 99%), transitioning observations between active, faded, and archived states before emergency summarization is required.</figcaption>\n</figure>\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS6.p3\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS6.p3.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Rather than waiting for the context window to fill, ACC monitors context pressure at the start of every ReAct iteration and applies five graduated stages:</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS6.p4\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<ul id=\"S2.SS3.SSS6.p4.1\" class=\"ltx_itemize\">\n<li id=\"S2.I5.i1\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\"><math id=\"S2.I5.i1.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\bullet\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\bullet</annotation></semantics></math></span> \n<div id=\"S2.I5.i1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S2.I5.i1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S2.I5.i1.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Stage 1 - Warning (70%):</span> Context pressure is logged for monitoring. No data reduction occurs, but the system begins tracking utilization trends.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"S2.I5.i2\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\"><math id=\"S2.I5.i2.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\bullet\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\bullet</annotation></semantics></math></span> \n<div id=\"S2.I5.i2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S2.I5.i2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S2.I5.i2.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Stage 2 - Observation Masking (80%):</span> Older tool result messages are replaced in-place with compact reference pointers (e.g., <span id=\"S2.I5.i2.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">[output offloaded to scratch file]</span>), preserving the conversation structure required by the LLM API while reducing token footprint from thousands of tokens to approximately 15 per observation. The most recent tool outputs are preserved at full fidelity.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"S2.I5.i3\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\"><math id=\"S2.I5.i3.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\bullet\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\bullet</annotation></semantics></math></span> \n<div id=\"S2.I5.i3.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S2.I5.i3.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S2.I5.i3.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Stage 2.5 - Fast Pruning (85%):</span> Before resorting to aggressive masking, a lightweight pruning pass walks backward through tool result messages. Results within a protected recency budget are preserved; older results are replaced with <span id=\"S2.I5.i3.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">[pruned]</span> markers. Unlike observation masking (which replaces with reference pointers to offloaded files), pruning is a deletion-class operation (content is discarded rather than offloaded) but it targets only outputs well beyond the recency window. This is substantially cheaper than LLM-based compaction and often reclaims enough space to avoid the more disruptive stages entirely.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"S2.I5.i4\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\"><math id=\"S2.I5.i4.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\bullet\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\bullet</annotation></semantics></math></span> \n<div id=\"S2.I5.i4.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S2.I5.i4.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S2.I5.i4.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Stage 3 - Aggressive Masking (90%):</span> The preservation window shrinks to only the most recent tool outputs. All other observations are masked.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"S2.I5.i5\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\"><math id=\"S2.I5.i5.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\bullet\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\bullet</annotation></semantics></math></span> \n<div id=\"S2.I5.i5.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S2.I5.i5.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S2.I5.i5.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Stage 4 - Full Compaction (99%):</span> The entire conversation history is serialized to a scratch file (ensuring no historical detail is permanently lost), and an LLM-based summarizer compresses the middle portion of the conversation while preserving recent messages verbatim.</p>\n</div></li>\n</ul>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS6.p5\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS6.p5.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">ACC’s compaction pipeline additionally maintains an <em id=\"S2.SS3.SSS6.p5.1.1\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">Artifact Index</em>, a structured registry of all files touched and operations performed during the session (<span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS6.p5.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">read</span>, <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS6.p5.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">created</span>, <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS6.p5.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">modified</span>, <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS6.p5.1.5\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">deleted</span>). This index is serialized into the compaction summary, ensuring the agent remembers what files it has worked with even after context is compressed. The history archive path is also injected into the summary (“<em id=\"S2.SS3.SSS6.p5.1.6\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">Full conversation history archived at <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS6.p5.1.6.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">&lt;path&gt;</span>. Use <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS6.p5.1.6.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">read_file</span> to recover details if needed.</em>”), making compaction effectively non-lossy: the agent can recover any detail by reading the archive. Quantitative evaluations demonstrate that ACC reduces peak context consumption of observations by approximately 54%, often eliminating the need for emergency compaction entirely over typical 30-turn sessions.</p>\n</div>\n<section id=\"S2.SS3.SSS6.Px1\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Adaptive memory.</h5>\n\n<figure id=\"S2.F14\" class=\"ltx_figure\"><img src=\"2603.05344v3/ace.png\" id=\"S2.F14.g1\" class=\"ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape\" style=\"aspect-ratio:648/288;\" width=\"648\" height=\"288\" alt=\"Refer to caption\">\n<figcaption class=\"ltx_caption ltx_centering\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure\">Figure 14: </span>Detailed view of the memory subsystem from <a href=\"#S2.F9\" title=\"In 2.3 Context Engineering Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Figure</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">9</span></a>. Stage 1: the BulletSelector scores playbook bullets by effectiveness, recency, and semantic similarity to the current query, and the selected bullets are injected into the Generator’s system prompt alongside the user query. Stage 2: an episodic memory mechanism triggers the Reflector every five messages of interaction; the Reflector analyzes accumulated experience and produces a reasoning trace, error identification, root-cause analysis, and correct approach. Stage 3: a Curator reads the reflection and plans concrete playbook mutations (add, update, tag, or remove bullets). Stage 4: the mutations are applied to the Playbook’s bullet table and persisted to a session-scoped JSON file.</figcaption>\n</figure>\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS6.Px1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS6.Px1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Agents working in a project over multiple sessions accumulate experience about which approaches succeed and which do not. The <em id=\"S2.SS3.SSS6.Px1.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">Agentic Context Engineering</em> (ACE) subsystem captures this experience as a <em id=\"S2.SS3.SSS6.Px1.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">playbook</em>: a collection of natural-language bullets, each tagged with effectiveness counters (helpful, harmful, or neutral) and a creation timestamp. Figure <a href=\"#S2.F14\" title=\"Figure 14 ‣ Adaptive memory. ‣ 2.3.6 Adaptive Context Compaction ‣ 2.3 Context Engineering Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">14</span></a> illustrates the four-stage pipeline that keeps the playbook current. In Stage 1, the <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS6.Px1.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">BulletSelector</span> ranks every bullet by a weighted score combining effectiveness (0.5), recency decay (0.3), and semantic similarity to the current query via cosine similarity over cached embeddings (0.2); the top-ranked bullets are injected into the Generator’s system prompt so the agent can act on prior experience. Stage 2 is governed by an <em id=\"S2.SS3.SSS6.Px1.p1.1.4\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">episodic memory</em> mechanism: every five messages of agent interaction, the system activates the <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS6.Px1.p1.1.5\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">Reflector</span> to analyze the accumulated experience. The Reflector produces a reasoning trace, error identification, root-cause analysis, and correct approach, which are then distilled into bullet-level effectiveness tags (helpful / harmful / neutral), without proposing any structural changes to the playbook. Stage 3’s <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS6.Px1.p1.1.6\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">Curator</span> reads the reflection and plans concrete mutations: adding new bullets, updating existing ones, re-tagging effectiveness counters, or removing stale entries, emitted as a <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS6.Px1.p1.1.7\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">DeltaBatch</span>. Finally, in Stage 4 the mutations are applied to the Playbook’s bullet table and the updated state is persisted to a session-scoped JSON file, ready for the next query cycle.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7\" class=\"ltx_subsubsection\">\n<h4 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection\">2.3.7 </span>Context Retrieval and Assembly Pipeline</h4>\n\n<figure id=\"S2.F15\" class=\"ltx_figure\"><img src=\"2603.05344v3/context_retrieval.png\" id=\"S2.F15.g1\" class=\"ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape\" style=\"aspect-ratio:648/400;\" width=\"648\" height=\"400\" alt=\"Refer to caption\">\n<figcaption class=\"ltx_caption ltx_centering\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure\">Figure 15: </span>End-to-end synthesis of the retrieval and context components from <a href=\"#S2.F9\" title=\"In 2.3 Context Engineering Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Figure</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">9</span></a>. Four layers transform a user query into a fully assembled LLM API call: (1) retrieval tools gather raw code artifacts, (2) the Code Explorer subagent orchestrates multi-step searches in an isolated context, (3) the context assembler merges retrieved material with conversation history and system instructions, and (4) the context optimizer enforces the token budget through staged compaction before the final API call.</figcaption>\n</figure>\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Context retrieval is the single most consequential capability of a coding agent: the quality of every downstream action (editing, testing, planning) is bounded by whether the agent has located the right code in the first place. In traditional RAG pipelines <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib44\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">44</a>]</cite>, retrieval is a static, one-shot operation: embed the query, fetch top-<math id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.p1.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"k\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">k</annotation></semantics></math> documents, and generate. This works reasonably well for factual question answering over homogeneous corpora, but codebases are fundamentally different. A single user request (“fix the login bug”) may require cross-referencing an authentication handler, a database schema, a test file, and a configuration module, none of which share obvious lexical overlap with the query. Recent work on <em id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">agentic search</em> <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib88\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">88</a>]</cite> has shown that effective retrieval in complex environments requires the agent to dynamically control <em id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">when</em>, <em id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">what</em>, and <em id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.p1.1.4\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">how</em> to retrieve, interleaving reasoning with search rather than treating retrieval as a preprocessing step <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib99\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">99</a>, <a href=\"#bib.bib80\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">80</a>]</cite>. <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.p1.1.5\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps\">OpenDev</span> instantiates this principle for software engineering through a four-layer pipeline (<a href=\"#S2.F15\" title=\"In 2.3.7 Context Retrieval and Assembly Pipeline ‣ 2.3 Context Engineering Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Figure</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">15</span></a>) that progressively escalates from simple lookups to multi-step agentic search to full context assembly and optimization.</p>\n</div>\n<section id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.Px1\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Layer 1: Anchor-based retrieval tool selection.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.Px1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.Px1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Five tools form the retrieval surface: <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.Px1.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">read_file</span> for targeted file access, <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.Px1.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">list_files</span> for glob-based discovery, <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.Px1.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">text_search</span> (ripgrep) for pattern matching, <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.Px1.p1.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">find_symbol</span> for LSP-based semantic resolution, and <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.Px1.p1.1.5\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">ast_search</span> (ast-grep) for structural pattern matching (<a href=\"#S2.SS4.SSS2\" title=\"2.4.2 File
