ltx_tag_subsection\">C.4 </span>Composition Mechanics</h3>\n\n<div id=\"A3.SS4.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"A3.SS4.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">The composition pipeline operates as follows:</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"A3.SS4.p2\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<ul id=\"A3.SS4.p2.1\" class=\"ltx_itemize\">\n<li id=\"A3.I1.i1\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\"><math id=\"A3.I1.i1.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\bullet\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\bullet</annotation></semantics></math></span> \n<div id=\"A3.I1.i1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"A3.I1.i1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"A3.I1.i1.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Filter <math id=\"A3.I1.i1.p1.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\to\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo stretchy=\"false\">→</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\to</annotation></semantics></math> Sort <math id=\"A3.I1.i1.p1.m2\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\to\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo stretchy=\"false\">→</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\to</annotation></semantics></math> Load <math id=\"A3.I1.i1.p1.m3\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\to\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo stretchy=\"false\">→</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\to</annotation></semantics></math> Join:</span> Each registered section’s condition predicate is evaluated against the runtime context dictionary. Sections returning <span id=\"A3.I1.i1.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">False</span> are excluded before any file I/O. Surviving sections are sorted by ascending priority, loaded from their markdown files (with frontmatter stripped), and concatenated with double-newline separators.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"A3.I1.i2\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\"><math id=\"A3.I1.i2.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\bullet\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\bullet</annotation></semantics></math></span> \n<div id=\"A3.I1.i2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"A3.I1.i2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"A3.I1.i2.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Two-part composition for prompt caching:</span> The <span id=\"A3.I1.i2.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">compose_two_part()</span> method partitions sections into <em id=\"A3.I1.i2.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">stable</em> (cacheable) and <em id=\"A3.I1.i2.p1.1.4\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">dynamic</em> parts. For Anthropic’s API, the stable part receives a <span id=\"A3.I1.i2.p1.1.5\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">cache_control</span> header, yielding approximately 88% cost reduction on the cached portion across multi-turn sessions. Typically 19 of 21 sections are stable; only <span id=\"A3.I1.i2.p1.1.6\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">scratchpad</span> and <span id=\"A3.I1.i2.p1.1.7\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">reminders-note</span> are dynamic.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"A3.I1.i3\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\"><math id=\"A3.I1.i3.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\bullet\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\bullet</annotation></semantics></math></span> \n<div id=\"A3.I1.i3.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"A3.I1.i3.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"A3.I1.i3.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Mode-specific composers:</span> A factory function <span id=\"A3.I1.i3.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">create_composer(templates_dir, mode)</span> returns the appropriate composer: <span id=\"A3.I1.i3.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">\"system/main\"</span> yields the 21-section action composer; <span id=\"A3.I1.i3.p1.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">\"system/thinking\"</span> yields the 4-section thinking composer. Planning mode uses a standalone template optimized for read-only exploration.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"A3.I1.i4\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\"><math id=\"A3.I1.i4.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\bullet\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\bullet</annotation></semantics></math></span> \n<div id=\"A3.I1.i4.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"A3.I1.i4.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"A3.I1.i4.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Variable substitution:</span> Templates use <span id=\"A3.I1.i4.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">${VAR}</span> placeholders resolved at render time by <span id=\"A3.I1.i4.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">PromptRenderer</span>. A centralized <span id=\"A3.I1.i4.p1.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">PromptVariables</span> registry maps symbolic names to concrete tool identifiers (e.g., <span id=\"A3.I1.i4.p1.1.5\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">${EDIT_TOOL.name}</span> <math id=\"A3.I1.i4.p1.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\to\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo stretchy=\"false\">→</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\to</annotation></semantics></math> <span id=\"A3.I1.i4.p1.1.6\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">edit_file</span>), decoupling template prose from tool naming.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"A3.I1.i5\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\"><math id=\"A3.I1.i5.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\bullet\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\bullet</annotation></semantics></math></span> \n<div id=\"A3.I1.i5.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"A3.I1.i5.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"A3.I1.i5.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Two-tier fallback:</span> If an individual section file is missing, the composer skips it and proceeds with a reduced prompt. If modular composition fails wholesale (e.g., templates directory absent), the builder falls back to a monolithic core template, guaranteeing agent startup under partial-deployment conditions.</p>\n</div></li>\n</ul>\n</div>\n</section>\n</section>\n<section id=\"A4\" class=\"ltx_appendix\">\n<h2 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_appendix\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix\">Appendix D </span>Edit Tool Fuzzy Matching Chain</h2>\n\n<div id=\"A4.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"A4.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">The <span id=\"A4.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">edit_file</span> tool (<a href=\"#S2.SS4.SSS2\" title=\"2.4.2 File Operations ‣ 2.4 Tool System ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.4.2</span></a>) implements a chain-of-responsibility pattern with nine replacer classes, each addressing a specific mismatch category between the LLM’s specified <span id=\"A4.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">old_content</span> and the actual file content. The chain short-circuits on first match, so exact matches incur zero overhead from the fuzzy passes. Each replacer returns the <em id=\"A4.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">actual substring found in the original file</em> (not the search query), preserving the file’s original formatting.</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"A4.p2\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<ul id=\"A4.p2.1\" class=\"ltx_itemize\">\n<li id=\"A4.I1.i1\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\">1.</span> \n<div id=\"A4.I1.i1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"A4.I1.i1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"A4.I1.i1.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Simple:</span> Exact string match (baseline).</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"A4.I1.i2\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;padding-top:0.5pt;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\">2.</span> \n<div id=\"A4.I1.i2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"A4.I1.i2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"A4.I1.i2.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Line-trimmed:</span> Strip trailing whitespace per line before comparing.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"A4.I1.i3\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;padding-top:0.5pt;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\">3.</span> \n<div id=\"A4.I1.i3.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"A4.I1.i3.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"A4.I1.i3.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Block-anchor:</span> Use first and last lines as anchors; score middle region via <span id=\"A4.I1.i3.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">SequenceMatcher</span> with a 0.3 similarity threshold for multi-candidate matches.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"A4.I1.i4\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;padding-top:0.5pt;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\">4.</span> \n<div id=\"A4.I1.i4.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"A4.I1.i4.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"A4.I1.i4.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Whitespace-normalized:</span> Collapse all whitespace runs to single spaces.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"A4.I1.i5\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;padding-top:0.5pt;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\">5.</span> \n<div id=\"A4.I1.i5.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"A4.I1.i5.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"A4.I1.i5.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Indentation-flexible:</span> Ignore all leading whitespace, skip blank lines.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"A4.I1.i6\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;padding-top:0.5pt;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\">6.</span> \n<div id=\"A4.I1.i6.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"A4.I1.i6.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"A4.I1.i6.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Escape-normalized:</span> Unescape common sequences (<span id=\"A4.I1.i6.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">\\n</span>, <span id=\"A4.I1.i6.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">\\t</span>, <span id=\"A4.I1.i6.p1.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">\\\\</span>).</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"A4.I1.i7\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;padding-top:0.5pt;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\">7.</span> \n<div id=\"A4.I1.i7.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"A4.I1.i7.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"A4.I1.i7.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Trimmed-boundary:</span> Try trimmed content; expand to full line boundaries if partial match found.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"A4.I1.i8\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;padding-top:0.5pt;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\">8.</span> \n<div id=\"A4.I1.i8.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"A4.I1.i8.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"A4.I1.i8.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Context-aware:</span> Use first and last non-empty lines as anchors, score all candidate regions with a 0.5 similarity threshold.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"A4.I1.i9\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;padding-top:0.5pt;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\">9.</span> \n<div id=\"A4.I1.i9.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"A4.I1.i9.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"A4.I1.i9.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Multi-occurrence:</span> Trimmed line-by-line exact match as last resort across all occurrences.</p>\n</div></li>\n</ul>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"A5\" class=\"ltx_appendix\">\n<h2 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_appendix\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix\">Appendix E </span>Shell Execution Pipeline</h2>\n\n<div id=\"A5.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"A5.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">The shell execution pipeline (<a href=\"#S2.SS4.SSS3\" title=\"2.4.3 Shell Execution and Background Tasks ‣ 2.4 Tool System ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.4.3</span></a>) processes every <span id=\"A5.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">run_command</span> invocation through six stages, illustrated in <a href=\"#S2.F17\" title=\"In 2.4.3 Shell Execution and Background Tasks ‣ 2.4 Tool System ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Figure</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">17</span></a>.</p>\n</div>\n<section id=\"A5.SS1\" class=\"ltx_subsection\">\n<h3 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_subsection\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection\">E.1 </span>Six-Stage Pipeline Details</h3>\n\n<div id=\"A5.SS1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<ul id=\"A5.SS1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_itemize\">\n<li id=\"A5.I1.i1\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\">1.</span> \n<div id=\"A5.I1.i1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"A5.I1.i1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"A5.I1.i1.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Safety gates.</span> Three checks run before any command executes: (a) permission configuration determines whether the command class requires approval; (b) allowed-command matching checks against user-configured safe patterns; (c) dangerous pattern blocking rejects catastrophic operations (<span id=\"A5.I1.i1.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">rm -rf /</span>, <span id=\"A5.I1.i1.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">sudo</span>, fork bombs, <span id=\"A5.I1.i1.p1.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">curl|bash</span> pipe chains, <span id=\"A5.I1.i1.p1.1.5\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">dd</span> to device files) with no user override.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"A5.I1.i2\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;padding-top:0.5pt;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\">2.</span> \n<div id=\"A5.I1.i2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"A5.I1.i2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"A5.I1.i2.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Command preparation.</span> Interactive prompts are auto-confirmed for known package managers (<span id=\"A5.I1.i2.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">npm init</span>, <span id=\"A5.I1.i2.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">npx</span>) by prepending <span id=\"A5.I1.i2.p1.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">yes |</span>. Python commands receive <span id=\"A5.I1.i2.p1.1.5\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1</span> to prevent output buffering that would defeat real-time streaming.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"A5.I1.i3\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;padding-top:0.5pt;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\">3.</span> \n<div id=\"A5.I1.i3.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"A5.I1.i3.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"A5.I1.i3.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Server detection.</span> A regex match against 16 server patterns (<a href=\"#A5.T6\" title=\"In E.2 Server Detection Patterns ‣ Appendix E Shell Execution Pipeline ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Table</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">6</span></a>) auto-promotes matching commands to background mode regardless of the caller’s setting.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"A5.I1.i4\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;padding-top:0.5pt;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\">4.</span> \n<div id=\"A5.I1.i4.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"A5.I1.i4.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"A5.I1.i4.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Execution fork.</span> Background commands spawn in a pseudo-terminal (<span id=\"A5.I1.i4.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">pty.openpty()</span> with <span id=\"A5.I1.i4.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">Popen</span> attached to the slave file descriptor) for terminal-emulated output that correctly handles ANSI codes, progress bars, and interactive programs. Foreground commands use <span id=\"A5.I1.i4.p1.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">subprocess.Popen</span> with pipes and <span id=\"A5.I1.i4.p1.1.5\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">start_new_session=True</span> for process-group isolation, ensuring that killing the command kills all child processes.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"A5.I1.i5\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;padding-top:0.5pt;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\">5.</span> \n<div id=\"A5.I1.i5.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"A5.I1.i5.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"A5.I1.i5.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Output management.</span> Output is capped at 30,000 characters using head-tail truncation (first 10,000 + last 10,000 on overflow). Real-time streaming delivers output to the UI via callback. <span id=\"A5.I1.i5.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">select.select()</span> polls at 100ms intervals, balancing responsiveness against CPU overhead.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"A5.I1.i6\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;padding-top:0.5pt;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\">6.</span> \n<div id=\"A5.I1.i6.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"A5.I1.i6.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"A5.I1.i6.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Timeout and interrupt.</span> Idle timeout kills commands after 60 seconds of no output. Absolute timeout caps execution at 600 seconds. The <span id=\"A5.I1.i6.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">InterruptToken</span> (shared per user query) is checked each polling cycle; when triggered, the handler kills the entire process group via <span id=\"A5.I1.i6.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">os.killpg()</span>.</p>\n</div></li>\n</ul>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"A5.SS2\" class=\"ltx_subsection\">\n<h3 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_subsection\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection\">E.2 </span>Server Detection Patterns</h3>\n\n<div id=\"A5.SS2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"A5.SS2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><a href=\"#A5.T6\" title=\"In E.2 Server Detection Patterns ‣ Appendix E Shell Execution Pipeline ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Table</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">6</span></a> lists the 16 regex patterns used to auto-promote commands to background mode. All patterns are matched with <span id=\"A5.SS2.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">re.IGNORECASE</span>.</p>\n</div>\n<figure id=\"A5.T6\" class=\"ltx_table\">\n<figcaption ltx_tag_appendix\">Appendix F </span>System Reminder Catalog</h2>\n\n<div id=\"A6.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"A6.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">This appendix provides the complete catalog of the 24 named system reminders described in <a href=\"#S2.SS3.SSS4\" title=\"2.3.4 Context-Aware System Reminders ‣ 2.3 Context Engineering Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.3.4</span></a>, organized by category, along with the 9-step injection timing within each ReAct iteration.</p>\n</div>\n<section id=\"A6.SS1\" class=\"ltx_subsection\">\n<h3 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_subsection\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection\">F.1 </span>Reminder Categories</h3>\n\n<div id=\"A6.SS1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"A6.SS1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">The 24 reminders are organized into six functional categories:</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"A6.SS1.p2\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<ul id=\"A6.SS1.p2.1\" class=\"ltx_itemize\">\n<li id=\"A6.I1.i1\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\"><math id=\"A6.I1.i1.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\bullet\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\bullet</annotation></semantics></math></span> \n<div id=\"A6.I1.i1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"A6.I1.i1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"A6.I1.i1.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Phase control</span> (4 reminders): Manage thinking/action phase transitions. Inject thinking traces into the action phase context; control whether the agent should reason deeply or act directly.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"A6.I1.i2\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\"><math id=\"A6.I1.i2.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\bullet\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\bullet</annotation></semantics></math></span> \n<div id=\"A6.I1.i2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"A6.I1.i2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"A6.I1.i2.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Task lifecycle</span> (5 reminders): Steer phase transitions in multi-step workflows. After a subagent returns, nudge the main agent to synthesize results. After plan approval, restate the plan and todos with explicit workflow instructions. On session resume, reference the existing plan file.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"A6.I1.i3\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\"><math id=\"A6.I1.i3.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\bullet\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\bullet</annotation></semantics></math></span> \n<div id=\"A6.I1.i3.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"A6.I1.i3.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"A6.I1.i3.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Todo enforcement</span> (2 reminders): Gate premature completion. When the agent calls <span id=\"A6.I1.i3.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">task_complete</span> with incomplete todos, reject the call and list remaining items. When all todos are done, signal finalization. Capped at 2 nudges per run.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"A6.I1.i4\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\"><math id=\"A6.I1.i4.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\bullet\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\bullet</annotation></semantics></math></span> \n<div id=\"A6.I1.i4.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"A6.I1.i4.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"A6.I1.i4.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Error recovery</span> (8 reminders): One generic nudge plus six type-specific nudges selected by error classification (permission, file-not-found, syntax, rate-limit, timeout, edit-mismatch) and one Docker-specific nudge. Capped at 3 attempts per error sequence.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"A6.I1.i5\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\"><math id=\"A6.I1.i5.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\bullet\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\bullet</annotation></semantics></math></span> \n<div id=\"A6.I1.i5.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"A6.I1.i5.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"A6.I1.i5.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Behavioral</span> (5 reminders): Correct observable anti-patterns. After 5+ consecutive read-only tool calls, break the exploration spiral. After the user denies a tool call, prevent re-attempt. On empty completion, request a brief outcome summary. At the iteration safety limit, force summarization.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"A6.I1.i6\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\"><math id=\"A6.I1.i6.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\bullet\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\bullet</annotation></semantics></math></span> \n<div id=\"A6.I1.i6.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"A6.I1.i6.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"A6.I1.i6.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">JSON retry</span> (2 reminders): Specialized parse-retry prompts for the memory system’s Reflector and Curator components when JSON output fails to parse.</p>\n</div></li>\n</ul>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"A6.SS2\" class=\"ltx_subsection\">\n<h3 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_subsection\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection\">F.2 </span>Injection Timing</h3>\n\n<div id=\"A6.SS2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"A6.SS2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Reminders are injected by the ReAct executor in a strict 9-step ordering within each iteration:</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"A6.SS2.p2\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<ul id=\"A6.SS2.p2.1\" class=\"ltx_itemize\">\n<li id=\"A6.I2.i1\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\">1.</span> \n<div id=\"A6.I2.i1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"A6.I2.i1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Auto-compaction check (context pressure evaluation).</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"A6.I2.i2\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;padding-top:0.5pt;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\">2.</span> \n<div id=\"A6.I2.i2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"A6.I2.i2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Interrupt check (user cancellation).</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"A6.I2.i3\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;padding-top:0.5pt;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\">3.</span> \n<div id=\"A6.I2.i3.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"A6.I2.i3.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Thinking phase with optional trace injection into action context.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"A6.I2.i4\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;padding-top:0.5pt;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\">4.</span> \n<div id=\"A6.I2.i4.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"A6.I2.i4.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Subagent-completion signal (if a subagent returned results).</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"A6.I2.i5\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;padding-top:0.5pt;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\">5.</span> \n<div id=\"A6.I2.i5.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"A6.I2.i5.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Drain UI-thread messages (approval results, user input).</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"A6.I2.i6\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;padding-top:0.5pt;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\">6.</span> \n<div id=\"A6.I2.i6.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"A6.I2.i6.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Interrupt check (second gate before LLM call).</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"A6.I2.i7\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;padding-top:0.5pt;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\">7.</span> \n<div id=\"A6.I2.i7.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"A6.I2.i7.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Action phase LLM call.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"A6.I2.i8\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;padding-top:0.5pt;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\">8.</span> \n<div id=\"A6.I2.i8.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"A6.I2.i8.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Response dispatch: reminders diverge based on response type:</p>\n<ul id=\"A6.I2.i8.p1.2\" class=\"ltx_itemize\">\n<li id=\"A6.I2.i8.I1.i1\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\"><math id=\"A6.I2.i8.I1.i1.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\bullet\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\bullet</annotation></semantics></math></span> \n<div id=\"A6.I2.i8.I1.i1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"A6.I2.i8.I1.i1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><em id=\"A6.I2.i8.I1.i1.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">No tool calls path:</em> check for failed-tool nudges, incomplete-todo nudges, and empty-completion nudges, in that order.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"A6.I2.i8.I1.i2\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\"><math id=\"A6.I2.i8.I1.i2.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\bullet\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\bullet</annotation></semantics></math></span> \n<div id=\"A6.I2.i8.I1.i2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"A6.I2.i8.I1.i2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><em id=\"A6.I2.i8.I1.i2.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">Has tool calls path:</em> after tool execution, check for plan-approved signals, all-todos-complete signals, tool-denied nudges, and consecutive-reads nudges.</p>\n</div></li>\n</ul>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"A6.I2.i9\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;padding-top:0.5pt;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\">9.</span> \n<div id=\"A6.I2.i9.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"A6.I2.i9.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Session persistence (auto-save).</p>\n</div></li>\n</ul>\n</div>\n<section id=\"A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Safety guards.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Two mechanisms prevent reminder degeneration into noise: (1) <em id=\"A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">one-shot flags</em> ensure certain reminders fire at most once per agent run (<span id=\"A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">plan_approved_signal_injected</span>, <span id=\"A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">all_todos_complete_nudged</span>, <span id=\"A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">completion_nudge_sent</span>); and (2) <em id=\"A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.5\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">attempt budgets</em> class=\"ltx_page_content\">\n<article class=\"ltx_document ltx_authors_1line\">\n<h1 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_document\">Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?</h1>\n<div class=\"ltx_author_before\">  </span><span class=\"ltx_creator ltx_role_author\">\n<span class=\"ltx_personname\">Aditya Parameswaran\n</span><span class=\"ltx_author_notes\"><span class=\"ltx_author_before\">  </span><span class=\"ltx_creator ltx_role_author\">\n<span class=\"ltx_personname\">Dan Klein\n</span><span class=\"ltx_author_notes\"><span class=\"ltx_author_before\">  </span><span class=\"ltx_creator ltx_role_author\">\n<span class=\"ltx_personname\">Kannan Ramchandran\n</span><span class=\"ltx_author_notes\"><span class=\"ltx_author_before\">  </span><span class=\"ltx_creator ltx_role_author\">\n<span class=\"ltx_personname\">Matei Zaharia\n</span><span class=\"ltx_author_notes\"><span class=\"ltx_author_notes_content\">\n<span class=\"ltx_contact ltx_role_affiliation\"><span class=\"ltx_contact_name\">Affiliation: </span>UC Berkeley\n</span></span></span></span>\n<span class=\"ltx_author_before\">  </span><span class=\"ltx_creator ltx_role_author\">\n<span class=\"ltx_personname\">Joseph E. Gonzalez\n</span><span class=\"ltx_author_notes\"><span class=\"ltx_author_notes_content\">\n<span class=\"ltx_contact ltx_role_affiliation\"><span class=\"ltx_contact_name\">Affiliation: </span>UC Berkeley\n</span></span></span></span>\n<span class=\"ltx_author_before\">  </span><span class=\"ltx_creator ltx_role_author\">\n<span class=\"ltx_personname\">Ion Stoica\n</span><span class=\"ltx_author_notes\"><span class=\"ltx_author_notes_content\">\n<span class=\"ltx_contact ltx_role_affiliation\"><span class=\"ltx_contact_name\">Affiliation: </span>UC Berkeley\n</span></span></span></span>\n<span class=\"ltx_creator ltx_role_author\"><span class=\"ltx_author_notes\"><span class=\"ltx_author_notes_content\">\n<span class=\"ltx_contact ltx_role_affiliation\"><span class=\"ltx_contact_name\">Affiliation: </span>Intesa Sanpaolo*Equal Contribution\n</span></span></span></span></div>\n\n<div id=\"abstract1\" class=\"ltx_abstract\"><h6 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_abstract\">Abstract</h6>\n    \n<p id=\"abstract1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Despite enthusiasm for Multi-Agent LLM Systems (MAS), their performance gains on popular benchmarks are often minimal. This gap highlights a critical need for a principled understanding of why MAS fail. Addressing this question requires systematic identification and analysis of failure patterns.\nWe introduce <span id=\"abstract1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST-Data</span>, a comprehensive dataset of 1600+ annotated traces collected across 7 popular MAS frameworks. <span id=\"abstract1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST-Data</span> is the first multi-agent system dataset to outline the failure dynamics in MAS for guiding the development of better future systems. To enable systematic classification of failures for <span id=\"abstract1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST-Data</span>, we build the first <span id=\"abstract1.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">M</span>ulti-<span id=\"abstract1.1.5\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">A</span>gent <span id=\"abstract1.1.6\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">S</span>ystem Failure <span id=\"abstract1.1.7\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">T</span>axonomy (<span id=\"abstract1.1.8\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST</span>). We develop <span id=\"abstract1.1.9\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST</span> through rigorous analysis of 150 traces, guided closely by expert human annotators and validated by high inter-annotator agreement (<math id=\"abstract1.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\kappa=0.88{}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.88</mn></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\kappa=0.88{}</annotation></semantics></math>). This process identifies 14 unique modes, clustered into 3 categories: (i) system design issues, (ii) inter-agent misalignment, and (iii) task verification.\nTo enable scalable annotation, we develop an LLM-as-a-Judge pipeline with high agreement with human annotations. We leverage <span id=\"abstract1.1.10\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST</span> and <span id=\"abstract1.1.11\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST-Data</span> to analyze failure patterns across models (GPT4, Claude 3, Qwen2.5, CodeLlama) and tasks (coding, math, general agent), demonstrating opportunities for improvement through better MAS design. Our analysis provides insights revealing that identified failures require more sophisticated solutions, highlighting a clear roadmap for future research. We publicly release our comprehensive dataset (<span id=\"abstract1.1.12\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST-Data</span>), the <span id=\"abstract1.1.13\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST</span>, and our LLM annotator to facilitate widespread research and development in MAS.<span id=\"footnote1\" class=\"ltx_note ltx_role_footnote\"><sup class=\"ltx_note_mark\">1</sup><span class=\"ltx_note_outer\"><span class=\"ltx_note_content\"><sup class=\"ltx_note_mark\">1</sup>\n          <span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_note\">1</span>\n          \n          \n          \n          \n          \n          \n          \n        <a href=\"https://github.com/multi-agent-systems-failure-taxonomy/MAST\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter\">https://github.com/multi-agent-systems-failure-taxonomy/MAST</a></span></span></span><span id=\"footnote2\" class=\"ltx_note ltx_role_footnote\"><sup class=\"ltx_note_mark\">2</sup><span class=\"ltx_note_outer\"><span class=\"ltx_note_content\"><sup class=\"ltx_note_mark\">2</sup>\n          <span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_note\">2</span>\n          \n          \n          \n          \n          \n          \n          \n        <a href=\"https://huggingface.co/datasets/mcemri/MAST-Data\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter\">https://huggingface.co/datasets/mcemri/MAST-Data</a></span></span></span></p>\n  \n</div>\n<div id=\"p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_italic\" style=\"font-size:90%;\">“Happy families are all alike; each unhappy family is unhappy in its own way.”<span id=\"p1.1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_upright\"> (<cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet\"><a href=\"#bib.bib1\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">Tolstoy [1]</a></cite>) \n<br class=\"ltx_break\"></span>“Successful systems all work alike; each failing system has its own problems.”<span id=\"p1.1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_upright\"> (Berkeley’25)\n</span></span></p>\n</div>\n<figure id=\"S0.F1\" class=\"ltx_figure\"><object type=\"image/svg+xml\" data=\"2503.13657v3/taxonomy_neurips_final_10_23_25.svg\" id=\"S0.F1.g1\" class=\"ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape\" style=\"aspect-ratio:476/244;\" width=\"476\" height=\"244\"></object>\n<figcaption class=\"ltx_caption ltx_centering\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure\">Figure 1: </span><span id=\"S0.F1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST</span>: A <span id=\"S0.F1.5\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Taxonomy of MAS Failure Modes</span>. The inter-agent conversation stages indicate when a failure typically occurs within the end-to-end MAS execution pipeline. A failure mode spanning multiple stages signifies that the underlying issue can manifest or have implications across these different phases of operation. The percentages shown represent the prevalence of each failure mode and category as observed in our analysis of 1642 MAS execution traces. Detailed definitions for each failure mode and illustrative examples are available in Appendix <a href=\"#A1\" title=\"Appendix A MAST Failure Categories: Deep Dive ‣ Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">A</span></a>.</figcaption>\n</figure>\n<section id=\"S1\" class=\"ltx_section\">\n<h2 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_section\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_section\">1 </span>Introduction</h2>\n\n<div id=\"S1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Recently, Large Language Model (LLM) based agentic systems have gained significant attention in the AI community <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib2\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">2</a>, <a href=\"#bib.bib3\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">3</a>, <a href=\"#bib.bib4\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">4</a>]</cite>.\nBuilding on this characteristic, multi-agent systems are increasingly explored in various domains, such as software engineering, drug discoveries, scientific simulations, and general-purpose agents <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib5\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">5</a>, <a href=\"#bib.bib6\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">6</a>, <a href=\"#bib.bib7\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">7</a>, <a href=\"#bib.bib8\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">8</a>, <a href=\"#bib.bib9\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">9</a>, <a href=\"#bib.bib10\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">10</a>, <a href=\"#bib.bib11\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">11</a>]</cite>.\nIn this study, we define an LLM-based <span id=\"S1.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">agent</span> as an artificial entity with prompt specifications (initial state), conversation trace (state), and ability to interact with the environments such as tool usage (action).\nA <span id=\"S1.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">multi-agent system</span> (<span id=\"S1.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">MAS</span>) is then defined as a collection of agents designed to interact through orchestration, enabling collective intelligence.\nMAS are structured to coordinate efforts, enabling task decomposition, performance parallelization, context isolation, specialized model ensembling, and diverse reasoning discussions <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib12\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">12</a>, <a href=\"#bib.bib13\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">13</a>, <a href=\"#bib.bib14\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">14</a>, <a href=\"#bib.bib15\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">15</a>, <a href=\"#bib.bib16\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">16</a>, <a href=\"#bib.bib17\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">17</a>]</cite>.</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S1.p2\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S1.p2.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Despite the increasing adoption of MAS, their performance gains often remain minimal compared to single-agent frameworks <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib18\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">18</a>]</cite> or simple baselines like best-of-N sampling <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib19\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">19</a>]</cite>.\nOur empirical analysis reveals 41% to 86.7% failure rate on 7 state-of-the-art (SOTA) open-source MAS detailed in Figure <a href=\"#A2.F5\" title=\"Figure 5 ‣ Appendix B Details of Multi-Agent Systems Evaluated ‣ Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">5</span></a> (Appendix <a href=\"#A2\" title=\"Appendix B Details of Multi-Agent Systems Evaluated ‣ Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">B</span></a>).\nFurthermore, there is no clear consensus on how to build robust and reliable MAS.\nThis motivates the fundamental question we address: <span id=\"S1.p2.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_italic\">Why do MAS fail?</span></p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S1.p3\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S1.p3.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">To address this question and systematically understand MAS failures, we introduce <span id=\"S1.p3.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST-Data</span>, a comprehensive, high-quality collection of 1642 annotated execution traces. We define failures as instances where the MAS does not achieve its intended task objectives. As shown in Table <a href=\"#S1.T1\" title=\"Table 1 ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">1</span></a>, we collect traces from 7 popular MAS frameworks run with two main model families (GPT-4 series and Claude series), covering tasks such as coding, math problem-solving, and general agent functionalities. Alongside <span id=\"S1.p3.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST-Data</span>, we also release <span id=\"S1.p3.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST-Data-human</span>, a smaller dataset featuring 21 traces annotated by three human experts each during our inter-annotator agreement studies. We create <span id=\"S1.p3.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST-Data</span> to outline failure dynamics in MAS and to guide the development of better future systems.</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S1.p4\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S1.p4.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Systematically annotating failures in diverse MAS for a large-scale dataset like <span id=\"S1.p4.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST-Data</span> presents challenges unique to MAS: the difficulty in verifying ground truth for root cause detection and the absence of standardized failure definitions. To mitigate these challenges in creating <span id=\"S1.p4.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST-Data</span>, we first develop the <span id=\"S1.p4.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">M</span>ulti-<span id=\"S1.p4.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">A</span>gent <span id=\"S1.p4.1.5\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">S</span>ystem Failure <span id=\"S1.p4.1.6\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">T</span>axonomy (<span id=\"S1.p4.1.7\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST</span>), illustrated in Figure <a href=\"#S0.F1\" title=\"Figure 1 ‣ Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">1</span></a>. We build <span id=\"S1.p4.1.8\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST</span> using Grounded Theory <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib20\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">20</a>]</cite> from a close analysis of over 150 MAS execution traces (each averaging over 15,000 lines of text). This analysis spans a subset of five open-source MAS frameworks and involves six expert human annotators. To ensure generalizable definitions in <span id=\"S1.p4.1.9\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST</span> for labeling <span id=\"S1.p4.1.10\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST-Data</span>, three annotators independently and iteratively labeled a total of 15 traces until achieving high inter-annotator agreement (<math id=\"S1.p4.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\kappa\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\kappa</annotation></semantics></math> = 0.88). This comprehensive analysis results in 14 distinct failure modes, clustered into 3 categories. While <span id=\"S1.p4.1.11\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST</span> serves as a foundational first step towards unifying the understanding of MAS failures, we do not claim it covers every potential failure pattern. To enable scalable annotation for the full <span id=\"S1.p4.1.12\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST-Data</span>, we then develop an LLM-as-a-judge pipeline (which we term the LLM annotator) <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib21\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">21</a>]</cite> using OpenAI’s o1 model. We calibrate the LLM annotator to achieve high agreement with human expert annotations (<math id=\"S1.p4.m2\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\kappa\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\kappa</annotation></semantics></math> = 0.77), and additionally validated applicability on two additional unseen MAS and benchmarks (<math id=\"S1.p4.m3\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\kappa\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\kappa</annotation></semantics></math> = 0.79).</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S1.p5\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S1.p5.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">To demonstrate <span id=\"S1.p5.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST</span>’s practical usage, our case studies (Appendix <a href=\"#A8\" title=\"Appendix H Intervention Case Studies ‣ Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">H</span></a>) highlight its role in guiding MAS development, and in Section <a href=\"#A3\" title=\"Appendix C MAST Python Library ‣ Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">C</span></a> we describe how to use the <span id=\"S1.p5.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST</span> easily as a python library using <code id=\"S1.p5.1.3\" class=\"ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter\">pip install agentdash</code>. For example, the CPO agent in ChatDev can exhibit ‘Failure Mode 1.2 - Disobey Role Specification’ by terminating conversation without the CEO agent’s consensus. We demonstrate that a straightforward system workflow adjustment ensuring the CEO had the final say contributed to a +9.4% increase in overall task success rate. While such <span id=\"S1.p5.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST</span>-guided interventions demonstrate improvements, achieving robust MAS reliability often requires more than isolated fixes, pointing towards the need for more complex solutions and fundamental MAS redesigns.</p>\n</div>\n<figure id=\"S1.T1\" class=\"ltx_table\">\n<figcaption class=\"ltx_caption ltx_centering\" style=\"font-size:90%;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_table\">Table 1: </span><span id=\"S1.T1.5\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST-Data</span> configuration details. HE: Human Evaluated (Task completions rates are checked by humans), HA: Human Annotated (Failure modes are annotated by humans), LA: LLM Annotated (Failure modes are annotated by LLM-as-a-Judge).</figcaption>\n<table id=\"S1.T1.6\" class=\"ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_align_middle\">\n<tr id=\"S1.T1.6.1\" class=\"ltx_tr\">\n<td id=\"S1.T1.6.1.1\" class=\"ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_tt\" style=\"padding:1.4pt 3.0pt;\">\n<span id=\"S1.T1.6.1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top\" style=\"width:71.1pt;\">\n<span id=\"S1.T1.6.1.1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S1.T1.6.1.1.1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\" style=\"font-size:90%;\">MAS</span></span>\n</span></td>\n<td id=\"S1.T1.6.1.2\" class=\"ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_tt\" style=\"padding:1.4pt 3.0pt;\">\n<span id=\"S1.T1.6.1.2.1\" class=\"ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top\" style=\"width:71.1pt;\">\n<span id=\"S1.T1.6.1.2.1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S1.T1.6.1.2.1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\" style=\"font-size:90%;\">Benchmark</span></span>\n</span></td>\n<td id=\"S1.T1.6.1.3\" class=\"ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_tt\" style=\"padding:1.4pt 3.0pt;\">\n<span id=\"S1.T1.6.1.3.1\" class=\"ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top\" style=\"width:113.8pt;\">\n<span id=\"S1.T1.6.1.3.1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S1.T1.6.1.3.1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\" style=\"font-size:90%;\">LLM</span></span>\n</span></td>\n<td id=\"S1.T1.6.1.4\" class=\"ltx_td ltx_align_left style=\"width:71.1pt;\">\n<span id=\"S1.T1.6.18.2.1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S1.T1.6.18.2.1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text\" style=\"font-size:90%;\">MMLU</span></span>\n</span></td>\n<td id=\"S1.T1.6.18.3\" class=\"ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_t\" style=\"padding:1.4pt 3.0pt;\">\n<span id=\"S1.T1.6.18.3.1\" class=\"ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top\" style=\"width:113.8pt;\">\n<span id=\"S1.T1.6.18.3.1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S1.T1.6.18.3.1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text\" style=\"font-size:90%;\">GPT-4o-mini</span></span>\n</span></td>\n<td id=\"S1.T1.6.18.4\" class=\"ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_t\" style=\"padding:1.4pt 3.0pt;\">\n<span id=\"S1.T1.6.18.4.1\" class=\"ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top\" style=\"width:56.9pt;\">\n<span id=\"S1.T1.6.18.4.1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S1.T1.6.18.4.1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text\" style=\"font-size:90%;\">HE, LA</span></span>\n</span></td>\n<td id=\"S1.T1.6.18.5\" class=\"ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_t\" style=\"padding:1.4pt 3.0pt;\">\n<span id=\"S1.T1.6.18.5.1\" class=\"ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top\" style=\"width:28.5pt;\">\n<span id=\"S1.T1.6.18.5.1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S1.T1.6.18.5.1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text\" style=\"font-size:90%;\">168</span></span>\n</span></td></tr>\n<tr id=\"S1.T1.6.19\" class=\"ltx_tr\">\n<td id=\"S1.T1.6.19.1\" class=\"ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_b ltx_border_t\" style=\"padding:1.4pt 3.0pt;\">\n<span id=\"S1.T1.6.19.1.1\" class=\"ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top\" style=\"width:71.1pt;\">\n<span id=\"S1.T1.6.19.1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S1.T1.6.19.1.1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text\" style=\"font-size:90%;\">Magentic-One</span></span>\n</span></td>\n<td id=\"S1.T1.6.19.2\" class=\"ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_b ltx_border_t\" style=\"padding:1.4pt 3.0pt;\">\n<span id=\"S1.T1.6.19.2.1\" class=\"ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top\" style=\"width:71.1pt;\">\n<span id=\"S1.T1.6.19.2.1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S1.T1.6.19.2.1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text\" style=\"font-size:90%;\">GAIA</span></span>\n</span></td>\n<td id=\"S1.T1.6.19.3\" class=\"ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_b ltx_border_t\" style=\"padding:1.4pt class=\"ltx_text\" style=\"font-size:90%;\">GPT-4o</span></span>\n</span></td>\n<td id=\"S1.T1.6.19.4\" class=\"ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_b ltx_border_t\" style=\"padding:1.4pt class=\"ltx_text\" style=\"font-size:90%;\">HE, LA</span></span>\n</span></td>\n<td id=\"S1.T1.6.19.5\" class=\"ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_b ltx_border_t\" style=\"padding:1.4pt 3.0pt;\">\n<span id=\"S1.T1.6.19.5.1\" class=\"ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top\" style=\"width:28.5pt;\">\n<span id=\"S1.T1.6.19.5.1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S1.T1.6.19.5.1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text\" style=\"font-size:90%;\">165</span></span>\n</span></td></tr>\n</table>\n</figure>\n<div id=\"S1.p6\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S1.p6.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">These findings suggest <span id=\"S1.p6.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST</span> reflects fundamental design challenges inherent in current MAS, not just artifacts of specific MAS implementation. By systematically defining failures, <span id=\"S1.p6.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST</span> serves as a framework to guide failure diagnosis and opens concrete research problems for the community.\nWe have released our traces and annotations and open-sourced the LLM annotator pipeline to foster research in the design of more robust and reliable MAS.</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S1.p7\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S1.p7.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">The contributions of this paper are as follows:</p>\n<ul id=\"S1.I1\" class=\"ltx_itemize ltx_leftmargin_flush\">\n<li id=\"S1.I1.i1\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\">•</span> \n<div id=\"S1.I1.i1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S1.I1.i1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">We introduce and <span id=\"S1.I1.i1.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">open-source</span> <span id=\"S1.I1.i1.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST-Data</span>, the first large-scale MAS failure dataset with consistent annotations from 7 MAS and four model families. And <span id=\"S1.I1.i1.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST-Data-human</span>, a detailed inter-annotator study results with human labels. Together serve to facilitate research into MAS failures.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"S1.I1.i2\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\">•</span> \n<div id=\"S1.I1.i2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S1.I1.i2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">We introduce <span id=\"S1.I1.i2.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST</span>, the first empirically grounded <span id=\"S1.I1.i2.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">taxonomy of MAS failures</span>, providing a structured framework for defining, understanding and annotating failures.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"S1.I1.i3\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\">•</span> \n<div id=\"S1.I1.i3.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S1.I1.i3.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">We develop a scalable LLM-as-a-judge <span id=\"S1.I1.i3.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">annotation pipeline</span> integrated with <span id=\"S1.I1.i3.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST</span> for efficiently annotating <span id=\"S1.I1.i3.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST-Data</span> and enabling analysis of MAS performance, diagnosis of failure modes, and understanding of failure breakdowns.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"S1.I1.i4\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\">•</span> \n<div id=\"S1.I1.i4.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S1.I1.i4.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">We demonstrate through <span id=\"S1.I1.i4.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">case studies</span> that failures identified by <span id=\"S1.I1.i4.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST</span> often stem from system design issues, not just LLM limitations or simple prompt following, and require more than superficial fixes, thereby highlighting the need for structural MAS redesigns.</p>\n</div></li>\n</ul>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2\" class=\"ltx_section\">\n<h2 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_section\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_section\">2 </span>Related Work</h2>\n\n<section id=\"S2.SS1\" class=\"ltx_subsection\">\n<h3 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_subsection\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection\">2.1 </span>Challenges in Agentic Systems</h3>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">The promising capabilities of agentic systems have inspired research into solving specific challenges. For instance, Agent Workflow Memory <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib22\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">22</a>]</cite> addresses long-horizon web navigation by introducing workflow memory. DSPy <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib23\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">23</a>]</cite> tackles issues in programming agentic flows, while StateFlow <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib24\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">24</a>]</cite> focuses on state control within agentic workflows to improve task-solving capabilities. Several surveys also highlight challenges and potential risks specifically within MAS <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib25\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">25</a>, <a href=\"#bib.bib26\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">26</a>]</cite>. While these works meaningfully contribute towards understanding specific issues or providing high-level overviews, they do not offer a fine-grained, empirically grounded taxonomy of <span id=\"S2.SS1.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_italic\">why</span> MAS fail across diverse systems and tasks. Numerous benchmarks also exist to evaluate agentic systems <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib27\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">27</a>, <a href=\"#bib.bib28\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">28</a>, <a href=\"#bib.bib29\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">29</a>, <a href=\"#bib.bib30\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">30</a>, <a href=\"#bib.bib31\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">31</a>, <a href=\"#bib.bib32\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">32</a>]</cite>. These evaluations are crucial but primarily facilitate a top-down perspective, focusing on aggregate performance or high-level objectives like trustworthiness and security <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib33\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">33</a>, <a href=\"#bib.bib34\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">34</a>]</cite>. Our work complements these efforts by providing a bottom-up analysis focused on identifying specific failure modes in MAS.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS2\" class=\"ltx_subsection\">\n<h3 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_subsection\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection\">2.2 </span>Design Principles for Agentic Systems</h3>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Several works highlight challenges in building robust agentic systems and suggest design principles, often focused on single-agent settings. For instance, Anthropic’s blog post emphasizes modular components and avoiding overly complex frameworks <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib35\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">35</a>]</cite>. Similarly, <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet\"><a href=\"#bib.bib19\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">Kapoor et al. [19]</a></cite> demonstrates how complexity can hinder practical adoption. Our work extends these insights to the multi-agent context. By systematically collecting and analyzing a large corpus of MAS failure instances within <span id=\"S2.SS2.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST-Data</span>, and by developing <span id=\"S2.SS2.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST</span>, we provide not only a structured understanding of <span id=\"S2.SS2.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_italic\">why</span> MAS fail but also empirical data from <span id=\"S2.SS2.p1.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST-Data</span> to support the development and validation of more robust design principles for MAS. This aligns with the call for clearer specifications and design principles <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib36\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">36</a>]</cite>.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS3\" class=\"ltx_subsection\">\n<h3 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_subsection\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection\">2.3 </span>Related Datasets and Taxonomy</h3>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Despite the growing interest in LLM agents, dedicated research systematically characterizing their failure modes remains limited, particularly for MAS. While <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet\"><a href=\"#bib.bib37\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">Bansal et al. [37]</a></cite> catalogs challenges in human-agent interaction, our contribution focuses specifically on failures within autonomous MAS execution. Other related work includes taxonomies for evaluating multi-turn LLM conversations <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib38\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">38</a>]</cite> or specific capabilities like code generation <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib39\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">39</a>]</cite>. These differ significantly from our goal of developing a generalizable failure taxonomy for multi-agent interactions and coordination.</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.p2\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.p2.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Further related efforts aim to improve MAS through different approaches. AgentEval <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib40\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">40</a>]</cite> proposes a framework using LLM agents to define and quantify multi-dimensional evaluation criteria reflecting task utility for end-users. AGDebugger <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib41\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">41</a>]</cite> introduces an interactive tool enabling developers to debug and steer agent teams by inspecting and editing message histories. And currentwork by <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet\"><a href=\"#bib.bib42\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">Zhang et al. [42]</a></cite> present the Who&amp;When dataset and MAS debugger, which focuses on summarizing failures for specific task items by attributing them to particular agents and error steps.</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.p3\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.p3.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Thus, <span id=\"S2.SS3.p3.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST-Data</span> and <span id=\"S2.SS3.p3.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST</span> represent, to our knowledge, the first empirically derived, comprehensive dataset and taxonomy focused specifically on MAS failures focus on failure patterns. Identifying these patterns highlights the need for continued research into robust evaluation metrics and mitigation strategies tailored for the unique challenges of MAS.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S3\" class=\"ltx_section\">\n<h2 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_section\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_section\">3 </span>The Multi-Agent Systems Dataset</h2>\n\n<figure id=\"S3.F2\" class=\"ltx_figure\"><img src=\"2503.13657v3/arxiv_figure_neurips_cropped.png\" id=\"S3.F2.g1\" class=\"ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape\" style=\"aspect-ratio:476/102;\" width=\"476\" height=\"102\" alt=\"Refer to caption\">\n<figcaption class=\"ltx_caption ltx_centering\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure\">Figure 2: </span>Methodological workflow for constructing the <span id=\"S3.F2.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST-Data</span> dataset, involving the empirical identification of failure modes, the development of <span id=\"S3.F2.5\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST</span>, iterative refinement through inter-annotator agreement studies (<math id=\"S3.F2.m2\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\kappa=0.88{}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.88</mn></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\kappa=0.88{}</annotation></semantics></math>), and the creation of a scalable LLM annotation pipeline. This figure highlights our systematic approach to creating a comprehensive dataset for studying MAS failures.</figcaption>\n</figure>\n<div id=\"S3.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S3.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">To facilitate a principled understanding of why MAS fail and to guide the development of more reliable future systems, we introduce <span id=\"S3.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST-Data</span>, the Multi-Agent System Failure Dataset. <span id=\"S3.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST-Data</span> is a comprehensive, empirically grounded dataset comprising 1642 annotated execution traces collected from 7 popular MAS frameworks, covering domains of coding, math, and generic tasks.</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S3.p2\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S3.p2.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Constructing such a dataset, however, presents distinct challenges. First, unlike in traditional software where failures often have clearly identifiable root causes, failures in MAS are frequently complex. They involve convoluted agent interactions and the compounding effects of individual model behaviors and overall system design. Therefore, pinpointing the precise nature and origin of a failure in MAS requires more than simple error detection; it necessitates understanding the system’s dynamics. Second, the lack of a standardized failure framework with clear definitions makes identifying and classifying MAS failures across different systems inconsistent, which complicates annotation and cross-system analysis.</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S3.p3\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S3.p3.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">To address these challenges, we develop a rigorous, principled methodology to construct <span id=\"S3.p3.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST-Data</span>. In this section, we detail our approach, which centers on building the first empirical MAS failure taxonomy, <span id=\"S3.p3.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST</span>, and a scalable annotation pipeline for systematic and comprehensive data collection. Figure <a href=\"#S3.F2\" title=\"Figure 2 ‣ 3 The Multi-Agent Systems Dataset ‣ Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2</span></a> summarizes our methodological workflow.</p>\n</div>\n<section id=\"S3.SS1\" class=\"ltx_subsection\">\n<h3 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_subsection\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection\">3.1 </span>Data Collection with Grounded Theory Analysis</h3>\n\n<div id=\"S3.SS1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S3.SS1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">To uncover a comprehensive set of failure patterns that are both diverse and generalizable to standardize failure labels which we detail further in Section <a href=\"#S3.SS2\" title=\"3.2 Standardizing Failure Labels via Inter-Annotator Agreement ‣ 3 The Multi-Agent Systems Dataset ‣ Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">3.2</span></a>, we first collect 150 traces from five MAS frameworks, which are closely examined by six human experts. Our goal at this stage is to identify as many distinct failure modes as possible, ensuring these observed patterns are not merely artifacts of a single system but can likely apply more broadly. To achieve this without predefined hypotheses, we adopt the <span id=\"S3.SS1.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Grounded Theory</span> (GT) approach <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib20\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">20</a>]</cite>. This qualitative research method allows failure modes to emerge organically from empirical data.</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S3.SS1.p2\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S3.SS1.p2.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">For this initial data collection, we use <em id=\"S3.SS1.p2.1.1\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">theoretical sampling</em> <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib43\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">43</a>]</cite> to ensure robust coverage across different system objectives and interaction patterns. This method guides our selection of the five MAS frameworks (HyperAgent, AppWorld, AG2, ChatDev, and MetaGPT) and two task categories (programming and math problem-solving). We then iteratively analyze these traces using core GT techniques: <em id=\"S3.SS1.p2.1.2\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">open coding</em> <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib44\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">44</a>]</cite> to label trace data with observed failure behaviors; <em id=\"S3.SS1.p2.1.3\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">constant comparative analysis</em> to refine our understanding of these failure behaviors and their recurrence across systems; <em id=\"S3.SS1.p2.1.4\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">memoing</em> to document insights; and <em id=\"S3.SS1.p2.1.5\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">theorizing</em> to structure these findings into an initial set of failure modes with their definitions. This iterative analysis continues until we reach <em id=\"S3.SS1.p2.1.6\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">theoretical saturation</em>, where further data analysis does not yield new failure mode insights. This initial process requires significant human effort, over 20 hours of annotation per expert for these 150 traces.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S3.SS2\" class=\"ltx_subsection\">\n<h3 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_subsection\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection\">3.2 </span>Standardizing Failure Labels via Inter-Annotator Agreement</h3>\n\n<div id=\"S3.SS2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S3.SS2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">To make the failure observations from our GT analysis useful for creating consistent labels in <span id=\"S3.SS2.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST-Data</span>, we recognize the critical need for standardized definitions that apply uniformly across different MAS. To address this, we develop the failure taxonomy - <span id=\"S3.SS2.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST</span>. <span id=\"S3.SS2.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST</span> serves as a foundational first step towards a common understanding of MAS failures by providing clear, empirically grounded failure observation labels. We provide a detailed description and analysis of <span id=\"S3.SS2.p1.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST</span> in Section <a href=\"#S4\" title=\"4 The Multi-Agent System Failure Taxonomy ‣ Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">4</span></a>.</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S3.SS2.p2\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S3.SS2.p2.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">To develop a taxonomy that is unambiguous and consistently applicable by different annotators, we rigorously validate and refine <span id=\"S3.SS2.p2.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST</span> definitions through Inter-Annotator Agreement (IAA) studies. This iterative process begins with a preliminary version of <span id=\"S3.SS2.p2.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST</span> derived from our GT findings. In each round of IAA, three expert annotators independently label a subset of five randomly selected traces from our initial 150+ trace collection using <span id=\"S3.SS2.p2.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST</span>. We then facilitate discussions to collectively resolve any disagreements. Based on these discussions, we iteratively refine <span id=\"S3.SS2.p2.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST</span> by adjusting failure mode definitions, adding new modes, or removing and merging existing ones until we achieve high consensus. We conduct three such rounds of IAA, requiring about 10 hours in total solely for resolving disagreements, not including the annotation time itself. We measure agreement using Cohen’s Kappa score, achieving a strong average of <math id=\"S3.SS2.p2.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\kappa=0.88{}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.88</mn></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\kappa=0.88{}</annotation></semantics></math> in the final rounds. This high IAA score signifies that <span id=\"S3.SS2.p2.1.5\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST</span> provides a clear and shared understanding of failure modes, crucial for the consistent annotation of <span id=\"S3.SS2.p2.1.6\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST-Data</span>. Figure <a href=\"#S3.F3\" title=\"Figure 3 ‣ 3.3 Enabling Scalable Annotation: The LLM-as-a-Judge Pipeline ‣ 3 The Multi-Agent Systems Dataset ‣ Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">3</span></a> illustrates an example of a trace snippet with a <span id=\"S3.SS2.p2.1.7\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST</span> label.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S3.SS3\" class=\"ltx_subsection\">\n<h3 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_subsection\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection\">3.3 </span>Enabling Scalable Annotation: The LLM-as-a-Judge Pipeline</h3>\n\n<div id=\"S3.SS3.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S3.SS3.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Manually annotating over 1600 MAS traces with fine-grained failure modes is time-consuming and costly. To enable scalable and automated failure annotation for <span id=\"S3.SS3.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST-Data</span>, we develop an LLM-as-a-Judge pipeline (LLM annotator), building upon our validated <span id=\"S3.SS3.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST</span>. This pipeline prompts an LLM (OpenAI’s o1 model) with an execution trace, the <span id=\"S3.SS3.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST</span> definitions, and few-shot examples from our human-annotated data (details in Appendix <a href=\"#A14\" title=\"Appendix N Examples of Different Failure Modes ‣ Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">N</span></a>) to classify observed failure modes. We validate the LLM annotator’s reliability against expert human annotations on a held-out set from our IAA studies. The LLM annotator achieves high agreement with human experts (accuracy 94%, Cohen’s Kappa of 0.77; Table <a href=\"#S3.T2\" title=\"Table 2 ‣ 3.3 Enabling Scalable Annotation: The LLM-as-a-Judge Pipeline ‣ 3 The Multi-Agent Systems Dataset ‣ Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2</span></a>), confirming its suitability for scaling the annotation process while adhering to <span id=\"S3.SS3.p1.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold\">MAST</span> definitions.</p>\n</div>\n<figure id=\"S3.T2\" class=\"ltx_table\">\n<figcaption class=\"ltx_caption ltx_centering\" style=\"font-size:90%;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_table\">Table 2: </span>Performance of LLM-as-a-judge
