Operations ‣ 2.4 Tool System ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Sections</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.4.2</span></a> and <a href=\"#S2.SS4.SSS5\" title=\"2.4.5 Multi-Language Semantic Code Analysis via LSP ‣ 2.4 Tool System ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.4.5</span></a>). The central design question is not what tools to provide, but how the agent selects among them. A naive agent defaults to text search for every lookup, a failure mode analogous to the “retrieve-everything” antipattern in traditional RAG <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib5\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">5</a>]</cite>. Effective retrieval instead begins by identifying the <em id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.Px1.p1.1.6\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">strongest anchor</em> in the query: the most specific, highest-signal element that constrains the search space. Symbol names (e.g., <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.Px1.p1.1.7\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">AuthController.validate</span>) route to <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.Px1.p1.1.8\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">find_symbol</span>, which resolves the definition semantically via LSP; string literals and error messages route to <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.Px1.p1.1.9\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">text_search</span>, which performs exact pattern matching; structural patterns (e.g., “all Python if-statements that check <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.Px1.p1.1.10\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">is_admin</span>”) route to <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.Px1.p1.1.11\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">ast_search</span>, which matches language-aware templates; and file-path conventions route to <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.Px1.p1.1.12\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">list_files</span> for glob-based discovery. By matching the retrieval tool to the anchor type, the agent avoids noisy, low-precision searches and reaches the relevant code in fewer steps. This is the coding-agent analog of Self-Ask’s <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib70\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">70</a>]</cite> decomposition strategy: rather than searching with the raw user query, the agent reasons about what kind of information it needs and selects the retrieval mechanism accordingly.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.Px2\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Layer 2: Multi-step agentic search via the Code Explorer.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.Px2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.Px2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Single-tool retrieval suffices when the agent knows exactly what to look for, but many tasks require <em id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.Px2.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">exploratory</em> retrieval: the agent must follow cross-references, discover unexpected dependencies, and iteratively narrow a broad search space. This is where the system transitions from static tool invocation to the interleaved reasoning-and-retrieval loop characteristic of agentic search <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib99\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">99</a>, <a href=\"#bib.bib80\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">80</a>]</cite>. When the main agent needs broad codebase understanding rather than a pinpoint lookup, it delegates to the Code Explorer subagent (<a href=\"#S2.SS2.SSS7\" title=\"2.2.7 Subagent Orchestration ‣ 2.2 Agent Core Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Sections</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.2.7</span></a> and <a href=\"#S2.SS4.SSS8\" title=\"2.4.8 Subagent Delegation, Skills, and Batch Execution ‣ 2.4 Tool System ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.4.8</span></a>), which runs in an isolated context window with access to the same five retrieval tools in read-only mode. The subagent performs multi-step searches autonomously: it might start with <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.Px2.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">find_symbol</span> to locate a class definition, read the file to discover its dependencies, then use <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.Px2.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">text_search</span> to trace how those dependencies are used across the project. Each step is guided by the subagent’s own reasoning about what it has found so far and what it still needs, embodying the “interleaving retrieval with chain-of-thought” pattern <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib80\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">80</a>]</cite>. Context isolation is critical: intermediate search results (potentially thousands of lines of code) stay in the subagent’s window, and only the distilled summary is returned to the main agent. This prevents the retrieval process itself from consuming the context budget that the main agent needs for reasoning and action.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.Px3\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Layer 3: Context assembly.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.Px3.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.Px3.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Retrieved code artifacts alone are insufficient; the agent also needs its behavioral instructions, accumulated experience, and conversation history. Before each model call, <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.Px3.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">ContextPicker</span> assembles the final message list from six ordered sources: (1) the system prompt augmented with selected playbook strategies from the adaptive memory (<a href=\"#S2.SS3.SSS6\" title=\"2.3.6 Adaptive Context Compaction ‣ 2.3 Context Engineering Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.3.6</span></a>), (2) project-level and user-level persistent rules, (3) inline <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.Px3.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">@file</span> references and image blocks supplied by the user, (4) the conversation history retrieved from <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.Px3.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">SessionManager</span>, (5) system reminders injected at the point of decision (<a href=\"#S2.SS3.SSS4\" title=\"2.3.4 Context-Aware System Reminders ‣ 2.3 Context Engineering Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.3.4</span></a>), and (6) the current user query. Each piece of context is wrapped in a <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.Px3.p1.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">ContextPiece</span> that tracks its provenance (source subsystem, priority, token cost), enabling downstream components to make informed retention decisions when the budget is tight. The assembled structure is validated by <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.Px3.p1.1.5\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">ValidatedMessageList</span>, which enforces structural integrity (every <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.Px3.p1.1.6\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">assistant</span> message with tool calls must be followed by matching tool results before the next user turn) and auto-repairs violations with synthetic error placeholders rather than failing outright.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.Px4\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Layer 4: Context optimization.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.Px4.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.Px4.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">The assembled context passes through the staged compaction pipeline described in <a href=\"#S2.SS3.SSS6\" title=\"2.3.6 Adaptive Context Compaction ‣ 2.3 Context Engineering Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.3.6</span></a>. Observations follow a lifecycle from <em id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.Px4.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">active</em> (recent, fully retained) through <em id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.Px4.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">faded</em> (eligible for masking after the 80% threshold) to <em id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.Px4.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">archived</em> (serialized to disk and replaced with a reference). Token budgets are calibrated against API-reported <span id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.Px4.p1.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">prompt_tokens</span> from the previous turn rather than local estimates, correcting for provider-side injections (safety preambles, tool schemas) that are invisible to the client. This final optimization step ensures that regardless of how much context was retrieved and assembled, the payload submitted to the LLM respects the model’s context window while preserving the most decision-relevant material.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.Px5\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">End-to-end flow.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.Px5.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.Px5.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">The four layers form a retrieval pipeline that mirrors the escalation pattern seen in agentic search systems <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib88\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">88</a>]</cite>: simple queries resolve at Layer 1 with a single tool call; complex queries escalate to Layer 2’s multi-step search; all results converge at Layer 3’s assembly; and Layer 4 enforces the token budget. This progressive escalation means that straightforward lookups (“read file X”) incur minimal overhead, while open-ended exploration (“how does the authentication system work?”) can leverage the full agentic search loop without the cost bleeding into the main agent’s context.</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.Px5.p2\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.Px5.p2.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">The context engineering layer shapes what the model sees; the tool system defines what the model can <em id=\"S2.SS3.SSS7.Px5.p2.1.1\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">do</em>: the concrete actions through which the agent modifies code, runs commands, and interacts with the development environment.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n</section>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS4\" class=\"ltx_subsection\">\n<h3 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_subsection\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection\">2.4 </span>Tool System</h3>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">The tools through which the agent interacts with the development environment form an extensible ecosystem that balances comprehensive capability with context efficiency, safety with flexibility, and built-in tools with dynamic discovery. <a href=\"#A1.T1\" title=\"In Appendix A Complete Tool Catalog ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Table</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">1</span></a> in <a href=\"#A1\" title=\"Appendix A Complete Tool Catalog ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Appendix</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">A</span></a> provides a complete catalog of all 35 built-in tools; the remainder of this section describes the registry architecture that organizes them into handler categories, then details each category: file operations, shell execution, web interaction, semantic code analysis via LSP, user interaction and task management, external tool discovery via MCP, and subagent delegation. A defense-in-depth safety architecture spans all categories.</p>\n</div>\n<section id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1\" class=\"ltx_subsubsection\">\n<h4 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection\">2.4.1 </span>Registry Architecture and Schema Construction</h4>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">A flat namespace of tools becomes unmanageable as capabilities grow: hard-coded dispatch logic is inflexible, and dynamic plugin loading without structure is unsafe. Alternatives range from hardcoded tool sets (simple but cannot add capabilities without code changes) to flat dynamic loading (flexible but chaotic, leading to namespace collisions, lack of organization, and difficult safety management). <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps\">OpenDev</span> adopts a registry with handler categories, organizing tools into handler classes with schema-based registration.</p>\n</div>\n<section id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px1\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Three separated concerns.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><a href=\"#S2.F16\" title=\"In Three separated concerns. ‣ 2.4.1 Registry Architecture and Schema Construction ‣ 2.4 Tool System ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Figure</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">16</span></a> illustrates the architecture. The tool system separates schema construction, dispatch routing, and lifecycle hooks into distinct components.</p>\n</div>\n<figure id=\"S2.F16\" class=\"ltx_figure\"><img src=\"2603.05344v3/tool_system.png\" id=\"S2.F16.g1\" class=\"ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape\" style=\"aspect-ratio:648/319;\" width=\"648\" height=\"319\" alt=\"Refer to caption\">\n<figcaption class=\"ltx_caption ltx_centering\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure\">Figure 16: </span>Expanded view of the Tool layer from <a href=\"#S2.F2\" title=\"In 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Figure</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2</span></a>. <span id=\"S2.F16.5\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">ToolSchemaBuilder</span> assembles JSON schemas from three sources (static built-in definitions, dynamically discovered MCP tools, subagent schemas) and injects them into the LLM prompt. <span id=\"S2.F16.6\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">ToolRegistry</span> dispatches tool calls to category-based handlers, each receiving a <span id=\"S2.F16.7\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">ToolExecutionContext</span> with cross-cutting services. Pre/post lifecycle hooks intercept calls for safety enforcement and extensibility.</figcaption>\n</figure>\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p2\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p2.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p2.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">ToolSchemaBuilder</span> assembles JSON schemas from three sources: (1) static <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p2.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">_BUILTIN_TOOL_SCHEMAS</span> defining approximately 40 built-in tools, with descriptions loaded from markdown templates via <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p2.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">load_tool_description()</span>; (2) dynamically discovered MCP schemas, including only those tools in the <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p2.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">_discovered_mcp_tools</span> set to avoid context bloat; and (3) subagent schemas injected by the <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p2.1.5\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">SubAgentManager</span> when present. The assembled schemas are injected into the LLM prompt, giving the model awareness of available capabilities.</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p3\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p3.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p3.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">ToolRegistry</span> serves as the central dispatcher, mapping tool names to handler methods across 12 handler classes organized by category (file, process, web, notebook, user interaction, task management, thinking, MCP discovery, batch execution; see <a href=\"#A1.T1\" title=\"In Appendix A Complete Tool Catalog ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Table</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">1</span></a> in <a href=\"#A1\" title=\"Appendix A Complete Tool Catalog ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Appendix</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">A</span></a> for the complete mapping). Each handler receives a <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p3.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">ToolExecutionContext</span> that bundles cross-cutting services: mode manager, approval manager, undo manager, task monitor, session manager, UI callback, and file-time tracker. The registry enforces mode restrictions by blocking write operations in plan mode with informative errors before dispatching to handlers.</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p4\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p4.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p4.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Lifecycle hooks</span> provide extensibility without modifying handler code. The hook system defines ten lifecycle events (<span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p4.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">SESSION_START</span>, <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p4.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">USER_PROMPT_SUBMIT</span>, <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p4.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">PRE_TOOL_USE</span>, <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p4.1.5\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">POST_TOOL_USE</span>, <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p4.1.6\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">POST_TOOL_USE_FAILURE</span>, <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p4.1.7\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">SUBAGENT_START</span>, <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p4.1.8\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">SUBAGENT_STOP</span>, <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p4.1.9\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">PRE_COMPACT</span>, <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p4.1.10\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">SESSION_END</span>, and <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p4.1.11\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">STOP</span>) covering the full agent lifecycle from session initialization to shutdown. <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p4.1.12\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">PreToolUse</span> hooks fire synchronously before execution: a hook returning exit code 2 hard-blocks the tool call, returning an error to the model that no amount of prompt engineering or approval configuration can override. Hooks can also mutate tool arguments by returning a JSON object with an <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p4.1.13\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">updatedInput</span> field, enabling transparent command rewriting (e.g., injecting <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p4.1.14\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">--dry-run</span> flags). <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p4.1.15\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">PostToolUse</span> and <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p4.1.16\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">PostToolUseFailure</span> hooks fire asynchronously via a thread pool after execution, suitable for auditing and logging without delaying the agent. External scripts registered as hooks receive full event context as JSON on stdin (including session ID, working directory, tool name, tool input, and (for post-hooks) tool response), enabling project-specific policies such as blocking writes to protected paths, enforcing naming conventions, or streaming audit logs to external systems. Hook matchers use compiled regex patterns against tool names, allowing fine-grained targeting from single-tool rules to catch-all policies.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px2\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Design evolution.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Early versions registered tools directly in a global namespace, causing naming collisions and complex per-tool safety configuration. Category-based handlers solved both: safety rules apply at the category level, and each category provides implicit namespacing.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px3\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Runtime approval.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px3.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px3.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Before any tool call reaches its handler, the runtime approval system gates execution based on user-configured trust boundaries. Three autonomy levels control the default posture: <em id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px3.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">Manual</em> requires explicit approval for every tool call; <em id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px3.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">Semi-Auto</em> auto-approves read-only operations (a curated allowlist of commands such as <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px3.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">ls</span>, <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px3.p1.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">cat</span>, <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px3.p1.1.5\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">git status</span>) while prompting for writes; and <em id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px3.p1.1.6\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">Auto</em> approves all operations for trusted workflows. Beyond the default level, an <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px3.p1.1.7\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">ApprovalRulesManager</span> evaluates each command against a prioritized rule set with four rule types: <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px3.p1.1.8\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps\">Pattern</span> (regex match against the full command string), <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px3.p1.1.9\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps\">Command</span> (exact match), <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px3.p1.1.10\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps\">Prefix</span> (prefix match, e.g., <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px3.p1.1.11\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">git</span> matching <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px3.p1.1.12\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">git push</span>), and <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px3.p1.1.13\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps\">Danger</span> (regex match with auto-deny semantics). Default danger rules at priority 100 (matching patterns such as <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px3.p1.1.14\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">rm -rf /</span>, <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px3.p1.1.15\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">rm -rf *</span>, and <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px3.p1.1.16\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">chmod 777</span>) are always active and cannot be overridden by user configuration or approval-level changes. Rules are evaluated in priority order; the first match determines the action (auto-approve, auto-deny, require approval, or require the user to edit the command before execution).</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px3.p2\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px3.p2.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Approval rules persist across sessions via two JSON stores: user-global rules at ˜<span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px3.p2.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">/.opendev/permissions.json</span> and project-scoped rules at <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px3.p2.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">.opendev/permissions.json</span>. When both exist, project rules take priority for the same pattern, enabling per-repository trust boundaries (e.g., a shared project can restrict <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px3.p2.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">docker</span> commands that a user’s personal config allows). The approval flow adapts to the active frontend: the TUI presents a blocking <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px3.p2.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">prompt_toolkit</span> menu with keyboard navigation, while the Web UI broadcasts an <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px3.p2.1.5\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">approval_required</span> WebSocket event and polls a threading event with a 300-second timeout, rendering an approval dialog in the browser. Every approval decision (command, action taken, matching rule, and timestamp) is recorded in a <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS1.Px3.p2.1.6\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">CommandHistory</span> for audit.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2\" class=\"ltx_subsubsection\">\n<h4 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection\">2.4.2 </span>File Operations</h4>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Five tools handle all file-system interactions (see File Ops category in <a href=\"#A1.T1\" title=\"In Appendix A Complete Tool Catalog ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Table</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">1</span></a>), from reading and writing to structured editing and searching. Together they form the agent’s primary means of code manipulation.</p>\n</div>\n<section id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px1\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\"><span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">read_file</span>: Line-numbered file reading.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Reads file contents with <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px1.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">cat -n</span> style line numbering, providing the agent with precise positional references for subsequent edits. Three parameters control the read window: <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px1.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">file_path</span> (required), <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px1.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">offset</span> (1-based line start, default 1), and <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px1.p1.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">max_lines</span> (default 2000). The handler applies several output transformations before returning content to the agent:</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px1.p2\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<ul id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px1.p2.1\" class=\"ltx_itemize\">\n<li id=\"S2.I6.i1\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\"><math id=\"S2.I6.i1.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\bullet\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\bullet</annotation></semantics></math></span> \n<div id=\"S2.I6.i1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S2.I6.i1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S2.I6.i1.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Binary detection:</span> Non-text files are detected and rejected with descriptive errors rather than returning corrupted byte sequences.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"S2.I6.i2\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\"><math id=\"S2.I6.i2.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\bullet\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\bullet</annotation></semantics></math></span> \n<div id=\"S2.I6.i2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S2.I6.i2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S2.I6.i2.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Output truncation:</span> Content exceeding 30,000 characters is truncated using a head-tail strategy that preserves the first 10,000 and last 10,000 characters with a truncation marker between them. This ensures the agent sees both the beginning (imports, class declarations) and end (recent additions) of long files.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"S2.I6.i3\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\"><math id=\"S2.I6.i3.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\bullet\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\bullet</annotation></semantics></math></span> \n<div id=\"S2.I6.i3.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S2.I6.i3.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S2.I6.i3.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Per-line truncation:</span> Individual lines exceeding 2,000 characters are truncated to prevent minified code or data files from consuming excessive context.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"S2.I6.i4\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\"><math id=\"S2.I6.i4.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\bullet\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\bullet</annotation></semantics></math></span> \n<div id=\"S2.I6.i4.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S2.I6.i4.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S2.I6.i4.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Stale-read tracking:</span> A <span id=\"S2.I6.i4.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">FileTimeTracker</span> records the timestamp of each read. The tracker records <span id=\"S2.I6.i4.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">datetime.now()</span> keyed by <span id=\"S2.I6.i4.p1.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">(session_id, file_path)</span> on every successful read. Before any edit, <span id=\"S2.I6.i4.p1.1.5\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">assert_fresh()</span> verifies that <span id=\"S2.I6.i4.p1.1.6\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">os.path.getmtime(file_path)</span> <math id=\"S2.I6.i4.p1.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\leq\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo>≤</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\leq</annotation></semantics></math> <span id=\"S2.I6.i4.p1.1.7\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">read_time + 50ms</span>, where the 50ms tolerance accommodates filesystem timestamp granularity (FAT32 rounds to 2-second boundaries; NTFS and ext4 offer sub-millisecond precision, but network filesystems introduce jitter). If the assertion fails, the edit is rejected with an error instructing the agent to re-read the file, preventing silent overwrites of concurrent user edits. A <span id=\"S2.I6.i4.p1.1.8\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">threading.Lock</span> per file path serializes concurrent write attempts to the same file.</p>\n</div></li>\n</ul>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px2\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\"><span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px2.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">write_file</span>: New file creation.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Creates new files only by rejecting attempts to overwrite existing files, directing the agent to use <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px2.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">edit_file</span> instead. This constraint prevents accidental full-file overwrites, which are a common failure mode when agents reconstruct files from memory rather than applying targeted edits. Parameters: <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px2.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">file_path</span>, <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px2.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">content</span>, and <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px2.p1.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">create_dirs</span> (which auto-creates parent directories when set). The handler runs the approval workflow for write operations, records the action with the undo manager for rollback capability, and returns the file path and byte count on success.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px3\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\"><span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px3.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">edit_file</span>: 9-pass fuzzy matching.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px3.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px3.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">When an LLM-based agent edits a file, it specifies <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px3.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">old_content</span> to find and <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px3.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">new_content</span> to replace. In practice, the LLM frequently produces <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px3.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">old_content</span> that differs slightly from the actual file: trailing whitespace variations, indentation mismatches, escape sequence differences, or minor reformatting from reconstructing code from memory rather than verbatim copy. A strict exact-match edit tool fails on these cases, producing “content not found” errors that consume context with error messages and recovery attempts.</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px3.p2\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px3.p2.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">The edit tool implements a chain-of-responsibility pattern with nine replacer classes, each addressing a specific mismatch category, from exact match through whitespace normalization, indentation flexibility, escape handling, and context-aware anchor matching (<a href=\"#A4\" title=\"Appendix D Edit Tool Fuzzy Matching Chain ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Appendix</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">D</span></a> enumerates all nine passes with descriptions). Each replacer returns the <em id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px3.p2.1.1\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">actual substring found in the original file</em> (not the search query), so the replacement preserves the file’s original formatting. Debug logging records which pass succeeded. The chain short-circuits on first match, so exact matches incur zero overhead from the fuzzy passes.</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px3.p3\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px3.p3.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Beyond matching, the edit handler enforces several safety and observability measures. Stale-read validation rejects edits to files modified since the agent’s last read. Uniqueness verification ensures the match is unambiguous: multiple matches produce errors rather than silent mis-edits. Backup state is created for undo tracking. After a successful edit, the handler calls <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px3.p3.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">lsp.touch_file(filepath)</span> to notify the running language server of the change, then waits up to 3 seconds (debounced) for diagnostics. Only Error-severity diagnostics are included; warnings and hints are suppressed to avoid context noise. Up to 20 diagnostics are appended to the tool output as structured feedback (e.g., “<span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px3.p3.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">LSP errors detected: line 42: undefined variable ‘foo’</span>”), giving the agent immediate feedback and enabling self-correction in the same turn. If no LSP server is running for the file type, the check is silently skipped. A unified diff is generated for display to the user.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px4\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\"><span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px4.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">list_files</span>: Directory listing and glob search.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px4.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px4.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Lists directory contents or performs glob-based file search. Parameters: <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px4.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">path</span> (directory to list), <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px4.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">pattern</span> (glob expression for filtering), <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px4.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">max_results</span> (default 100). Results render as a tree display showing directory structure. Common ignore patterns are excluded by default: <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px4.p1.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">node_modules</span>, <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px4.p1.1.5\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">.git</span>, <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px4.p1.1.6\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">__pycache__</span>, <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px4.p1.1.7\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">.venv</span>, <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px4.p1.1.8\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">.DS_Store</span>, and other platform-specific artifacts. Output is capped at 500 entries to prevent context overflow from large repositories.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px5\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\"><span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px5.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">search</span>: Dual-mode content search.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px5.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px5.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Supports two search modes addressing complementary needs. With <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px5.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">type=\"text\"</span>, the tool delegates to ripgrep for high-performance regex-based content search with configurable context lines, supporting the full PCRE2 pattern syntax. With <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px5.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">type=\"ast\"</span>, the tool delegates to ast-grep for structural code search using language-aware pattern templates with <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px5.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">$VAR</span> wildcards (e.g., <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px5.p1.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">if $COND: $BODY</span> matches any Python if-statement regardless of specific condition or body content). Parameters: <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px5.p1.1.5\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">pattern</span> (regex or ast-grep template), <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px5.p1.1.6\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">path</span> (search root), <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px5.p1.1.7\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">type</span> (“text” or “ast”), <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px5.p1.1.8\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">lang</span> (language hint for ast mode). Results are capped at 50 matches and 30,000 characters total output.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px6\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Design evolution.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px6.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS2.Px6.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">The initial edit tool used a two-pass strategy (exact match, then whitespace-stripped match). This was the single largest source of “content not found” errors. Analyzing failure logs revealed that LLM formatting drift falls into distinct, predictable categories (whitespace normalization, indentation shifts, escape sequence differences, partial-context anchoring), each addressable by a targeted matching pass. Generalizing this observation into a chain-of-responsibility architecture with nine progressively relaxed replacers resolved the vast majority of edit failures while preserving exact-match performance through short-circuit evaluation.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS4.SSS3\" class=\"ltx_subsubsection\">\n<h4 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection\">2.4.3 </span>Shell Execution and Background Tasks</h4>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS3.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS3.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Four tools handle shell execution and background task management (see Process category in <a href=\"#A1.T1\" title=\"In Appendix A Complete Tool Catalog ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Table</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">1</span></a>). The agent needs to run arbitrary shell commands for testing, building, and system interaction, but must do so safely; long-running processes like development servers require background execution with output capture.</p>\n</div>\n<figure id=\"S2.F17\" class=\"ltx_figure\"><img src=\"2603.05344v3/bash_tool.png\" id=\"S2.F17.g1\" class=\"ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape\" style=\"aspect-ratio:648/321;\" width=\"648\" height=\"321\" alt=\"Refer to caption\">\n<figcaption class=\"ltx_caption ltx_centering\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure\">Figure 17: </span>Detailed pipeline for the Process handler (<a href=\"#S2.F16\" title=\"In Three separated concerns. ‣ 2.4.1 Registry Architecture and Schema Construction ‣ 2.4 Tool System ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Figure</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">16</span></a>). Commands pass through three safety gates (permission config, allowed-command matching, dangerous pattern blocking), then command preparation (auto-confirm, unbuffered Python), server detection (regex match against 16 patterns for auto-background promotion), execution fork (PTY-based background or piped foreground with process-group isolation), output management (30k char limit with head/tail truncation, 100ms polling), and timeout/interrupt handling (60s idle, 600s absolute, <span id=\"S2.F17.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">InterruptToken</span> integration).</figcaption>\n</figure>\n<section id=\"S2.SS4.SSS3.Px1\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\"><span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS3.Px1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">run_command</span>: Six-stage shell execution.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS3.Px1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS3.Px1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><a href=\"#S2.F17\" title=\"In 2.4.3 Shell Execution and Background Tasks ‣ 2.4 Tool System ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Figure</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">17</span></a> illustrates the pipeline, which processes every shell command through six stages: (1) safety gates that block dangerous patterns with no override, (2) command preparation that auto-confirms package manager prompts and unbuffers Python output, (3) server detection via regex match against 16 framework patterns (<a href=\"#A5.SS2\" title=\"E.2 Server Detection Patterns ‣ Appendix E Shell Execution Pipeline ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">E.2</span></a>) that auto-promotes long-running servers to background mode, (4) execution fork between PTY-based background and piped foreground with process-group isolation, (5) output management with 30k-character head-tail truncation and 100ms polling, and (6) timeout handling with 60-second idle and 600-second absolute limits. <a href=\"#A5\" title=\"Appendix E Shell Execution Pipeline ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Appendix</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">E</span></a> provides the full stage-by-stage details and the complete server pattern table.</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS3.Px1.p2\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS3.Px1.p2.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Commands promoted to background are registered with the <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS3.Px1.p2.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">BackgroundTaskManager</span>, which assigns 7-character hex IDs (from <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS3.Px1.p2.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">uuid4().hex[:7]</span>, providing <math id=\"S2.SS4.SSS3.Px1.p2.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"{\\sim}268\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>∼</mo><mn>268</mn></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">{\\sim}268</annotation></semantics></math>M unique values). Registration creates the task record, opens an output file at <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS3.Px1.p2.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">/tmp/opendev/{sanitized-dir}/tasks/{id}.output</span>, writes any initial startup output captured during the first 20 seconds, and spawns a daemon thread that continuously streams PTY output to the file via <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS3.Px1.p2.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">select.select()</span> polling. Tasks transition through four states: RUNNING <math id=\"S2.SS4.SSS3.Px1.p2.m2\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\to\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo stretchy=\"false\">→</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\to</annotation></semantics></math> COMPLETED (exit code 0), FAILED (non-zero exit), or KILLED (via signal). Listener callbacks notify the UI of each state transition, enabling real-time status display in the TUI footer.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS4.SSS3.Px2\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\"><span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS3.Px2.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">list_processes</span>: Background task listing.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS3.Px2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS3.Px2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Returns all tracked background tasks with PID, status (running/completed/failed/killed), and wall-clock runtime. This gives the agent visibility into what processes are active, enabling it to check on long-running servers, identify stalled builds, or determine which tasks need attention.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS4.SSS3.Px3\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\"><span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS3.Px3.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">get_process_output</span>: Task output retrieval.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS3.Px3.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS3.Px3.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Retrieves the last 100 lines from a background task’s output file by task ID, giving the agent access to server logs, build output, and error messages without needing to re-run the command. This is essential for monitoring development servers, inspecting test results from background runs, and diagnosing failures in long-running processes.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS4.SSS3.Px4\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\"><span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS3.Px4.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">kill_process</span>: Graceful process termination.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS3.Px4.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS3.Px4.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Terminates a running background task using graceful escalation: send SIGTERM to the entire process group via <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS3.Px4.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">os.killpg()</span>, wait 5 seconds for graceful shutdown, then escalate to SIGKILL if the process is still running. The daemon output thread is signaled to stop, and the PTY master file descriptor is closed. Process group killing ensures that child processes spawned by the command (e.g., webpack dev server spawning file watchers) are terminated along with the parent.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS4.SSS3.Px5\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Design evolution.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS3.Px5.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS3.Px5.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">The initial implementation used <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS3.Px5.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">subprocess.run()</span> with a fixed timeout. Development servers invariably hit the timeout and were killed. Activity-based idle timeout solved the server problem, and PTY-based execution solved output buffering issues where programs would produce no visible output until process termination.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS4.SSS4\" class=\"ltx_subsubsection\">\n<h4 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection\">2.4.4 </span>Web Interaction</h4>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS4.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS4.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Four tools provide web interaction capabilities (see Web category in <a href=\"#A1.T1\" title=\"In Appendix A Complete Tool Catalog ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Table</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">1</span></a>) for documentation research, content inspection, and browser-based testing. All web tools are read-only and safe for use in plan mode.</p>\n</div>\n<section id=\"S2.SS4.SSS4.Px1\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\"><span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS4.Px1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">fetch_url</span>: Browser-engine web fetching.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS4.Px1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS4.Px1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Retrieves web content using Crawl4AI, a browser-engine crawling library built on Playwright. The browser-engine approach handles JavaScript-rendered content that simple HTTP clients would miss (single-page applications, dynamically loaded documentation). HTML is converted to markdown for context-efficient consumption by the LLM. Output is capped at 50,000 characters with a 30-second per-page timeout. File downloads are blocked to prevent disk abuse.</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS4.Px1.p2\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS4.Px1.p2.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">For multi-page exploration, the tool supports deep crawling with three configurable strategies: breadth-first (BFS), depth-first (DFS), or best-first (priority by content relevance). Parameters control maximum crawl depth, page limit, and domain filters to prevent crawling beyond the target site. Playwright Chromium is auto-installed on first use, with the installation triggered transparently when the tool is first invoked.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS4.SSS4.Px2\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\"><span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS4.Px2.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">web_search</span>: Privacy-respecting search.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS4.Px2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS4.Px2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Searches the web via DuckDuckGo, chosen for its privacy-respecting design (no user tracking or search history retention). Returns up to 10 results, each containing title, URL, and text snippet. Domain filters allow restricting results to specific sites (e.g., searching only official documentation domains). The tool returns structured results that the agent can then follow up on with <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS4.Px2.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">fetch_url</span> for full content retrieval.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS4.SSS4.Px3\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\"><span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS4.Px3.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">capture_web_screenshot</span>: Visual page capture.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS4.Px3.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS4.Px3.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Takes full-page screenshots via Playwright’s headless browser. Configurable viewport dimensions (default 1920<math id=\"S2.SS4.SSS4.Px3.p1.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\times\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\times</annotation></semantics></math>1080) allow capturing pages at different responsive breakpoints. Optional PDF output mode produces paginated documents. Timeout extends up to 180 seconds for complex pages with heavy JavaScript initialization. Returns the screenshot file path, which the agent can reference in subsequent analysis or present to the user.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS4.SSS4.Px4\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\"><span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS4.Px4.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">open_browser</span>: System browser launch.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS4.Px4.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS4.Px4.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Opens a URL or local file in the system’s default browser via platform-native commands. Local file paths are automatically converted to <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS4.Px4.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">file://</span> URIs. This tool bridges the gap between the agent’s headless environment and the user’s visual workflow, making it useful for previewing generated HTML, reviewing web applications under development, or opening documentation links that require authentication the agent cannot provide.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS4.SSS4.Px5\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Design evolution.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS4.Px5.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS4.Px5.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">The initial implementation used simple HTTP requests via the <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS4.Px5.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">requests</span> library, which failed on JavaScript-rendered single-page applications that dominate modern documentation and web frameworks. Switching to Crawl4AI with Playwright’s browser engine solved this, enabling full DOM rendering before content extraction.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5\" class=\"ltx_subsubsection\">\n<h4 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection\">2.4.5 </span>Multi-Language Semantic Code Analysis via LSP</h4>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Six tools provide multi-language semantic code analysis via LSP (see Symbols category in <a href=\"#A1.T1\" title=\"In Appendix A Complete Tool Catalog ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Table</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">1</span></a>), split into two read-only navigation tools and four structural editing tools. Text-based tools can search for strings but miss semantic structure: finding all usages of a method requires distinguishing method calls from variable names, handling overloading, and tracking references across files. Building custom parsers for each language is infeasible, so <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps\">OpenDev</span> adopts Language Server Protocol integration via standard language servers <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib58\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">58</a>]</cite>, reusing a mature ecosystem where each server is maintained by domain experts.</p>\n</div>\n<figure id=\"S2.F18\" class=\"ltx_figure\"><img src=\"2603.05344v3/lsp.png\" id=\"S2.F18.g1\" class=\"ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape\" style=\"aspect-ratio:648/318;\" width=\"648\" height=\"318\" alt=\"Refer to caption\">\n<figcaption class=\"ltx_caption ltx_centering\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure\">Figure 18: </span>Detailed architecture for the Symbols handler (<a href=\"#S2.F16\" title=\"In Three separated concerns. ‣ 2.4.1 Registry Architecture and Schema Construction ‣ 2.4 Tool System ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Figure</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">16</span></a>). The system is organized into four layers: Agent Tool Layer (six symbol tools), Symbol Retriever (unified API), LSP Server Wrapper (language detection, per-language server pool, symbol conversion), and Solid Language Server (two-level cache, file buffer management, LSP protocol operations). The Language Server Handler manages subprocess lifecycle and JSON-RPC 2.0 communication with external language server processes. Language detection maps 30+ file extensions to their respective servers, which are started lazily on first query and reused across subsequent requests.</figcaption>\n</figure>\n<section id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px1\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Four-layer LSP abstraction.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><a href=\"#S2.F18\" title=\"In 2.4.5 Multi-Language Semantic Code Analysis via LSP ‣ 2.4 Tool System ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Figure</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">18</span></a> illustrates the architecture, organized into four layers that progressively translate between agent-facing tool calls and language-server-specific protocol messages. The <em id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px1.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">Agent Tool Layer</em> exposes the six tools described below; each accepts a file path and a symbol name, with language detection, server selection, and protocol translation handled transparently by the lower layers. The <em id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px1.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">Symbol Retriever</em> provides a unified API that resolves symbol names to positions using a <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px1.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">NamePathMatcher</span> supporting exact match (<span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px1.p1.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">MyClass.method</span>), partial path match (<span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px1.p1.1.5\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">method</span> matching any symbol whose path ends with <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px1.p1.1.6\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">.method</span>), and wildcard match (<span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px1.p1.1.7\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">My*</span> matching <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px1.p1.1.8\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">MyClass</span>, <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px1.p1.1.9\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">MyModule</span>). The <em id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px1.p1.1.10\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">LSP Server Wrapper</em> handles language detection (30+ file extensions; see <a href=\"#S2.F18\" title=\"In 2.4.5 Multi-Language Semantic Code Analysis via LSP ‣ 2.4 Tool System ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Figure</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">18</span></a>) and server lifecycle via a singleton pool: one server per language, started lazily, with automatic liveness checks and transparent restart on crash. The <em id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px1.p1.1.11\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">Solid Language Server</em> manages the low-level LSP protocol through a subprocess handler communicating via JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio, with two daemon threads per server for I/O, thread-safe request IDs, and configurable per-request timeouts. Each language server extends a common base class with language-specific overrides (initialization parameters, ignored directories, cross-file reference wait times), allowing new languages to be added by dropping in a server class without modifying the core framework.</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px1.p2\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px1.p2.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">To avoid redundant LSP round-trips, each language server maintains a two-level cache keyed by file content hash (MD5). Level 1 caches raw LSP responses; Level 2 caches processed symbol trees with parent-child relationships and body previews. When a file has not changed, queries return from Level 2 without contacting the server. When a file has changed but the raw response schema has not, only Level 2 is recomputed from cached Level 1 data. Cache storage uses pickle serialization in the project’s <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px1.p2.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">.solidlsp/cache/&lt;language_id&gt;/</span> directory, with a version field that ensures incompatible caches are discarded.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px2\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\"><span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px2.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">find_symbol</span>: Symbol definition lookup.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Parameters: <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px2.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">symbol_name</span> (supports qualified names like <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px2.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">MyClass.method</span>, partial matches, and wildcards), optional <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px2.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">file_path</span> to scope the search. Returns symbol definitions with kind (function, class, variable, etc.), location (file, line, column), name path (e.g., <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px2.p1.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">module.Class.method</span>), and body preview (first 200 characters). When multiple matches exist, all are returned with their full paths, letting the agent disambiguate.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px3\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\"><span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px3.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">find_referencing_symbols</span>: Cross-file reference search.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px3.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px3.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Parameters: <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px3.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">symbol_name</span>, <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px3.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">file_path</span> (where defined), <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px3.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">include_declaration</span> (whether to include the definition itself). Semantically finds all references (calls, imports, type annotations) grouped by file. Used for impact analysis before refactoring and for understanding how a symbol is consumed across the codebase.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px4\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\"><span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px4.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">rename_symbol</span>: Workspace-wide semantic rename.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px4.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px4.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Parameters: <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px4.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">symbol_name</span>, <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px4.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">file_path</span>, <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px4.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">new_name</span> (validated as a legal identifier: starts with letter or underscore, contains only alphanumeric characters). Applies workspace edits returned by the LSP server’s <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px4.p1.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">textDocument/rename</span> in reverse order (bottom-to-top within each file) so that earlier edits do not shift the line numbers of later ones. Only renames code references; strings and comments are left unchanged.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px5\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\"><span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px5.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">replace_symbol_body</span>: Body-preserving rewrite.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px5.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px5.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Parameters: <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px5.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">symbol_name</span>, <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px5.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">file_path</span>, <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px5.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">new_body</span>, <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px5.p1.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">preserve_signature</span> (default true). Detects the body boundary (colon for Python, opening brace for C-like languages) and replaces only the body while keeping the signature, decorators, and docstring intact. This enables the agent to rewrite function implementations without accidentally altering their public interface.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px6\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\"><span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px6.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">insert_before_symbol</span> and <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px6.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">insert_after_symbol</span>: Positional code insertion.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px6.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px6.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Parameters: <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px6.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">symbol_name</span>, <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px6.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">file_path</span>, <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px6.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">content</span>. Inserts content before or after a named symbol at matching indentation level with blank-line separation. Useful for adding methods adjacent to related code, inserting helper functions near their callers, or placing test cases next to the functions they exercise.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px7\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Design evolution.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px7.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS5.Px7.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">The initial approach considered building custom AST-based analysis using tree-sitter grammars. While tree-sitter provides fast, incremental parsing, it lacks the semantic understanding that language servers provide: type resolution, cross-file reference tracking, and workspace-wide renaming. LSP integration leverages a mature ecosystem where each language server is maintained by domain experts, and the on-demand server lifecycle ensures that resource consumption scales with actual usage rather than the number of supported languages.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS4.SSS6\" class=\"ltx_subsubsection\">\n<h4 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection\">2.4.6 </span>User Interaction, Task Management, and Planning</h4>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS6.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS6.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Eight tools enable user interaction, task management, and plan-based workflows (see Task Mgmt, User Input, Planning, and Completion categories in <a href=\"#A1.T1\" title=\"In Appendix A Complete Tool Catalog ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Table</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">1</span></a>). They form the human-in-the-loop backbone of the system, ensuring the agent can gather requirements, report progress, and obtain approval at critical decision points.</p>\n</div>\n<section id=\"S2.SS4.SSS6.Px1\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\"><span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS6.Px1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">ask_user</span>: Structured multi-choice questions.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS6.Px1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS6.Px1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Presents up to four questions per invocation, each with a structured format designed for efficient user interaction. Every question includes: a header label (max 12 characters, displayed as a compact chip/tag for visual scanning), 2–4 options each with a label and description explaining implications, and an optional <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS6.Px1.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">multiSelect</span> flag for non-exclusive choices. An “Other” option with free-text input is auto-appended to every question, ensuring users are never constrained to the agent’s proposed choices.</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS6.Px1.p2\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS6.Px1.p2.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">The rendering adapts to the active UI: the TUI presents questions as a modal dialog with keyboard navigation, while the Web UI uses a polling-based survey component where the agent’s thread blocks until the user submits a response via WebSocket. This blocking-with-timeout design ensures the agent waits for user input without consuming CPU or progressing with assumptions.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS4.SSS6.Px2\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Task tracking (<span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS6.Px2.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">write_todos</span>, <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS6.Px2.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">update_todo</span>, <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS6.Px2.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">complete_todo</span>, <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS6.Px2.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">list_todos</span>): Lightweight kanban task list.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS6.Px2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS6.Px2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Four tools manage a lightweight kanban-style task list that persists across agent iterations:</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS6.Px2.p2\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<ul id=\"S2.SS4.SSS6.Px2.p2.1\" class=\"ltx_itemize\">\n<li id=\"S2.I7.i1\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\"><math id=\"S2.I7.i1.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\bullet\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\bullet</annotation></semantics></math></span> \n<div id=\"S2.I7.i1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S2.I7.i1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S2.I7.i1.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">write_todos</span>: Creates or replaces the entire task list from a structured definition. Each task has a title, description, and status (todo, doing, done).</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"S2.I7.i2\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\"><math id=\"S2.I7.i2.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\bullet\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\bullet</annotation></semantics></math></span> \n<div id=\"S2.I7.i2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S2.I7.i2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S2.I7.i2.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">update_todo</span>: Modifies an existing task by numeric ID, title, or slug. Enforces the constraint that at most one task can have “doing” status at a time: setting a new task to “doing” automatically returns the previously active task to “todo”.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"S2.I7.i3\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\"><math id=\"S2.I7.i3.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\bullet\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\bullet</annotation></semantics></math></span> \n<div id=\"S2.I7.i3.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S2.I7.i3.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S2.I7.i3.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">complete_todo</span>: Marks a task as done with an optional completion log message recording what was accomplished.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"S2.I7.i4\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\"><math id=\"S2.I7.i4.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\bullet\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\bullet</annotation></semantics></math></span> \n<div id=\"S2.I7.i4.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S2.I7.i4.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S2.I7.i4.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">list_todos</span>: Returns all tasks sorted by status priority: doing first, then todo, then done. This ordering ensures the agent’s attention is drawn to active and pending work.</p>\n</div></li>\n</ul>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS4.SSS6.Px3\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\"><span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS6.Px3.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">present_plan</span>: Plan review and approval.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS6.Px3.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS6.Px3.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Reads the plan file (written by the agent during plan mode), displays its contents to the user, and requests explicit approval before proceeding to implementation. The user responds with one of three outcomes:</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS6.Px3.p2\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<ul id=\"S2.SS4.SSS6.Px3.p2.1\" class=\"ltx_itemize\">\n<li id=\"S2.I8.i1\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\"><math id=\"S2.I8.i1.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\bullet\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\bullet</annotation></semantics></math></span> \n<div id=\"S2.I8.i1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S2.I8.i1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><em id=\"S2.I8.i1.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">approve_auto</em>: Approve the plan and auto-approve all subsequent edits that implement it, minimizing approval friction for trusted plans.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"S2.I8.i2\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\"><math id=\"S2.I8.i2.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\bullet\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\bullet</annotation></semantics></math></span> \n<div id=\"S2.I8.i2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S2.I8.i2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><em id=\"S2.I8.i2.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">approve</em>: Approve the plan but review each individual edit during implementation, maintaining fine-grained control.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"S2.I8.i3\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\"><math id=\"S2.I8.i3.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\bullet\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\bullet</annotation></semantics></math></span> \n<div id=\"S2.I8.i3.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S2.I8.i3.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><em id=\"S2.I8.i3.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">modify</em>: Reject with feedback, providing specific changes the agent should incorporate before re-presenting.</p>\n</div></li>\n</ul>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS6.Px3.p3\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS6.Px3.p3.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">On approval, plan steps are automatically extracted into the todo list, creating a structured execution tracker that the agent uses to methodically implement each step and report progress.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS4.SSS6.Px4\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\"><span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS6.Px4.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">task_complete</span>: Explicit completion signal.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS6.Px4.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS6.Px4.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Signals that the agent has finished its current task, providing a summary message and success/failure status. This tool serves a critical architectural role: it gives the ReAct executor a structured termination signal, distinguishing intentional completion from iteration exhaustion (hitting the maximum iteration limit). Without this tool, the agent would either loop until cut off or produce an unstructured final message, making it difficult for the system to determine whether the task was actually completed.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS4.SSS6.Px5\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Design evolution.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS6.Px5.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS6.Px5.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Early versions lacked structured user interaction; the agent output free-text questions that were difficult to parse reliably. Introducing the structured multi-choice format with typed options and descriptions improved response quality, reduced misunderstanding, and enabled the UI to render consistent survey-style dialogs across both TUI and Web interfaces.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S2.SS4.SSS7\" class=\"ltx_subsubsection\">\n<h4 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection\">2.4.7 </span>Token-Efficient External Tool Discovery via MCP</h4>\n\n<div id=\"S2.SS4.SSS7.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S2.SS4.SSS7.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">One tool, <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS7.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">search_tools</span>, provides token-efficient external tool discovery via the Model Context Protocol <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite\">[<a href=\"#bib.bib1\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">1</a>]</cite> (see Discovery category in <a href=\"#A1.T1\" title=\"In Appendix A Complete Tool Catalog ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Table</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">1</span></a>). External tools discovered through search are then invoked via the <span id=\"S2.SS4.SSS7.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">McpToolHandler</span>, which dispatches calls to the appropriate server. The core problem is context efficiency: a system with 100 external tools, each schema averaging 200 tokens, consumes 20,000 tokens purely for tool definitions.
