class=\"ltx_foreignobject_container\"><span class=\"ltx_foreignobject_content\">\n<span id=\"S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.pic1.1\" class=\"ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom\" style=\"width:40.85em;\">\n<span id=\"S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.pic1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.pic1.1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif ltx_font_bold\" style=\"--ltx-fg-color:#25588C;\">Lesson: Calibrate from API-reported token counts, not local estimates</span></span>\n</span></span></span></foreignObject></g><g fill-opacity=\"1.0\" transform=\"matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 15.56 14.1)\"><foreignObject style=\"--ltx-fo-width:44.93em;--ltx-fo-height:9.09em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.19em;font-size:10pt;\" height=\"128.53\" overflow=\"visible\" transform=\"matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 125.84)\" width=\"621.7\"><span class=\"ltx_foreignobject_container\"><span class=\"ltx_foreignobject_content\">\n<span id=\"S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.pic1.2\" class=\"ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom\" style=\"width:44.93em;\">\n<span id=\"S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.pic1.2.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.pic1.2.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text\" style=\"--ltx-fg-color:#000000;\">Using the API’s reported <span id=\"S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.pic1.2.1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">prompt_tokens</span> from the previous call as the calibration anchor is essential for accurate context management. Providers inject invisible content (safety preambles, tool schema serializations, internal formatting) that makes local token counting systematically underestimate actual usage. In our system, the discrepancy was large enough to cause compaction to trigger too late, leading to context overflow errors (<a href=\"#S2.SS3.SSS7\" title=\"2.3.7 Context Retrieval and Assembly Pipeline ‣ 2.3 Context Engineering Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.3.7</span></a>). Always treat the provider’s reported token count as ground truth; local estimates are useful only as a fallback when no prior API response is available.</span></span>\n</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>\n</div>\n</section>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S3.SS2\" class=\"ltx_subsection\">\n<h3 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_subsection\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection\">3.2 </span>Steering Behavior Over Long Horizons</h3>\n\n<div id=\"S3.SS2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S3.SS2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">System prompt influence decays as conversations grow. Instructions that reliably govern the agent’s first few turns are routinely violated after 30 or more tool calls, when the instruction is far from the model’s attention window and buried under dozens of tool results. Behavioral guidance is therefore a signal-to-noise engineering problem: how to maintain compliance without drowning the context in repeated directives.</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S3.SS2.p2\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\"><span class=\"ltx_inline-block\"><svg id=\"S3.SS2.p2.pic1\" class=\"ltx_picture\" height=\"205.28\" overflow=\"visible\" version=\"1.1\" viewBox=\"0 0 650 205.28\" width=\"650\"><g style=\"--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;\" fill=\"#000000\" stroke=\"#000000\" stroke-width=\"0.4pt\" transform=\"translate(0,205.28) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)\"><g style=\"--ltx-fill-color:#BFD0E1;\" fill=\"#BFD0E1\" fill-opacity=\"1.0\"><path style=\"stroke:none\" d=\"M 0 0 L 0 205.28 L 650 205.28 L 650 0 Z\"></path></g><g style=\"--ltx-fill-color:#F6F9FB;\" fill=\"#F6F9FB\" fill-opacity=\"1.0\"><path style=\"stroke:none\" d=\"M 0.55 0.55 L 0.55 184 L 649.45 184 L 649.45 0.55 Z\"></path></g><g style=\"--ltx-fill-color:#EEF2F7;\" fill=\"#EEF2F7\" fill-opacity=\"1.0\"><path style=\"stroke:none\" d=\"M 0.55 184.56 L 0.55 204.73 L 649.45 204.73 L 649.45 184.56 Z\"></path></g><g style=\"--ltx-stroke-color:#29629B;--ltx-fill-color:#29629B;--ltx-fg-color:#29629B;\" color=\"#29629B\" fill=\"#29629B\" stroke=\"#29629B\" stroke-width=\"2.5pt\"><path style=\"fill:none\" d=\"M 1.73 205.28 L 1.73 0\"></path></g><g fill-opacity=\"1.0\" transform=\"matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 15.56 191.18)\"><foreignObject style=\"--ltx-fo-width:40.85em;--ltx-fo-height:0.69em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.19em;font-size:10pt;\" height=\"12.3\" overflow=\"visible\" transform=\"matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 9.61)\" width=\"565.25\"><span class=\"ltx_foreignobject_container\"><span class=\"ltx_foreignobject_content\">\n<span id=\"S3.SS2.p2.pic1.1\" class=\"ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom\" style=\"width:40.85em;\">\n<span id=\"S3.SS2.p2.pic1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S3.SS2.p2.pic1.1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif ltx_font_bold\" style=\"--ltx-fg-color:#25588C;\">Lesson: Inject reminders at the point of decision, not upfront</span></span>\n</span></span></span></foreignObject></g><g fill-opacity=\"1.0\" transform=\"matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 15.56 14.1)\"><foreignObject style=\"--ltx-fo-width:44.93em;--ltx-fo-height:11.49em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.19em;font-size:10pt;\" height=\"161.74\" overflow=\"visible\" transform=\"matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 159.05)\" width=\"621.7\"><span class=\"ltx_foreignobject_container\"><span class=\"ltx_foreignobject_content\">\n<span id=\"S3.SS2.p2.pic1.2\" class=\"ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom\" style=\"width:44.93em;\">\n<span id=\"S3.SS2.p2.pic1.2.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S3.SS2.p2.pic1.2.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text\" style=\"--ltx-fg-color:#000000;\">Short, targeted reminders at maximum recency are more effective than long system prompt sections that the model has partially forgotten after 20 turns. Crucially, these reminders should use <span id=\"S3.SS2.p2.pic1.2.1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">role: user</span> rather than <span id=\"S3.SS2.p2.pic1.2.1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">role: system</span>: in our experiments, user-role reminders consistently produced stronger compliance, likely because the model assigns higher salience to recent user messages than to system context that has been pushed down by intervening turns (<a href=\"#S2.SS3.SSS4\" title=\"2.3.4 Context-Aware System Reminders ‣ 2.3 Context Engineering Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.3.4</span></a>). However, reminder frequency must be capped per type; a reminder injected on every turn becomes background noise that the model learns to ignore, paradoxically reducing compliance.</span></span>\n</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S3.SS2.p3\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\"><span class=\"ltx_inline-block\"><svg id=\"S3.SS2.p3.pic1\" class=\"ltx_picture\" height=\"138.87\" overflow=\"visible\" version=\"1.1\" viewBox=\"0 0 650 138.87\" width=\"650\"><g style=\"--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;\" fill=\"#000000\" stroke=\"#000000\" stroke-width=\"0.4pt\" transform=\"translate(0,138.87) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)\"><g style=\"--ltx-fill-color:#BFD0E1;\" fill=\"#BFD0E1\" fill-opacity=\"1.0\"><path style=\"stroke:none\" d=\"M 0 0 L 0 138.87 L 650 138.87 L 650 0 Z\"></path></g><g style=\"--ltx-fill-color:#F6F9FB;\" fill=\"#F6F9FB\" fill-opacity=\"1.0\"><path style=\"stroke:none\" d=\"M 0.55 0.55 L 0.55 117.59 L 649.45 117.59 L 649.45 0.55 Z\"></path></g><g style=\"--ltx-fill-color:#EEF2F7;\" fill=\"#EEF2F7\" fill-opacity=\"1.0\"><path style=\"stroke:none\" d=\"M 0.55 118.14 L 0.55 138.31 L 649.45 138.31 L 649.45 118.14 Z\"></path></g><g style=\"--ltx-stroke-color:#29629B;--ltx-fill-color:#29629B;--ltx-fg-color:#29629B;\" color=\"#29629B\" fill=\"#29629B\" stroke=\"#29629B\" stroke-width=\"2.5pt\"><path style=\"fill:none\" d=\"M 1.73 138.87 L 1.73 0\"></path></g><g fill-opacity=\"1.0\" transform=\"matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 15.56 124.77)\"><foreignObject style=\"--ltx-fo-width:40.85em;--ltx-fo-height:0.69em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.19em;font-size:10pt;\" height=\"12.3\" overflow=\"visible\" transform=\"matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 9.61)\" width=\"565.25\"><span class=\"ltx_foreignobject_container\"><span class=\"ltx_foreignobject_content\">\n<span id=\"S3.SS2.p3.pic1.1\" class=\"ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom\" style=\"width:40.85em;\">\n<span id=\"S3.SS2.p3.pic1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S3.SS2.p3.pic1.1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif ltx_font_bold\" style=\"--ltx-fg-color:#25588C;\">Lesson: Separate thinking from action</span></span>\n</span></span></span></foreignObject></g><g fill-opacity=\"1.0\" transform=\"matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 15.56 14.1)\"><foreignObject style=\"--ltx-fo-width:44.93em;--ltx-fo-height:6.69em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.19em;font-size:10pt;\" height=\"95.32\" overflow=\"visible\" transform=\"matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 92.63)\" width=\"621.7\"><span class=\"ltx_foreignobject_container\"><span class=\"ltx_foreignobject_content\">\n<span id=\"S3.SS2.p3.pic1.2\" class=\"ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom\" style=\"width:44.93em;\">\n<span id=\"S3.SS2.p3.pic1.2.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S3.SS2.p3.pic1.2.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text\" style=\"--ltx-fg-color:#000000;\">When tools are available, LLMs tend to act quickly rather than think deeply. Providing a separate thinking phase with no tool access produces substantially better reasoning traces, because the model is not pressured by the availability of action (<a href=\"#S2.SS2.SSS6\" title=\"2.2.6 Extended ReAct Execution Loop ‣ 2.2 Agent Core Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.2.6</span></a>). This separation is more effective than asking the model to “think carefully” in the same call where tools are available. The mechanism matters: it is the absence of tool schemas from the API call, not an instruction to refrain from using them, that changes the model’s behavior.</span></span>\n</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>\n</div>\n<section id=\"S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Explicit decision trees for tool selection.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Agents default to text search (grep) for nearly every lookup, even when a more precise tool exists. This wastes iterations and floods the context with false positives. Encoding a retrieval-tool decision tree directly into the agent’s prompt (routing symbol names to semantic search, string patterns to text search, structural patterns to AST search, and file-name conventions to glob) reduced unnecessary grep calls and improved first-attempt retrieval accuracy. The key is that the decision criteria must be concrete and anchored to observable features of the query (“if the target is a function or class name, use <span id=\"S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter\">find_symbol</span>”), not abstract (“use the most appropriate tool”).</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Provider-conditional prompt sections.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Different LLM providers have meaningfully different capabilities: extended thinking, function calling conventions, context limits. Rather than cluttering the system prompt with provider-agnostic instructions, registering provider-specific sections that load only when the corresponding provider is active keeps the prompt budget focused (<a href=\"#S2.SS3.SSS1.Px2\" title=\"Mode-specific variants and variable substitution. ‣ 2.3.1 Dynamic System Prompt Construction ‣ 2.3 Context Engineering Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.3.1</span></a>). Unknown providers receive no section; graceful degradation is better than incorrect guidance.</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\"><span class=\"ltx_inline-block\"><svg id=\"S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.pic1\" class=\"ltx_picture\" height=\"206.05\" overflow=\"visible\" version=\"1.1\" viewBox=\"0 0 650 206.05\" width=\"650\"><g style=\"--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;\" fill=\"#000000\" stroke=\"#000000\" stroke-width=\"0.4pt\" transform=\"translate(0,206.05) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)\"><g style=\"--ltx-fill-color:#BFD0E1;\" fill=\"#BFD0E1\" fill-opacity=\"1.0\"><path style=\"stroke:none\" d=\"M 0 0 L 0 206.05 L 650 206.05 L 650 0 Z\"></path></g><g style=\"--ltx-fill-color:#F6F9FB;\" fill=\"#F6F9FB\" fill-opacity=\"1.0\"><path style=\"stroke:none\" d=\"M 0.55 0.55 L 0.55 184.77 L 649.45 184.77 L 649.45 0.55 Z\"></path></g><g style=\"--ltx-fill-color:#EEF2F7;\" fill=\"#EEF2F7\" fill-opacity=\"1.0\"><path style=\"stroke:none\" d=\"M 0.55 185.33 L 0.55 205.5 L 649.45 205.5 L 649.45 185.33 Z\"></path></g><g style=\"--ltx-stroke-color:#29629B;--ltx-fill-color:#29629B;--ltx-fg-color:#29629B;\" color=\"#29629B\" fill=\"#29629B\" stroke=\"#29629B\" stroke-width=\"2.5pt\"><path style=\"fill:none\" d=\"M 1.73 206.05 L 1.73 0\"></path></g><g fill-opacity=\"1.0\" transform=\"matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 15.56 191.95)\"><foreignObject style=\"--ltx-fo-width:40.85em;--ltx-fo-height:0.69em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.19em;font-size:10pt;\" height=\"12.3\" overflow=\"visible\" transform=\"matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 9.61)\" width=\"565.25\"><span class=\"ltx_foreignobject_container\"><span class=\"ltx_foreignobject_content\">\n<span id=\"S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.pic1.1\" class=\"ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom\" style=\"width:40.85em;\">\n<span id=\"S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.pic1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.pic1.1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif ltx_font_bold\" style=\"--ltx-fg-color:#25588C;\">Lesson: Separate agent construction from agent execution</span></span>\n</span></span></span></foreignObject></g><g fill-opacity=\"1.0\" transform=\"matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 15.56 14.1)\"><foreignObject style=\"--ltx-fo-width:44.93em;--ltx-fo-height:11.55em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.19em;font-size:10pt;\" height=\"162.51\" overflow=\"visible\" transform=\"matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 159.82)\" width=\"621.7\"><span class=\"ltx_foreignobject_container\"><span class=\"ltx_foreignobject_content\">\n<span id=\"S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.pic1.2\" class=\"ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom\" style=\"width:44.93em;\">\n<span id=\"S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.pic1.2.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.pic1.2.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text\" style=\"--ltx-fg-color:#000000;\">Long-running agents benefit from a clean separation between scaffolding (pre-runtime assembly) and the harness (runtime orchestration). Scaffolding (constructing the system prompt, building tool schemas, registering subagents) runs once before the first prompt and produces a fully initialized agent. The harness then wraps the reasoning loop with tool dispatch, context management, safety enforcement, and session persistence (<a href=\"#S2.SS2\" title=\"2.2 Agent Core Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.2</span></a>). This separation prevents construction-time concerns from tangling with runtime concerns: the harness never checks whether the agent is fully initialized, because eager construction guarantees it always is (<a href=\"#S2.SS2.SSS1\" title=\"2.2.1 Agent Scaffolding ‣ 2.2 Agent Core Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.2.1</span></a>). The practical benefit is that each concern can evolve independently: adding a new tool requires only a registry change at construction time, while changing the compaction strategy requires only a harness change at runtime.</span></span>\n</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>\n</div>\n</section>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S3.SS3\" class=\"ltx_subsection\">\n<h3 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_subsection\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection\">3.3 </span>Safety Through Architectural Constraints</h3>\n\n<div id=\"S3.SS3.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S3.SS3.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Runtime permission checks are the wrong primary abstraction for agent safety. A model that sees a dangerous tool in its schema can reason about invoking it, argue for why it should be allowed, and probe for edge cases in the permission logic. The more robust approach is to make violations structurally impossible: if write tools are absent from the agent’s schema, the agent cannot attempt writes because it never sees a way to invoke them (<a href=\"#S2.SS2\" title=\"2.2 Agent Core Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.2</span></a>). This is the difference between a guard rail and a missing road: the model cannot reason about capabilities it does not know exist.</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S3.SS3.p2\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\"><span class=\"ltx_inline-block\"><svg id=\"S3.SS3.p2.pic1\" class=\"ltx_picture\" height=\"171.61\" overflow=\"visible\" version=\"1.1\" viewBox=\"0 0 650 171.61\" width=\"650\"><g style=\"--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;\" fill=\"#000000\" stroke=\"#000000\" stroke-width=\"0.4pt\" transform=\"translate(0,171.61) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)\"><g style=\"--ltx-fill-color:#BFD0E1;\" fill=\"#BFD0E1\" fill-opacity=\"1.0\"><path style=\"stroke:none\" d=\"M 0 0 L 0 171.61 L 650 171.61 L 650 0 Z\"></path></g><g style=\"--ltx-fill-color:#F6F9FB;\" fill=\"#F6F9FB\" fill-opacity=\"1.0\"><path style=\"stroke:none\" d=\"M 0.55 0.55 L 0.55 151.56 L 649.45 151.56 L 649.45 0.55 Z\"></path></g><g style=\"--ltx-fill-color:#EEF2F7;\" fill=\"#EEF2F7\" fill-opacity=\"1.0\"><path style=\"stroke:none\" d=\"M 0.55 152.12 L 0.55 171.06 L 649.45 171.06 L 649.45 152.12 Z\"></path></g><g style=\"--ltx-stroke-color:#29629B;--ltx-fill-color:#29629B;--ltx-fg-color:#29629B;\" color=\"#29629B\" fill=\"#29629B\" stroke=\"#29629B\" stroke-width=\"2.5pt\"><path style=\"fill:none\" d=\"M 1.73 171.61 L 1.73 0\"></path></g><g fill-opacity=\"1.0\" transform=\"matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 15.56 157.51)\"><foreignObject style=\"--ltx-fo-width:40.85em;--ltx-fo-height:0.69em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.11em;font-size:10pt;\" height=\"11.07\" overflow=\"visible\" transform=\"matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 9.61)\" width=\"565.25\"><span class=\"ltx_foreignobject_container\"><span class=\"ltx_foreignobject_content\">\n<span id=\"S3.SS3.p2.pic1.1\" class=\"ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom\" style=\"width:40.85em;\">\n<span id=\"S3.SS3.p2.pic1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S3.SS3.p2.pic1.1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif ltx_font_bold\" style=\"--ltx-fg-color:#25588C;\">Lesson: Make unsafe tools invisible, not blocked</span></span>\n</span></span></span></foreignObject></g><g fill-opacity=\"1.0\" transform=\"matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 15.56 14.1)\"><foreignObject style=\"--ltx-fo-width:44.93em;--ltx-fo-height:9.15em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.19em;font-size:10pt;\" height=\"129.3\" overflow=\"visible\" transform=\"matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 126.61)\" width=\"621.7\"><span class=\"ltx_foreignobject_container\"><span class=\"ltx_foreignobject_content\">\n<span id=\"S3.SS3.p2.pic1.2\" class=\"ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom\" style=\"width:44.93em;\">\n<span id=\"S3.SS3.p2.pic1.2.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S3.SS3.p2.pic1.2.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text\" style=\"--ltx-fg-color:#000000;\">Schema gating (removing tools from the agent’s available set rather than checking permissions at call time) is fundamentally more robust than runtime permission checks. When a tool is absent from the schema, the agent cannot attempt to invoke it, argue for an exception, or probe for bypass conditions. Defense-in-depth with independently designed layers ensures that no single bypass compromises safety: schema gating prevents unauthorized attempts, the approval system intercepts operations requiring human review, file freshness validation prevents overwriting concurrent edits, and shadow git snapshots (<a href=\"#S2.SS5.SSS2\" title=\"2.5.2 Operation Log and Undo ‣ 2.5 Persistence Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.5.2</span></a>) make all filesystem changes reversible. These layers are deliberately independent; a bug in one does not weaken another.</span></span>\n</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>\n</div>\n<section id=\"S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Approval persistence prevents fatigue.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">When a user marks an approval rule as “always allow,” persisting it to disk so it survives session restarts is critical. Without persistence, users must re-approve the same operations every session, causing approval fatigue that leads to blanket auto-approval, defeating the safety system entirely.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Lifecycle hooks as extensibility.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">External scripts that observe or intercept agent lifecycle events enable custom policies, logging, CI integration, and security enforcement without modifying agent code. The hook interface must be designed early: blocking vs. non-blocking semantics, input mutation support, and merged global/project-level configurations are all necessary for hooks to be useful rather than decorative.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S3.SS3.SSS0.Px3\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Modal priority during interrupt.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S3.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S3.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">When the user presses an interrupt key while a modal dialog (approval prompt, user question) is active, the system should cancel the dialog rather than interrupting the agent. Interrupting the agent while a dialog is pending creates orphaned UI state (dangling spinners, stale futures, unresolved promises) that requires manual cleanup.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S3.SS4\" class=\"ltx_subsection\">\n<h3 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_subsection\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection\">3.4 </span>Designing for Approximate Outputs</h3>\n\n<div id=\"S3.SS4.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S3.SS4.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">LLMs reliably produce approximately-correct outputs. Edit targets drift from actual file content: trailing whitespace, indentation differences, escape sequence variations. Recovery strategies reference tools the agent does not have. Search queries route to suboptimal tools. A system that demands exact correctness from the model will spend most of its time in error-recovery loops. The alternative is to design tools and interfaces that absorb LLM imprecision as a first-class property.</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S3.SS4.p2\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\"><span class=\"ltx_inline-block\"><svg id=\"S3.SS4.p2.pic1\" class=\"ltx_picture\" height=\"155.47\" overflow=\"visible\" version=\"1.1\" viewBox=\"0 0 650 155.47\" width=\"650\"><g style=\"--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;\" fill=\"#000000\" stroke=\"#000000\" stroke-width=\"0.4pt\" transform=\"translate(0,155.47) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)\"><g style=\"--ltx-fill-color:#BFD0E1;\" fill=\"#BFD0E1\" fill-opacity=\"1.0\"><path style=\"stroke:none\" d=\"M 0 0 L 0 155.47 L 650 155.47 L 650 0 Z\"></path></g><g style=\"--ltx-fill-color:#F6F9FB;\" fill=\"#F6F9FB\" fill-opacity=\"1.0\"><path style=\"stroke:none\" d=\"M 0.55 0.55 L 0.55 134.19 L 649.45 134.19 L 649.45 0.55 Z\"></path></g><g style=\"--ltx-fill-color:#EEF2F7;\" fill=\"#EEF2F7\" fill-opacity=\"1.0\"><path style=\"stroke:none\" d=\"M 0.55 134.74 L 0.55 154.92 L 649.45 154.92 L 649.45 134.74 Z\"></path></g><g style=\"--ltx-stroke-color:#29629B;--ltx-fill-color:#29629B;--ltx-fg-color:#29629B;\" color=\"#29629B\" fill=\"#29629B\" stroke=\"#29629B\" stroke-width=\"2.5pt\"><path style=\"fill:none\" d=\"M 1.73 155.47 L 1.73 0\"></path></g><g fill-opacity=\"1.0\" transform=\"matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 15.56 141.37)\"><foreignObject style=\"--ltx-fo-width:40.85em;--ltx-fo-height:0.69em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.19em;font-size:10pt;\" height=\"12.3\" overflow=\"visible\" transform=\"matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 9.61)\" width=\"565.25\"><span class=\"ltx_foreignobject_container\"><span class=\"ltx_foreignobject_content\">\n<span id=\"S3.SS4.p2.pic1.1\" class=\"ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom\" style=\"width:40.85em;\">\n<span id=\"S3.SS4.p2.pic1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S3.SS4.p2.pic1.1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif ltx_font_bold\" style=\"--ltx-fg-color:#25588C;\">Lesson: Design tools to absorb LLM imprecision</span></span>\n</span></span></span></foreignObject></g><g fill-opacity=\"1.0\" transform=\"matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 15.56 14.1)\"><foreignObject style=\"--ltx-fo-width:44.93em;--ltx-fo-height:7.89em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.19em;font-size:10pt;\" height=\"111.93\" overflow=\"visible\" transform=\"matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 109.24)\" width=\"621.7\"><span class=\"ltx_foreignobject_container\"><span class=\"ltx_foreignobject_content\">\n<span id=\"S3.SS4.p2.pic1.2\" class=\"ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom\" style=\"width:44.93em;\">\n<span id=\"S3.SS4.p2.pic1.2.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S3.SS4.p2.pic1.2.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text\" style=\"--ltx-fg-color:#000000;\">The edit operation is the clearest example. A strict exact-match edit tool causes the majority of agent errors in practice, not because the agent’s intent is wrong, but because its reproduction of the target text is slightly off. Building a chain of progressively relaxed matchers, where each returns the <em id=\"S3.SS4.p2.pic1.2.1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_emph ltx_font_italic\">actual substring found in the file</em> to preserve original formatting, converts these near-misses into successful edits (<a href=\"#S2.SS4.SSS2\" title=\"2.4.2 File Operations ‣ 2.4 Tool System ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.4.2</span></a>). The chain short-circuits on first match, so exact matches incur zero overhead. The general principle: when the agent’s intent is unambiguous but its literal output is imprecise, the tool should bridge the gap rather than reject the attempt.</span></span>\n</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S3.SS4.p3\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\"><span class=\"ltx_inline-block\"><svg id=\"S3.SS4.p3.pic1\" class=\"ltx_picture\" height=\"172.84\" overflow=\"visible\" version=\"1.1\" viewBox=\"0 0 650 172.84\" width=\"650\"><g style=\"--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;\" fill=\"#000000\" stroke=\"#000000\" stroke-width=\"0.4pt\" transform=\"translate(0,172.84) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)\"><g style=\"--ltx-fill-color:#BFD0E1;\" fill=\"#BFD0E1\" fill-opacity=\"1.0\"><path style=\"stroke:none\" d=\"M 0 0 L 0 172.84 L 650 172.84 L 650 0 Z\"></path></g><g style=\"--ltx-fill-color:#F6F9FB;\" fill=\"#F6F9FB\" fill-opacity=\"1.0\"><path style=\"stroke:none\" d=\"M 0.55 0.55 L 0.55 151.56 L 649.45 151.56 L 649.45 0.55 Z\"></path></g><g style=\"--ltx-fill-color:#EEF2F7;\" fill=\"#EEF2F7\" fill-opacity=\"1.0\"><path style=\"stroke:none\" d=\"M 0.55 152.12 L 0.55 172.29 L 649.45 172.29 L 649.45 152.12 Z\"></path></g><g style=\"--ltx-stroke-color:#29629B;--ltx-fill-color:#29629B;--ltx-fg-color:#29629B;\" color=\"#29629B\" fill=\"#29629B\" stroke=\"#29629B\" stroke-width=\"2.5pt\"><path style=\"fill:none\" d=\"M 1.73 172.84 L 1.73 0\"></path></g><g fill-opacity=\"1.0\" transform=\"matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 15.56 158.74)\"><foreignObject style=\"--ltx-fo-width:40.85em;--ltx-fo-height:0.69em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.19em;font-size:10pt;\" height=\"12.3\" overflow=\"visible\" transform=\"matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 9.61)\" width=\"565.25\"><span class=\"ltx_foreignobject_container\"><span class=\"ltx_foreignobject_content\">\n<span id=\"S3.SS4.p3.pic1.1\" class=\"ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom\" style=\"width:40.85em;\">\n<span id=\"S3.SS4.p3.pic1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S3.SS4.p3.pic1.1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif ltx_font_bold\" style=\"--ltx-fg-color:#25588C;\">Lesson: Adapt recovery hints to the agent’s available tool set</span></span>\n</span></span></span></foreignObject></g><g fill-opacity=\"1.0\" transform=\"matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 15.56 14.87)\"><foreignObject style=\"--ltx-fo-width:44.93em;--ltx-fo-height:9.09em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.25em;font-size:10pt;\" height=\"129.3\" overflow=\"visible\" transform=\"matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 125.84)\" width=\"621.7\"><span class=\"ltx_foreignobject_container\"><span class=\"ltx_foreignobject_content\">\n<span id=\"S3.SS4.p3.pic1.2\" class=\"ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom\" style=\"width:44.93em;\">\n<span id=\"S3.SS4.p3.pic1.2.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S3.SS4.p3.pic1.2.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text\" style=\"--ltx-fg-color:#000000;\">When truncating large output and suggesting recovery strategies, the system must check which tools the agent actually has (<a href=\"#S2.SS3.SSS2\" title=\"2.3.2 Tool Result Optimization ‣ 2.3 Context Engineering Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.3.2</span></a>). If the agent can delegate to a subagent, suggest that; if it cannot (because it is itself a subagent), suggest incremental processing with offset/limit parameters. Generic hints that recommend unavailable tools cause the agent to attempt impossible actions and enter error loops. The same principle applies to error messages: “re-read the file and retry your edit with current content” is vastly more actionable than “try again,” so classifying errors into specific categories and retrieving targeted recovery templates for each improves recovery rates (<a href=\"#S2.SS3.SSS5\" title=\"2.3.5 Context-Injected Error Recovery ‣ 2.3 Context Engineering Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.3.5</span></a>).</span></span>\n</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>\n</div>\n<section id=\"S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Auto-promoting server-like commands.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Development servers, build watchers, and test suites that run indefinitely will hit any foreground timeout. Detecting server-like commands via regex patterns and automatically promoting them to background execution with output capture prevents the agent from blocking on a process that was never meant to terminate (<a href=\"#S2.SS4.SSS3\" title=\"2.4.3 Shell Execution and Background Tasks ‣ 2.4 Tool System ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.4.3</span></a>).</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2\" class=\"ltx_paragraph\">\n<h5 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph\">Auto-installing missing dependencies.</h5>\n\n<div id=\"S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Tools that depend on external runtimes should auto-install the dependency on first use rather than failing with an opaque error. Check for the dependency, install if missing, and retry. This eliminates a common class of setup-related failures that confuse both the agent and the user, and is another instance of designing tools to absorb environmental imprecision.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S3.SS5\" class=\"ltx_subsection\">\n<h3 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_subsection\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection\">3.5 </span>Lazy Loading and Bounded Growth</h3>\n\n<div id=\"S3.SS5.p1\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S3.SS5.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Eager loading fails at scale. Loading all MCP tool schemas at startup consumed 40% of the context budget before the agent processed its first user message. Loading all skill definitions populated the prompt with content the agent would never use in most sessions. The solution in both cases is lazy discovery: load metadata indexes at startup, defer full content to the point of use (<a href=\"#S2.SS4.SSS7\" title=\"2.4.7 Token-Efficient External Tool Discovery via MCP ‣ 2.4 Tool System ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.4.7</span></a>).</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S3.SS5.p2\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S3.SS5.p2.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">For MCP tools, lazy discovery reduces the startup context cost from 40% to under 5%. The agent receives a compact summary of available servers and their capabilities; full tool schemas are loaded only when the agent selects a server for a specific task. For skills, a two-phase approach serves the same purpose: a metadata index (name, description, trigger conditions) is loaded at startup, while the full skill content (which may include multi-page prompt templates) is loaded only when the agent decides to invoke the skill.</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S3.SS5.p3\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S3.SS5.p3.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">External metadata (model capabilities, pricing, context limits) benefits from a stale-while-revalidate caching strategy (<a href=\"#S2.SS5.SSS4\" title=\"2.5.4 Provider and Model Cache ‣ 2.5 Persistence Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.5.4</span></a>): on startup, serve from cache if fresh; if stale, serve the stale data and refresh in the background; if the refresh fails, continue with stale data. This guarantees offline startup and eliminates “cannot connect” failures that block the entire system.</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S3.SS5.p4\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\"><span class=\"ltx_inline-block\"><svg id=\"S3.SS5.p4.pic1\" class=\"ltx_picture\" height=\"156.24\" overflow=\"visible\" version=\"1.1\" viewBox=\"0 0 650 156.24\" width=\"650\"><g style=\"--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;\" fill=\"#000000\" stroke=\"#000000\" stroke-width=\"0.4pt\" transform=\"translate(0,156.24) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)\"><g style=\"--ltx-fill-color:#BFD0E1;\" fill=\"#BFD0E1\" fill-opacity=\"1.0\"><path style=\"stroke:none\" d=\"M 0 0 L 0 156.24 L 650 156.24 L 650 0 Z\"></path></g><g style=\"--ltx-fill-color:#F6F9FB;\" fill=\"#F6F9FB\" fill-opacity=\"1.0\"><path style=\"stroke:none\" d=\"M 0.55 0.55 L 0.55 134.96 L 649.45 134.96 L 649.45 0.55 Z\"></path></g><g style=\"--ltx-fill-color:#EEF2F7;\" fill=\"#EEF2F7\" fill-opacity=\"1.0\"><path style=\"stroke:none\" d=\"M 0.55 135.51 L 0.55 155.69 L 649.45 155.69 L 649.45 135.51 Z\"></path></g><g style=\"--ltx-stroke-color:#29629B;--ltx-fill-color:#29629B;--ltx-fg-color:#29629B;\" color=\"#29629B\" fill=\"#29629B\" stroke=\"#29629B\" stroke-width=\"2.5pt\"><path style=\"fill:none\" d=\"M 1.73 style=\"--ltx-fo-width:40.85em;--ltx-fo-height:0.69em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.19em;font-size:10pt;\" height=\"12.3\" overflow=\"visible\" transform=\"matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 9.61)\" width=\"565.25\"><span class=\"ltx_foreignobject_container\"><span class=\"ltx_foreignobject_content\">\n<span id=\"S3.SS5.p4.pic1.1\" class=\"ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom\" style=\"width:40.85em;\">\n<span id=\"S3.SS5.p4.pic1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S3.SS5.p4.pic1.1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif ltx_font_bold\" style=\"--ltx-fg-color:#25588C;\">Lesson: Bound every resource that grows with session length</span></span>\n</span></span></span></foreignObject></g><g fill-opacity=\"1.0\" transform=\"matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 15.56 14.87)\"><foreignObject style=\"--ltx-fo-width:44.93em;--ltx-fo-height:7.89em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.25em;font-size:10pt;\" height=\"112.7\" overflow=\"visible\" transform=\"matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 109.24)\" width=\"621.7\"><span class=\"ltx_foreignobject_container\"><span class=\"ltx_foreignobject_content\">\n<span id=\"S3.SS5.p4.pic1.2\" class=\"ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom\" style=\"width:44.93em;\">\n<span id=\"S3.SS5.p4.pic1.2.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S3.SS5.p4.pic1.2.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text\" style=\"--ltx-fg-color:#000000;\">Unbounded resources fail in long sessions. Without explicit caps, undo history accumulates snapshots indefinitely, concurrent tool calls can overwhelm the system, and behavioral nudges can flood the context. The design rule is simple: every resource that grows with session length must have a cap. Iteration limits prevent runaway agent loops. Undo history is bounded to a fixed number of snapshots. Concurrent tool calls are capped to prevent resource exhaustion. Nudge budgets limit how many times each reminder type can fire. Read-only tool calls run in parallel while write calls serialize (<a href=\"#S2.SS2.SSS3\" title=\"2.2.3 Conversation Lifecycle ‣ 2.2 Agent Core Layer ‣ 2 System Architecture ‣ Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal:Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">Section</span> <span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2.2.3</span></a>).</span></span>\n</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S3.SS5.p5\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\"><span class=\"ltx_inline-block\"><svg id=\"S3.SS5.p5.pic1\" class=\"ltx_picture\" height=\"156.24\" overflow=\"visible\" version=\"1.1\" viewBox=\"0 0 650 156.24\" width=\"650\"><g style=\"--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;\" fill=\"#000000\" stroke=\"#000000\" stroke-width=\"0.4pt\" transform=\"translate(0,156.24) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)\"><g style=\"--ltx-fill-color:#BFD0E1;\" fill=\"#BFD0E1\" fill-opacity=\"1.0\"><path style=\"stroke:none\" d=\"M 0 0 L 0 156.24 L 650 156.24 L 650 0 Z\"></path></g><g style=\"--ltx-fill-color:#F6F9FB;\" fill=\"#F6F9FB\" fill-opacity=\"1.0\"><path style=\"stroke:none\" d=\"M 0.55 0.55 L 0.55 134.96 L 649.45 134.96 L 649.45 0.55 Z\"></path></g><g style=\"--ltx-fill-color:#EEF2F7;\" fill=\"#EEF2F7\" style=\"--ltx-stroke-color:#29629B;--ltx-fill-color:#29629B;--ltx-fg-color:#29629B;\" color=\"#29629B\" fill=\"#29629B\" stroke=\"#29629B\" stroke-width=\"2.5pt\"><path style=\"fill:none\" d=\"M 1.73
